teile.einleitung: Ovomaltine is a malt drink powder from Switzerland. It was developed in 1904 in Bern by Albert Wander. Many children in Switzerland know the Ovo mug at breakfast.
wichtigste: Ovomaltine was invented in 1904 by Albert Wander in Bern.
The company was called Wander and was based in Bern.
Ovomaltine consists mainly of malt, milk and cocoa.
You stir the powder into cold or warm milk.
The name is made up of the Latin words for egg and malt.
In England the drink is called Ovaltine.

abschnitte.text: The pharmacist **Georg Wander** founded a laboratory in Bern in which he did research on **malt extract**. Malt is made when you let grain such as barley germinate and then dry it. His son **Albert Wander** developed from it, in **1904**, a powder that you could drink with milk. This is how **Ovomaltine** came about.

Ovomaltine consists mainly of **malt**, **milk** and **cocoa**. In the past it also contained **egg**. The name points to this: “ovum” means egg in Latin, and “maltum” stands for malt. The powder is stirred into cold or warm milk. Typically it does not dissolve completely, and small grains remain.

Ovomaltine was soon also sold abroad. In Great Britain and other countries it is called **Ovaltine**. In Switzerland today there are also bars, biscuits and the spread **Ovomaltine crunchy cream**. Ovomaltine is made in **Neuenegg** in the canton of Bern.

For many people, Ovo is part of childhood, for example at breakfast or after skiing. Advertising often linked the drink with **sport** and energy. That is why Ovomaltine is still regarded today as a typically Swiss product, even though the Wander company now belongs to a foreign group.

gewusst: The name Ovomaltine comes from the Latin words for egg and malt.
Ovomaltine has existed for over 120 years.

teile.einleitung: The Jaquet-Droz automata are three mechanical figures from the 18th century. They can write, draw and play music, and are on display in the Museum of Art and History in Neuchâtel.
wichtigste: The automata were built in the 18th century.
The builder was the watchmaker Pierre Jaquet-Droz with his assistants.
There are three figures: the writer, the draughtsman and the musician.
They move by means of cogwheels and springs, with no electricity at all.
The automata still work today.
You can see them in the museum in Neuchâtel.

abschnitte.text: **Pierre Jaquet-Droz** was a watchmaker from La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel. Together with his son and other assistants, in the 18th century he built three artful **automata**. An automaton is a machine that carries out movements by itself. At that time the figures were shown and admired at royal courts all over Europe.

The **writer** dips a quill in ink and writes a text on paper. You can set which letters he writes. The **draughtsman** draws several small pictures. The **musician** plays a small organ, and as she does so her chest rises and falls as if she were breathing. Her eyes also move.

Inside the figures, thousands of small parts are at work: **cogwheels**, springs, levers and cams. A wound spring provides the power. The cams control how the arms, head and eyes move. Some people therefore call the writer an early forerunner of the computer, because it can be programmed.

gewusst: The automata are over 250 years old and are still working.
In the museum in Neuchâtel they are demonstrated regularly.

teile.einleitung: The Act of Mediation was a constitution that Napoleon Bonaparte gave to Switzerland in 1803. With it, six new cantons were founded, including the Grisons and Vaud.
wichtigste: The Act of Mediation came into force in 1803.
It was issued by Napoleon Bonaparte.
It ended the Helvetic Republic.
The cantons once more received more rights of their own.
Switzerland then had 19 cantons.
New were St Gallen, the Grisons, Aargau, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud.
The Mediation period ended in 1813 with the fall of Napoleon.

abschnitte.text: **Mediation** means acting as a go-between. In 1798, French troops had occupied the old Confederation. After that the **Helvetic Republic** came into being, a unitary state in which the cantons had hardly any say. Many people were dissatisfied with this, and disputes arose. Napoleon stepped in as mediator and gave Switzerland a new constitution, the Act of Mediation.

With the Act of Mediation, the old **13 states** became cantons with rights of their own again. Six new cantons were added: **St Gallen, the Grisons, Aargau, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud**. This gave Switzerland 19 cantons. The Grisons had previously only been allied with the Confederation. Vaud, Aargau, Thurgau and Ticino had formerly been subject territories.

The cantons sent representatives to the **Tagsatzung** (Diet), the joint assembly. Each year a different one of the large cantons was the **Vorort**, that is, the leading canton. Its head of government bore the title **Landammann of Switzerland**. In this period Switzerland was closely tied to France and had to supply soldiers for Napoleon's army.

abschnitte.titel: The end of the Mediation period
abschnitte.text: When Napoleon suffered great defeats in 1813, the Act of Mediation lost its force. In 1815 the cantons concluded a new **Federal Treaty**. At the **Congress of Vienna**, Geneva, Neuchâtel and Valais were admitted as new cantons. The six cantons from the Mediation period remained and are still part of Switzerland today.

gewusst: In 2003 the cantons of St Gallen, the Grisons, Aargau, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud celebrated 200 years of existence as cantons.

teile.einleitung: The Napf is a mountain in the Swiss Central Plateau on the border between the cantons of Lucerne and Bern. Around it lies a hilly landscape with deep ravines. In the streams of the Napf area, small grains of gold can be found.
wichtigste: The Napf is 1,408 metres high.
It lies on the border of the cantons of Lucerne and Bern.
The Napf area is crossed by many steep ravines and streams.
The mountain consists mainly of Nagelfluh, a rock made of gravel and stones.
In the streams you can pan fine gold dust and small grains of gold.
On the summit stands a mountain inn with a wide view.

abschnitte.text: The **Napf** lies between the **Emmental** in the canton of Bern and the **Entlebuch** in the canton of Lucerne. It is 1,408 metres high. Around the summit lie many wooded hills and deep, narrow valleys called **Gräben** (ravines). In clear weather you can see from the summit as far as the Alps and the Jura.

The Napf consists for the most part of **Nagelfluh**. This is a rock made of many round stones cemented together as if in concrete. Millions of years ago, rivers carried gravel and rubble from the young Alps into the foreland. There it was deposited and, over time, became solid rock.

The Nagelfluh also contains a tiny amount of **gold**. When water wears away the rock, fine **flakes of gold** reach the streams. Because gold is heavy, it stays lying on the bottom. With a **gold-panning pan** you can carefully swirl the sand until the shiny little grains are left. You will not get rich from it, though.

No road for public transport leads up the Napf. You reach the summit mainly **on foot**. At the top stands a **mountain inn**. Part of the Napf area belongs to the **UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch**, an area in which nature and people are especially protected and supported.

gewusst: Gold panning is a popular hobby in the Napf area, and there are even courses for it.
Nagelfluh gets its name because the round stones in it look like nail heads.

teile.einleitung: The Goldau Nature and Animal Park lies in the canton of Schwyz among huge boulders. These rocks come from a massive rockfall in 1806. Today the park is home mainly to animals native to Europe and Switzerland.
wichtigste: The animal park lies in Goldau in the municipality of Arth in the canton of Schwyz.
It is in the area of the Goldau rockslide of 1806.
At that time huge masses of rock fell from the Rossberg into the valley.
In the park live native animals such as deer, wild boar, bears and wolves.
Many animals, such as deer, can be watched at close range and fed.
The animal park helps to reintroduce rare animals such as the bearded vulture.

abschnitte.text: On **2 September 1806**, a huge mass of rock broke away on the **Rossberg**. It fell into the valley and buried the village of **Goldau** and several hamlets. Many people lost their lives. The rockslide is one of the worst natural disasters in the history of Switzerland. Even today you can see the pale break-off point on the Rossberg.

Where the boulders once came to rest, a forest grew over time. In this special terrain, the **animal park** was founded in the 20th century. The paths lead between large, moss-covered **blocks of rock**. In this way you experience nature and history at the same time.

In the Goldau animal park live mainly **native animals**. These include **deer**, **ibex**, **wild boar**, lynx and owls. In one large enclosure, **bears** and **wolves** live together. In one part of the park, deer roam freely, and you may feed them with special food.

The animal park takes part in the protection of rare animals. One example is the **bearded vulture**, a large bird of prey that had almost died out in the Alps. Young bearded vultures from breeding programmes are released in the mountains. The park also explains to visitors how important the protection of nature is.

gewusst: The rocks from the rockslide of 1806 still lie around in the animal park today.
In the Goldau animal park, bears and wolves share a common enclosure, which is rare in animal parks.

teile.einleitung: The Mittlere Brücke (Middle Bridge) is the oldest bridge over the Rhine in Basel. A first bridge at this spot was built around 1225. The present stone bridge dates from 1905 and links Grossbasel with Kleinbasel.
wichtigste: The Mittlere Brücke stands in Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt.
The first bridge at this spot was built around 1225.
It links Grossbasel with Kleinbasel.
The present stone bridge was inaugurated in 1905.
On the bridge stands a small chapel, the Käppelijoch.
Trams run over the bridge.

abschnitte.titel: A bridge with a long history
abschnitte.text: Around **1225**, the Bishop of Basel had a first bridge built over the **Rhine**. It was very important at the time, because there were only a few bridges over such a wide river. For a long time the bridge was partly of wood and partly of stone. Traders, travellers and pilgrims crossed the Rhine here. In this way Basel became an important trading place.

On the left of the Rhine lies **Grossbasel** with the Minster and the Town Hall. On the right of the Rhine, **Kleinbasel** arose after the bridge was built, at first a small town of its own. The bridge linked the two parts. People in Basel still call the two sides this today. After the Mittlere Brücke, further bridges over the Rhine were later built in Basel.

In the middle of the bridge stands a small chapel, the **Käppelijoch**. In the past it was a place for prayers and also for court sentences. Today couples in love sometimes hang padlocks on the railing. From the bridge you can see the Minster and the houses on the bank of the Rhine.

Because traffic kept growing, the old bridge was replaced by a new one made of **stone**. It was inaugurated in 1905. Today **trams**, bicycles and pedestrians cross the bridge. In summer many people swim in the Rhine beneath the bridge, and beside it run the small **Rhine ferries**, which are driven only by the current.

gewusst: For a long time the Mittlere Brücke was simply called “the Rhine bridge”, because there was no other in Basel.
The Basel Rhine ferries have no engine: the current of the Rhine pushes them across the river.

teile.einleitung: Engelberg Abbey lies in the canton of Obwalden in a high valley at the foot of the Titlis. Benedictine monks have lived here for over 900 years, and in the show dairy you can watch how cheese is made.
wichtigste: Engelberg Abbey was founded in the year 1120.
Benedictine monks live here by the Rule of Saint Benedict.
In the show dairy you can see through glass panes how cheese is made.
For a long time Engelberg was a small state of its own under the abbot.
Since 1815 Engelberg has belonged to the canton of Obwalden.

abschnitte.text: The monastery was founded in **1120** by a nobleman named **Konrad von Sellenbüren**. He brought monks to the remote high valley. Since then **Benedictines** have lived there. Their life follows the Rule of Saint Benedict, which combines prayer and work.

abschnitte.titel: A monastery as a small state
abschnitte.text: For many centuries the valley of Engelberg was a small territory of its own. The **abbot** of the monastery was at the same time the ruler of the land. This changed with the French invasion in 1798. Since **1815**, Engelberg has belonged to the canton of **Obwalden**, although geographically it borders Nidwalden more closely.

The monastery has a **show dairy**. Through large glass panes, visitors watch the cheesemaker warm milk in a copper vat, add rennet and shape the cheese. The milk comes from farms in the surrounding area. In the shop you can taste and buy the cheese straight away.

The village of Engelberg is now a well-known holiday resort. From there, cable cars run up the **Titlis** with its glacier. The monastery also runs a **monastery school** with a Gymnasium (academic secondary school). The large abbey church from the 18th century is bright inside and richly decorated.

gewusst: The name Engelberg means “mountain of the angels”.
The organ in Engelberg Abbey church is regarded as one of the largest in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The **Rhône** is one of the great rivers of Switzerland. It rises at the **Rhône Glacier**, flows through the whole of **Valais** and into **Lake Geneva**. In **Geneva** it leaves the lake and flows through France to the **Mediterranean**.
wichtigste: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier near the Furka Pass.
It flows through the whole of Valais.
After that it flows into Lake Geneva.
In Geneva the Rhône leaves Lake Geneva again.
It flows through France to the Mediterranean.
In Upper Valais, the Rhône is called “Rotten” in German dialect.

abschnitte.titel: From the glacier into the valley
abschnitte.text: The Rhône begins as meltwater at the **Rhône Glacier** near the **Furka Pass**. First it flows through the **Goms**, the uppermost valley of Valais. In Upper Valais, the river is called “**Rotten**” in the dialect. At **Brig** and **Visp** the valley becomes wider. Many streams from the side valleys flow into the Rhône and make it ever larger.

The Rhône flows through the whole of Valais, past **Sion** and **Martigny**. At Martigny it makes a large bend to the north, the **Rhône bend**. In the past it often burst its banks and flooded the valley. That is why in the 19th and 20th centuries it was **straightened** and secured with embankments. Today the Rhône is being made safer again in a large project, and in some places given more room.

At the eastern end of **Lake Geneva**, the Rhône flows into the lake. Its water is cloudy from glacial silt, and in the lake the silt settles. In **Geneva** the Rhône leaves the lake again, now much clearer. Shortly afterwards the **Arve** flows into the Rhône from France. At the point where the two meet, you can see the clear and the cloudy water side by side.

After Geneva the Rhône flows into **France**. In **Lyon** the Saône joins it. After that it flows south to the **Mediterranean**. Before its mouth it divides into several arms and forms the **Camargue**, a large wetland with many birds. In total the Rhône is about 800 kilometres long.

gewusst: In Upper Valais the Rhône is called “Rotten” in the dialect.
In Geneva you can see the clear Rhône water and the cloudy water of the Arve flowing side by side.

teile.einleitung: The Klausen Pass is an Alpine pass in central Switzerland. It links the canton of Uri with the canton of Glarus and is one of the most beautiful pass roads in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Klausen Pass links Altdorf in the canton of Uri with Linthal in the canton of Glarus.
The summit of the pass lies at about 1,950 metres above sea level.
On the Uri side, the road runs through the Schächental valley.
In winter the pass road is closed because of snow.
The Urnerboden on the Glarus side belongs to the canton of Uri.

abschnitte.text: The road over the **Klausen Pass** begins in **Altdorf**, the main town of Uri. It leads up through the long **Schächental** valley to the summit of the pass. On the other side it goes down to **Linthal** in the canton of Glarus. The road has many bends and offers a wide view of the mountains.

For a long time there was only a pack path over the Klausen for people and animals. The present road was built towards the end of the **19th century**. Since then, carriages, and later cars and PostBuses, have been able to cross the pass. In summer a PostBus runs over the Klausen.

On the Glarus side of the pass lies the **Urnerboden**. This is a huge, flat alp and is regarded as one of the largest alps in Switzerland. Although it lies on the Glarus side of the watershed, it belongs to the **canton of Uri**. In summer many cows graze there.

Like many high passes, the Klausen Pass is **closed in winter**, because too much snow lies and avalanches threaten. It usually reopens in late spring. In summer, many cyclists, motorcyclists and walkers are out on the route.

gewusst: In the past a famous car race, the Klausen Race, took place on the pass road.
The Urnerboden belongs to Uri, although from Uri you first have to drive over the pass to reach it.

teile.einleitung: Ittingen Charterhouse is a former monastery near Frauenfeld in the canton of Thurgau. Carthusian monks once lived here, and today there are museums, a hotel, gardens and a farm of its own.
wichtigste: Ittingen Charterhouse lies near Frauenfeld in the canton of Thurgau.
A charterhouse is a monastery of the Carthusian monks.
The monks lived very quietly, each in a small house of his own.
In the 19th century the monastery was dissolved.
Today an art museum, a hotel, gardens and an estate farm belong to it.
On the farm, cheese, wine and other foods are produced.

abschnitte.text: A **charterhouse** is a monastery of the **Carthusian order**. The Carthusian monks lived very withdrawn and spoke little. Each monk lived in a **cell** of his own, a little house with a garden. There he prayed, read and worked alone. Only for certain services and on feast days did everyone come together.

Carthusian monks lived in Ittingen from the 15th century. In the 19th century, the canton of Thurgau dissolved the monastery. After that the complex belonged to one family for a long time and was used as a **farm estate**. Later a **foundation** was set up, which carefully renovated the old buildings. Since then the charterhouse has been open to everyone.

Today the charterhouse houses the **Thurgau Art Museum** and the **Ittingen Museum**, which tells of the monks' lives. There is also a **hotel**, a restaurant and beautiful **gardens**. The **estate farm** has animals, fields and vines. Cheese, wine, beer and other products are made here.

gewusst: In the charterhouse you can visit an old monk's cell and see how the monks lived.
Hops and vines grow all around the charterhouse.

teile.einleitung: The Rüeblitorte is a moist cake made with grated carrots. It comes from the canton of Aargau, which is therefore also called the “Rüebli canton”. Typical decoration is small carrots made of marzipan.
wichtigste: Rüebli is the Swiss word for carrot.
The Rüeblitorte is regarded as a speciality of the canton of Aargau.
Aargau is often called the “Rüebli canton”.
For the cake you need grated carrots, ground almonds or nuts, eggs and sugar.
On top there is usually a white icing.
Small marzipan carrots are the typical decoration.

abschnitte.text: A Rüeblitorte contains finely grated **carrots**, ground **almonds** or hazelnuts, eggs and sugar. Only a little flour is needed. Often a little lemon or cinnamon is added. The carrots make the batter moist, which is why the cake stays juicy for a long time.

First you beat egg yolks and sugar until frothy. Then you mix in the carrots and almonds. The egg whites are whisked to **stiff peaks** and carefully folded in, which makes the cake light. After baking and cooling it gets an icing of icing sugar. Finally the marzipan carrots are placed on top.

In Aargau there is a lot of fertile farmland, and vegetables such as carrots have been grown there for a long time. That is why the canton got the nickname **Rüebli canton**. The cake fits this picture well. Today it is known and baked all over Switzerland and abroad too.

The Rüeblitorte is a popular **birthday cake** and often appears on the table at family celebrations. You can also find it in many bakeries and cafés. Because carrots taste slightly sweet, many people do not even notice that there is a vegetable in the cake.

gewusst: In the English-speaking world, a similar cake is known as “carrot cake”.
Carrots are orange because they contain a lot of carotene, a pigment that the body can convert into vitamin A.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Neuchâtel lies in the west of Switzerland, in the Jura and on Lake Neuchâtel. French is spoken there, and the canton borders France.
wichtigste: The main town is the city of Neuchâtel.
French is spoken in the canton of Neuchâtel, which is part of French-speaking Switzerland (Romandie).
In the west it borders France, and part of the border is the river Doubs.
Since 1815, Neuchâtel has been a canton of the Swiss Confederation.
Until 1848 it was at the same time a principality of the King of Prussia.
On 1 March the canton celebrates the founding of the republic in 1848.
The coat of arms has three vertical stripes in green, white and red.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Neuchâtel lies on the northern shore of **Lake Neuchâtel**. This lake is the largest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland. Behind the shore, the heights of the **Jura** rise. Valleys such as the Val-de-Ruz and the Val-de-Travers lie there. In the west, the river **Doubs** forms part of the border with **France**.

Neuchâtel has a special history. From 1707 it belonged to the **King of Prussia**. In 1815 it was admitted as a canton into the **Swiss Confederation**. Even so, it remained a Prussian principality at the same time. On **1 March 1848**, the people of Neuchâtel proclaimed the **republic**. Since then this day has been a public holiday in the canton.

The coat of arms has three **vertical stripes** in green, white and red. At the top of the red stripe there is a small white cross. These colours date from the time of the republic. **French** is spoken in the canton. This makes it part of **Romandie**, French-speaking Switzerland.

The largest city is **La Chaux-de-Fonds**, high up in the Jura. Together with **Le Locle**, it is famous for the **watch industry**. The two cities were built so that watchmakers had plenty of light in their workshops. They are now UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The main town, **Neuchâtel**, lies on the lake and has a beautiful old town with a castle.

gewusst: In the Val-de-Travers lies the Creux du Van, a huge rock amphitheatre with steep walls.
For a long time Neuchâtel was both a canton and a principality, which existed nowhere else in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The **Randen** is a wooded hill area in the canton of **Schaffhausen**. It consists of **Jurassic limestone** and extends into Germany. With its viewing towers and flower meadows, it is a popular walking area.
wichtigste: The Randen is a wooded hill area in the canton of Schaffhausen.
It consists of limestone and belongs to the Jura.
Part of the Randen lies in Germany.
At 912 metres, the Hagen is the highest point of the canton of Schaffhausen.
On the Randen stand several viewing towers.
On the dry meadows, rare plants such as orchids grow.

abschnitte.text: The Randen lies north of the town of Schaffhausen. It consists of **limestone**, which was deposited in a sea a very long time ago. Geologically it belongs to the **Jura**, more precisely to the part that continues into the Swabian Alb in Germany. The Randen is covered with a lot of **forest**. In between lie meadows and small villages.

The highest point of the Randen on Swiss soil is the **Hagen** at 912 metres. It is also the highest point of the canton of Schaffhausen. On the Hagen and at other places stand **viewing towers**. From the top you can see over the forests to the Black Forest and, in clear weather, to the Alps. Walking paths link the towers with each other.

On the Randen there are many **lean meadows**. These are dry meadows with few nutrients on which especially many plant species grow. They include various **orchids**. Many butterflies and other insects also live here. That is why parts of the Randen are under **nature protection**.

gewusst: The Randen extends across the national border into Germany.
Wild orchids bloom on the meadows of the Randen.

teile.einleitung: The Lucerne Chügelipastete is a well-known speciality from the canton of Lucerne. It consists of a large case of puff pastry filled with small meatballs in a cream sauce.
wichtigste: The Chügelipastete is a traditional dish from Lucerne.
“Chügeli” is Swiss German for little balls.
The case is baked from puff pastry.
It is filled with meatballs in a light cream sauce.
Mushrooms and raisins are often included too.
Another name is Fritschipastete.

abschnitte.text: The pie is a large, round case of **puff pastry** with a lid. Inside goes a filling of small **meatballs**, often made of veal or sausage meat. With it comes a light **cream sauce**, often with mushrooms. In many recipes, soaked raisins are also included, which gives a slightly sweet taste.

The Chügelipastete is also called **Fritschipastete**. The name recalls the **Fritschi**, an important figure of the Lucerne carnival. The Fritschi belongs to the Safran guild, an old Lucerne guild. In this way the dish is closely linked with the history and customs of the city of Lucerne.

In the past, the Chügelipastete was a special **festive meal**, because preparing it takes a lot of work. Today it is served in many Lucerne restaurants and can also be bought ready-made at bakeries. You cut the pie into pieces and usually eat it with rice or just as it is. For many families it is part of the holidays.

gewusst: The little “Pastetli” that people know all over Switzerland are a kind of little sister of the large Chügelipastete.

teile.einleitung: Vadian is the scholarly name of Joachim von Watt from St Gallen. He was a doctor, scholar and mayor, and in the 16th century he introduced the Reformation in the city of St Gallen.
wichtigste: Vadian's real name was Joachim von Watt.
He lived from 1484 to 1551 and came from St Gallen.
The name comes from his Latin name Vadianus.
He was a doctor, scholar, poet and mayor.
He introduced the Reformation in the city of St Gallen.
A monument in St Gallen recalls him.

abschnitte.text: Joachim von Watt was born in **St Gallen** in 1484. He studied at the university in **Vienna** and became a well-known scholar there. Like many scholars of his time, he gave himself a **Latin name**: Vadianus, Vadian for short. In Vienna he was even honoured as a poet and for a time was head of the university.

Later Vadian returned to St Gallen and worked as the **town doctor**. Soon he also became important in politics. He became **mayor** of the city and held this office several times. He also wrote books on history and geography. He was very curious and even climbed Mount Pilatus to study it.

Vadian was a friend of the Zurich reformer **Huldrych Zwingli**. With his help, the **Reformation** was introduced in the city of St Gallen in the 1520s. This made the city Reformed. The monastery of St Gallen, however, remained Catholic. That is why there was tension between the city and the monastery for a long time.

Vadian died in St Gallen in 1551. He gave his valuable collection of books to the city. This became the **Vadiana**, today's cantonal library. On the market square there is a **monument** to Vadian. Streets and schools also carry his name.

gewusst: Vadian's library is one of the oldest public libraries in Switzerland.
Vadian was one of the first people to climb Mount Pilatus in order to study it.

teile.einleitung: Obwalden is a canton in central Switzerland whose main town is Sarnen. Together with Nidwalden, it used to form the land of Unterwalden, one of the three original cantons.
wichtigste: The main town of Obwalden is Sarnen.
German is spoken, in everyday life the Obwalden dialect.
The coat of arms is red at the top and white at the bottom, with a double key in the opposite colour.
Obwalden has seven municipalities.
Engelberg belongs to Obwalden but lies apart from the rest of the canton.
Brother Klaus, the patron saint of Switzerland, lived in Obwalden.

abschnitte.text: Obwalden has **seven municipalities**: Sarnen, Kerns, Sachseln, Alpnach, Giswil, Lungern and Engelberg. The main town is **Sarnen** on **Lake Sarnen**. The name means “ob dem Wald”, that is, above the forest. A special feature is **Engelberg**: it belongs to Obwalden but is not directly connected to the rest of the canton.

The coat of arms of Obwalden is **red** at the top and **white** at the bottom. On it stands a **double key** in the opposite colour: white on the red part, red on the white part. The key is the symbol of Saint Peter. Nidwalden also has a key in its coat of arms. The two cantons used to form the land of **Unterwalden** together.

**Niklaus von Flüe**, known as Brother Klaus, lived in Obwalden in the 15th century. He was a farmer and later withdrew as a hermit to the Ranft gorge near Flüeli. Many people came to him for advice. His advice is said to have helped settle a dispute between the Confederate states in 1481. Today he is regarded as the **patron saint of Switzerland**.

In **Engelberg** stands a large **monastery**, which was founded as early as the 12th century. Above the village rises the **Titlis** with its glacier. A cable car whose cabin turns during the journey goes up it. In winter, Engelberg is a well-known ski resort. In Sarnen, the **White Book** is also kept, an old chronicle that tells the legend of William Tell.

gewusst: The White Book of Sarnen contains one of the oldest written versions of the William Tell story.
Obwalden is one of the cantons with the fewest municipalities.

teile.einleitung: The Schiller Bell is an old bell from Schaffhausen. It was cast in 1486 and hung for a long time in the tower of the Allerheiligen Minster. Its Latin inscription is said to have inspired Friedrich Schiller to write his famous “Song of the Bell”.
wichtigste: The Schiller Bell was cast in 1486.
It hung in the Allerheiligen Minster in Schaffhausen.
It bears the inscription “Vivos voco, mortuos plango, fulgura frango”.
Schiller placed these words at the head of his “Song of the Bell”.
Today you can see the bell near the minster.

abschnitte.text: The bell was cast in **1486** for the Allerheiligen Minster in Schaffhausen. It bears a Latin inscription: “**Vivos voco, mortuos plango, fulgura frango**”. In English this means: “I call the living, I mourn the dead, I break the lightning.” This describes the tasks of a church bell: calling people to services, ringing at funerals and ringing during thunderstorms.

The poet **Friedrich Schiller** published the long poem “Das Lied von der Glocke” (“Song of the Bell”) in 1799. It describes how a bell is cast and links this to the lives of people. Schiller placed exactly the words of the Schaffhausen inscription above the poem. That is why people say this bell is supposed to have inspired him. Whether he ever saw it himself is not proven.

After centuries in the tower, the old bell was replaced by a new one at the end of the 19th century. The Schiller Bell was not melted down, however. Today it stands in the area of the **cloister** at the Allerheiligen Minster. Visitors can look at it close up there.

gewusst: In the past people believed that the ringing of bells could drive away lightning and bad weather, hence the phrase “fulgura frango”.
The Allerheiligen Minster was originally the church of a Benedictine monastery from the 11th century.

teile.einleitung: Louis Chevrolet was a racing driver and car builder. He was born in 1878 in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel and in the USA co-founded the car brand Chevrolet.
wichtigste: Louis Chevrolet was born in 1878 in La Chaux-de-Fonds.
As a child he moved with his family to France.
Around 1900 he emigrated to North America.
In the USA he became a successful motor racing driver.
In 1911 he founded the Chevrolet company with William C. Durant.
The Chevrolet car brand still exists today.

abschnitte.text: Louis Chevrolet was born in **La Chaux-de-Fonds**, a town of watchmakers. While he was still a child, his family moved to **Beaune** in France. There, as a young man, he worked with bicycles and repaired them. He was very interested in technology and speed. Around 1900 he emigrated to Canada and soon afterwards to the **USA**.

In the USA, Chevrolet worked as a mechanic and soon became a well-known **motor racing driver**. He won many races and was known for his daring driving style. His brothers Arthur and Gaston also raced cars. Later he built **racing cars** of his own, with which other drivers were successful.

In 1911, Louis Chevrolet founded the company **Chevrolet** together with the businessman **William C. Durant**. After a few years, Louis Chevrolet left the company because of disputes. But the brand with his name became very large and today belongs to **General Motors**. Louis Chevrolet died in Detroit in 1941.

gewusst: Many people in the USA do not know that the name of the well-known car brand comes from a man from Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Mythen are two pointed mountain peaks above the town of Schwyz. They are called Grosser Mythen and Kleiner Mythen and are the landmark of the canton of Schwyz. A steep but well-built walking path leads up the Grosser Mythen.
wichtigste: The Mythen stand above the main town of Schwyz.
The Grosser Mythen is 1,898 metres high.
The Kleiner Mythen is somewhat lower.
A path with many bends leads up the Grosser Mythen.
At the top of the Grosser Mythen stands a mountain restaurant.
The rock of the Mythen originally comes from further south.

abschnitte.text: Anyone coming to **Schwyz** sees them at once: the two steep rock teeth of the **Mythen**. The **Grosser Mythen** is 1,898 metres high, the **Kleiner Mythen** somewhat lower. With their pointed shapes they look almost like mountains from a picture book. They are the best-known **landmark** of the canton of Schwyz.

A **walking path** with very many tight bends, called **switchbacks**, leads up the Grosser Mythen. The path is steep but secured with railings. The starting point is usually the **Holzegg**, which you reach by cable car. At the top stands a small **mountain restaurant** with a wide view over central Switzerland as far as the lakes.

The Mythen are also exciting for geology. Their rock is older than the rocks beneath. A very long time ago, when the Alps were formed, it was pushed from the south over other layers. After that, much of what surrounded it was worn away. What remained were individual blocks of rock that experts call **klippen**.

The **Kleiner Mythen** is lower, but harder to climb. You can only get up it with **climbing skills** or a mountain guide. Between the two peaks lies a saddle. In winter the Mythen are covered with snow and are especially beautiful to look at from Schwyz.

gewusst: The walking path up the Grosser Mythen has almost fifty switchbacks.
The rock of the Mythen is older than the ground on which they stand.

teile.einleitung: The Inn is a large river that rises in the canton of Graubünden. It flows through the whole Engadine, then through Austria and Germany until it runs into the Danube.
wichtigste: The Inn rises near the Maloja Pass in the Upper Engadine.
It flows through the whole Engadine.
The Engadine gets its name from the Inn, which is called “En” in Romansh.
After that the Inn flows through Austria, for example through Innsbruck.
At Passau in Germany it flows into the Danube.
With the Danube, its water reaches the Black Sea.

abschnitte.text: The Inn rises high in the mountains near the **Maloja Pass**. Soon after its source, it flows through the lakes of the Upper Engadine, such as Lake Sils and Lake Silvaplana. Then it goes down the valley past St Moritz. On the way it takes in many mountain streams and grows bigger and bigger.

The **Engadine** is a long high valley in the south-east of Switzerland. Its name comes from the Inn, which is called “En” in Romansh. A distinction is made between the Upper Engadine and the Lower Engadine. In the Engadine, besides German, people often speak **Romansh**, the fourth national language of Switzerland. At Martina, the Inn leaves Switzerland.

After Switzerland, the Inn flows through the **Tyrol** in Austria. The city of **Innsbruck** carries its name: it grew up at a bridge over the Inn. Later the river forms part of the border between Austria and Germany. In the city of **Passau** in Bavaria, it flows into the Danube.

abschnitte.titel: As far as the Black Sea
abschnitte.text: Most Swiss rivers flow via the Rhine into the North Sea or via the Rhône into the Mediterranean. The Inn is different. Via the **Danube**, its water travels through several countries to the **Black Sea**. A raindrop from the Engadine therefore has a very long way ahead of it.

gewusst: In Passau, the Inn often carries more water than the Danube, into which it flows.
The water of the Inn is very pale and greenish, because it carries a lot of fine rock dust from the Alps.

teile.einleitung: Schabziger is a special cheese from the canton of Glarus. It is green, shaped like a small cone and has a very strong, spicy flavour. It gets its colour from a herb called Schabziger clover.
wichtigste: Schabziger comes from the canton of Glarus.
It is green because Schabziger clover is mixed into it.
It has the shape of a small cone, called a “Stöckli”.
It is made from skimmed milk.
It is usually grated and eaten, for example, with butter on bread.
It is considered one of the oldest brand products in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Schabziger is no ordinary cheese. It is hard, **green** and shaped like a small cone. This shape is called a **Stöckli**. Its taste is strong and spicy. That is why people usually eat only a little of it at a time.

To make Schabziger you need **skimmed milk**, that is, milk without cream. From it you get **Ziger**, a kind of fresh cheese. The Ziger matures for some time. Then it is ground, mixed with salt and dried **Schabziger clover** and pressed into the cone shape.

Schabziger has a very long tradition. As early as the year **1463**, the Glarus **Landsgemeinde** (open-air assembly) passed rules for how it was made and marked. That is why it counts as one of the oldest brand products in Switzerland. In the past it was traded far beyond Glarus.

Schabziger is mostly **grated**. Mixed with butter it makes **Zigerbutter**, which is spread on bread. You can also sprinkle it over pasta, potatoes or soup. In Glarus there is even a special grater for it.

gewusst: Schabziger contains almost no fat, because it is made from skimmed milk.
In English the cheese is sometimes called “Sapsago”.

teile.einleitung: The Moléson is a well-known viewpoint mountain in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg. It is about 2,000 metres high, and by funicular and cable car you can get almost to the summit.
wichtigste: The Moléson lies in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.
It is about 2,000 metres high.
At its foot lies the holiday resort of Moléson-sur-Gruyères.
A funicular and a cable car lead up.
From the summit you can see Lake Geneva and the Alps.
In the area there is an alpine dairy where you can watch cheese being made.

abschnitte.text: The **Moléson** is one of the highest mountains in the Fribourg Pre-Alps. Because it stands a little in front of the other mountains, you have a wide **view** from the top. In clear weather you can see **Lake Geneva**, the Jura and many peaks of the Alps. Below lies the little town of **Gruyères** with its castle.

At the foot of the mountain lies the holiday resort of **Moléson-sur-Gruyères**. From there a **funicular** first runs to Plan-Francey. Then a **cable car** continues to just below the summit. The last stretch can be walked. In winter there are ski pistes on the Moléson.

Around the Moléson lie many **alpine pastures** on which cows graze in summer. **Cheese** is traditionally made here. In an old alpine dairy you can watch cheese being made over a wood fire in a copper vat. The Gruyère region is famous for Gruyère and for Vacherin fribourgeois.

gewusst: On the Moléson there is a small observatory where you can watch the stars.

teile.einleitung: St John's Abbey lies in Müstair in the Val Müstair, at the far east of the canton of the Grisons. It is well over 1,000 years old and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: St John's Abbey stands in Müstair in the canton of the Grisons.
It was founded around the year 800.
It is famous for its very old wall paintings.
Since 1983 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Benedictine nuns live there today.

abschnitte.text: The **Val Müstair** lies beyond the Ofen Pass on the border with Italy. In the village of **Müstair** stands St John's Abbey. The name Müstair comes from the Latin word for monastery. A legend tells that Charlemagne founded the monastery. What is certain is that it came into being around **800**.

In the abbey church, **wall paintings** from the time around 800 have survived. They show stories from the Bible, for example from the life of Jesus. For a long time they were hidden under later paintings and were only uncovered again recently. Such old pictures are very rare in Europe.

Since **1983**, St John's Abbey has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. This means that it is regarded as especially valuable for the whole of humanity and is protected. Researchers examine the buildings closely to learn more about the Middle Ages. A museum shows finds and works of art from the monastery.

Since the Middle Ages, **Benedictine nuns** have lived in the monastery. They pray several times a day and work in the monastery, for example in the garden. The monastery has been inhabited for over 1,200 years. Visitors can look round the church and the museum.

gewusst: St John's Abbey is one of the oldest surviving monasteries in Switzerland.
The massive Planta Tower in the monastery dates from the 10th century.

teile.einleitung: St Nicholas Cathedral is the main church of the city of Fribourg in the canton of Fribourg. It was built in the Middle Ages in the Gothic style and has a tower 74 metres high.
wichtigste: The cathedral stands in the old town of Fribourg.
It is dedicated to Saint Nicholas.
It was built in the Gothic style over about 200 years.
Its tower is 74 metres high.
From the tower you can see over the whole old town.
It is the bishop's church of the Diocese of Lausanne, Geneva and Fribourg.

abschnitte.text: Building of the church began at the end of the 13th century. It was only finished about 200 years later. It is built in the **Gothic style**, with pointed arches and tall windows. For a long time it was a town church. In the 20th century it became a **cathedral**, that is, the main church of a bishop.

The **tower** is 74 metres high and shapes the look of the city. You can climb up many steps. From the top you can see over the **old town**, the bridges and the Sarine, which flows in a tight loop around the city. In clear weather you can see as far as the Pre-Alps. Large bells hang in the tower.

The cathedral's **stained-glass windows** are famous. Many of them were made around 1900 by the Polish artist **Józef Mehoffer**. They glow in strong colours and show saints and plants. Above the main portal, stone figures show the **Last Judgement**. The cathedral also has a well-known **organ**.

gewusst: Fribourg is bilingual: in French the cathedral is called Cathédrale Saint-Nicolas.
The old town of Fribourg is one of the largest medieval old towns in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Muotatal weather prophets (Wetterschmöcker) are men from the Muotatal valley in the canton of Schwyz who forecast the weather in their own way. To do so they observe nature. Twice a year they announce their forecasts for the coming half year.
wichtigste: The Muotatal lies in the canton of Schwyz.
The weather prophets forecast the weather with the help of observations of nature.
For example, they observe ants, fir cones, plants, animals and clouds.
They are united in an association founded in 1947.
In spring and autumn they present their forecasts at a meeting.
The event is well known and popular with many people all over Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In Swiss German, **schmöcke** means to smell. A Wetterschmöcker is therefore someone who, so to speak, smells the weather. Of course, the men do not use only their noses. They look closely at how **animals** and **plants** behave, and they pay attention to clouds, wind and light.

Each weather prophet has his own methods. One, for example, observes how **ants** build their mounds. Another looks at **fir cones** or pays attention to when certain plants flower. Such knowledge about weather signs was often handed down in the past from generation to generation, above all among farmers and alpine herders.

The weather prophets belong to the **Meteorological Association of Inner Schwyz**, which was founded in **1947**. In spring they forecast the weather for the summer, in autumn for the winter. The meetings are cheerful events with a large audience. At the end, a prize goes to whoever came closest in the past half year.

The official weather reports in Switzerland are produced by **MeteoSwiss** with measuring instruments, satellites and computers. The weather prophets are not scientists but keep up a **tradition**. Their forecasts are often worded humorously. Many people still like to listen, because the observations show how closely people in the mountain valley are connected with nature.

gewusst: The weather prophets' forecasts are spread through newspapers, radio and television all over Switzerland.
The weather prophets do not forecast the weather for tomorrow, but for a whole half year.

teile.einleitung: **Rapperswil** is a town on **Lake Zurich** in the canton of St Gallen. Because of its many rose gardens, it is called the “**Rose Town**”. Since 2007, together with Jona, it has formed the municipality of Rapperswil-Jona.
wichtigste: Rapperswil lies on Lake Zurich in the canton of St Gallen.
The town is called the “Rose Town”.
In several gardens, thousands of roses bloom.
Above the old town stands Rapperswil Castle.
A long wooden footbridge leads across the lake to Hurden.
Since 2007 Rapperswil has belonged to the municipality of Rapperswil-Jona.

abschnitte.text: Rapperswil has several **rose gardens** in which thousands of roses of many varieties bloom in summer. One lies by the **Capuchin monastery**, another in the old town. Two roses can also be seen in the town's **coat of arms**. That is where the nickname “Rose Town” comes from.

The **old town** lies on a small peninsula in the lake. Above it towers **Rapperswil Castle**, which was built in the Middle Ages by the Counts of Rapperswil. For a long time the castle housed a **Polish Museum**, which recalls the history of Poland. The narrow alleys, the lakeside promenade and the harbour make the old town a popular destination for outings.

Between Rapperswil and **Hurden** in the canton of Schwyz, a long **wooden footbridge** crosses the lake. It is over 800 metres long and intended only for pedestrians. As early as the Middle Ages there was a bridge here. Pilgrims on their way to **Einsiedeln Abbey** crossed the lake here. Today the footbridge is part of the Way of St James.

Rapperswil is the home of **Circus Knie**, the well-known Swiss national circus. In the town there is also **Knie's Children's Zoo**, where children can get close to animals. The **OST, Eastern Switzerland University of Applied Sciences**, also has a site right on the lake. Many students study engineering and other subjects here.

gewusst: Roses can also be seen in the coat of arms of Rapperswil.
The wooden footbridge to Hurden links the cantons of St Gallen and Schwyz.

teile.einleitung: Mostbröckli is a meat speciality from the Appenzell region in eastern Switzerland. It is made of beef that is seasoned, smoked and dried. You eat it in wafer-thin slices.
wichtigste: Mostbröckli comes from the Appenzell region.
It is made from lean beef.
The meat is salted, seasoned, smoked and dried.
It is cut into very thin slices.
People like to eat Mostbröckli as a mid-morning snack (Znüni), an afternoon snack (Zvieri) or on a platter with bread and cheese.

abschnitte.text: Mostbröckli is a **dried meat** made of beef. For it, a lean piece is used, that is, meat with little fat. It is typical of the two cantons of **Appenzell Innerrhoden** and **Appenzell Ausserrhoden**. It is also very popular in the area around St Gallen.

First the meat is rubbed with **salt** and spices and stored for some time. After that it is **smoked** over wood. The smoke gives the meat its typical taste and makes it keep longer. Finally it is left to dry until it is firm. Each butcher has his own recipe for the spices.

Mostbröckli is cut into **wafer-thin slices**. It is eaten cold, for example with bread, butter and Appenzeller cheese. On a **platter** of different specialities it is rarely missing in eastern Switzerland. The name has to do with **Most**, that is, apple juice or cider, which in the Appenzell region was often drunk with it in the past.

gewusst: Unlike Bündnerfleisch from the Grisons, which is air-dried, Mostbröckli is also smoked.

teile.einleitung: The Salève is a long mountain ridge just south of Geneva. It lies in France, but the people of Geneva call it their local mountain. From the top you can see over the whole city and Lake Geneva.
wichtigste: The Salève lies in France, in the department of Haute-Savoie.
It is only a few kilometres from the city of Geneva.
The people of Geneva call it their local mountain.
It is just over 1,300 metres high.
A cable car leads up the mountain from the border near Geneva.
From the top you can see Geneva, Lake Geneva and, in clear weather, Mont Blanc.

abschnitte.text: The **Salève** is a limestone mountain that belongs to the Pre-Alps. It begins right behind the **national border** between Switzerland and France. The canton of Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France. That is why its nearest big mountain is not in Switzerland.

A **cable car** leads up from the foot of the mountain near the border. It was built in the 1930s. At the top there are footpaths, meadows and restaurants. Many people from Geneva go up at the weekend to walk or to enjoy the view.

The Salève has steep **rock walls**. More than a hundred years ago, climbers from Geneva were already practising here. The French word “varappe” for rock climbing comes from a gully on the Salève. Today many **paragliders** also take off here.

From the top you have a wide view over **Geneva** and **Lake Geneva**. On the other side you can see the Alps, in clear weather as far as **Mont Blanc**. That is why the Salève is also called the “balcony of Geneva”.

gewusst: The word “varappe”, which is used in French for climbing, comes from the Varappe, a gully on the Salève.
The canton of Geneva borders France for more than 100 kilometres, but borders the rest of Switzerland for only a few kilometres.

teile.einleitung: The Landsgemeinde of Appenzell Innerrhoden is one of the last two Landsgemeinden in Switzerland. Every year the citizens entitled to vote gather in the open air in the village of Appenzell and vote by raising their hands.
wichtigste: The Landsgemeinde takes place on the last Sunday in April.
It is held on the Landsgemeinde square in Appenzell.
Voting is done by a show of hands.
For example, the government and the Landammann are elected.
Since 1991, women have also been allowed to vote at the Landsgemeinde.

abschnitte.titel: A fixed day in the year
abschnitte.text: The **Innerrhoden Landsgemeinde** takes place every year on the **last Sunday in April**. The meeting place is the **Landsgemeinde square** in the village of Appenzell. The citizens entitled to vote stand together in the so-called **Ring**. The members of the government stand on a stage.

On each question, the citizens entitled to vote raise a **hand**, either for yes or for no. The Landammann looks over the crowd and decides which side has the majority. In this way laws are passed and people are elected, for example the government and the judges. Anyone who wants to vote must be able to show their voting card.

In the past only men were allowed to attend the Landsgemeinde. They carried a **sword** or a **bayonet** as a sign that they were entitled to vote. Some men keep up this custom to this day. Today, however, the paper voting card is more important.

Appenzell Innerrhoden was the last canton in which women were allowed to vote at cantonal level. In **1990**, the **Federal Supreme Court** decided that women must be given the right to vote. Since the Landsgemeinde of **1991**, they have taken part in the vote. Since then the Ring has been much fuller.

gewusst: The Landsgemeinde in Appenzell attracts many spectators every year.
Before the vote, the government and the judges walk in a solemn procession to the Landsgemeinde square.

teile.einleitung: The Lauterbrunnen Valley in the Bernese Oberland is famous for its many waterfalls. Between tall, vertical rock walls the water plunges into the depths, and the best known is the Staubbach Falls.
wichtigste: The Lauterbrunnen Valley lies in the Bernese Oberland.
Over 70 waterfalls plunge from the rock walls.
The Staubbach Falls are among the best-known waterfalls in Switzerland.
The Trümmelbach Falls flow inside the mountain.
The valley was shaped by a glacier.

abschnitte.text: The **Lauterbrunnen Valley** lies south of Interlaken in the **Bernese Oberland**. It is a typical **U-shaped valley**: a glacier shaped it in the Ice Age, with a flat valley floor and almost vertical rock walls. Famous mountains such as the **Jungfrau** rise above the valley. The name Lauterbrunnen means roughly “clear springs”.

The **Staubbach Falls** plunge almost 300 metres over a rock wall near the village of Lauterbrunnen. The water falls so far that on the way it dissolves into a fine spray, like dust. That is where its name comes from. The poet **Johann Wolfgang von Goethe** visited it and afterwards wrote a poem.

Further back in the valley lie the **Trümmelbach Falls**. They do not flow down the outside of the wall but **inside the mountain**. A lift and tunnels take visitors up. The water comes from the glaciers of the **Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau** and thunders with great force through the rocky gorges.

High above the valley lie the villages of **Wengen** and **Mürren**. Both are **car-free**, and you can reach them only by rail. In the valley itself lie Lauterbrunnen and Stechelberg. In summer many people walk through the valley, and in winter people ski in the area.

gewusst: After his visit to the Staubbach Falls, Goethe wrote the poem “Song of the Spirits over the Waters”.
Part of the Lauterbrunnen Valley belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.

teile.einleitung: The **Papet vaudois** is a typical dish from the canton of Vaud. It consists of leeks and potatoes and is eaten with a hearty Vaud sausage. Many families like to cook it especially in winter.
wichtigste: The Papet vaudois is a speciality from the canton of Vaud.
It consists mainly of leeks and potatoes.
It is served with a Vaud sausage.
The word “papet” means something like mash.
The dish is simple, filling and often eaten in winter.

abschnitte.text: For the Papet vaudois, **leeks** are cut into pieces and lightly sautéed. Then **potatoes** are added, which slowly become soft in the pot. Often some stock is added, and sometimes a splash of white wine. In the end the vegetables are so soft that they look almost like a coarse mash. That is where the name comes from: in this area “papet” means something like mash.

A **Vaud sausage** is laid on top of the leeks and potatoes. Well known are the **Saucisson vaudois** and the **Saucisse aux choux**, a sausage with cabbage. Both sausages are protected specialities: only sausages from the region may bear these names. The sausage is usually cooked gently along with the vegetables. In this way the whole dish gets its spicy flavour.

The canton of Vaud lies in French-speaking Switzerland on **Lake Geneva**, and its main town is **Lausanne**. French is spoken here, which is why the dish has a French name. The Papet vaudois is an old **farmhouse dish**: it needs few ingredients, which in the past people grew or made themselves. Today it is on the menu in many restaurants in the region and is regarded as a piece of Vaud tradition.

gewusst: “Vaudois” is the French word for “from Vaud”.
The Vaud sausages are registered in Switzerland as protected specialities, similar to certain kinds of cheese.

teile.einleitung: The Mouettes genevoises are small yellow boats in Geneva. They cross Lake Geneva from one bank of the city to the other, almost like a bus on the water. They are part of Geneva's public transport.
wichtigste: “Mouette” is French and means “seagull”.
The Mouettes are small yellow passenger boats.
They link the left and right banks of the lake in Geneva.
There are several lines with fixed stops.
With an ordinary ticket for bus and tram, you can also use the Mouettes.

abschnitte.text: In Geneva, the **Rhône** flows out of Lake Geneva. The city therefore lies on two banks. To avoid always having to cross a bridge, there are the **Mouettes**. These small yellow boats run regularly back and forth between the banks on several **lines**. The crossing takes only a few minutes.

The Mouettes are part of Geneva's **public transport**. That is why the same ticket applies to them as to buses and trams. Many people use them to get to work or school. Tourists also like to use them, because from the water you have a lovely view of the city and the **Jet d'eau**.

The name **Mouettes** means **seagulls** in English. Seagulls are birds that you often see on the lake. Like the birds, the little boats also dart across the water. The yellow colour makes them easy to see and has become a hallmark of Geneva.

gewusst: From the water you can see the Jet d'eau, Geneva's famous water fountain, especially well.

teile.einleitung: Neuchâtel, in German Neuenburg, is the main town of the canton of Neuchâtel. The city lies on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel at the foot of the Jura. It is known for its old town of pale yellow stone, its castle and its university.
wichtigste: Neuchâtel is the main town of the canton of Neuchâtel.
In German the city is called Neuenburg.
French is spoken in Neuchâtel.
The city lies on Lake Neuchâtel.
Above the old town stand the castle and the collegiate church.
Neuchâtel belonged to Prussia for a long time and only became a republic in 1848.

abschnitte.text: The name **Neuchâtel** means “new castle”. The city is already mentioned in the year **1011**. Above the old town stand the **castle** and the **collegiate church**, in French the Collégiale. Today the government and parliament of the canton meet in the castle.

Neuchâtel has an unusual history. From **1707**, the principality of Neuchâtel was linked with the **King of Prussia**. In 1815 it nevertheless became a canton of the Confederation. In **1848**, the people of Neuchâtel proclaimed the **republic**. A few years later Prussia finally gave up its claims.

Many houses in the old town are built of a **yellowish limestone** from the Jura. That is why Neuchâtel looks warm and bright in sunshine. The writer Alexandre Dumas is said to have compared the city with butter for this reason. In the alleys there are fountains, squares and small shops.

Neuchâtel has a **university** and many schools. In the region, research has long been carried out on **watches** and precise technology. Near the city lies the **Laténium** museum. It shows finds from prehistory, including objects of the **Celts** from nearby La Tène.

gewusst: A whole period of the Celts, the La Tène period, is named after the find site of La Tène near Neuchâtel.
In Neuchâtel people say that French is spoken there especially clearly and beautifully.

teile.einleitung: Lake Maggiore is a large lake south of the Alps. Its northern end lies in the canton of Ticino, but the largest part belongs to Italy. On its shore lies the lowest point in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Maggiore lies for the most part in Italy, the north in Ticino.
Locarno lies at the northern end of the lake.
The lowest point in Switzerland, at about 193 metres above sea level, lies on Lake Maggiore.
The climate by the lake is mild, and even palm trees grow.
On the Brissago Islands there is a botanical garden.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Maggiore** is also called **Langensee** in German, meaning “long lake”, because it is very long and narrow. Only the northern part lies in Switzerland, in the canton of **Ticino**. The largest part belongs to **Italy**. Large rivers such as the **Ticino** and the **Maggia** flow into the lake.

The shore of Lake Maggiore lies at only about **193 metres above sea level**. This is the **lowest point in Switzerland**. For comparison: the highest point, the Dufourspitze in Valais, is over 4,600 metres high. So within little Switzerland there are huge differences in height.

The Alps protect the lake from cold winds from the north. That is why the climate on Lake Maggiore is especially **mild**. In gardens, **palm trees**, camellias and other plants from warm countries grow. On the **Brissago Islands** there is a botanical garden with plants from all over the world.

At the northern end of the lake lies the town of **Locarno**. It is known for the **film festival** on the Piazza Grande, where films are shown under the open sky. Right next to it lies **Ascona** with its lakeside promenade. Many people from German-speaking Switzerland spend their holidays here.

gewusst: With its many hours of sunshine, Locarno is one of the sunniest places in Switzerland.
After Lake Garda, Lake Maggiore is the second largest lake in Italy.

t1djmf0o.t: International Committee of the Red Cross

teile.einleitung: The International Committee of the Red Cross, ICRC for short, is an aid organisation based in Geneva. It was founded in 1863 and helps people who suffer because of wars and armed conflicts.
wichtigste: The ICRC was founded in Geneva in 1863.
Henry Dunant gave the impetus for it.
Its emblem is a red cross on a white background, the reversed Swiss flag.
The ICRC helps the injured, prisoners and people in war zones.
It works to make sure the Geneva Conventions are respected.
The ICRC is neutral and does not take sides.

abschnitte.text: In 1859, after a battle at Solferino in Italy, the Geneva businessman **Henry Dunant** saw thousands of wounded men whom hardly anyone was looking after. He helped others to care for them. He wrote a book about it: “A Memory of Solferino”. In it he suggested founding relief societies in all countries. In 1901, Dunant received the first **Nobel Peace Prize**.

In 1863, Dunant and four other people from Geneva founded a committee, often called the **Committee of Five**. General Guillaume-Henri Dufour was also part of it. This committee became the International Committee of the Red Cross. As early as 1864, several states signed the first **Geneva Convention**. It requires that wounded soldiers are protected and cared for.

As the protective emblem, a **red cross on a white background** was chosen. This is the Swiss flag with the colours swapped, as an honour to Switzerland. Anyone wearing this emblem is not to be attacked in war. Later the **Red Crescent**, which many countries use, was added.

The ICRC visits **prisoners of war** and makes sure they are treated humanely. It helps families who were separated in war to get back in touch. It brings water, food and medical help to war zones. **Neutrality** is important: the ICRC helps all people in need, no matter which side they are on.

gewusst: The ICRC has received the Nobel Peace Prize three times.
In Geneva there is a museum about the Red Cross and the Red Crescent.

teile.einleitung: Martigny is a town in Lower Valais. The Romans already had an important settlement here, which they called Octodurus. A Roman amphitheatre still recalls this time today.
wichtigste: Martigny lies in the canton of Valais at the bend of the Rhône.
Here the Rhône turns almost at a right angle to the north.
The Romans called the place Octodurus.
A Roman amphitheatre has survived to this day.
French is spoken in Martigny.
From here the road leads to the Great St Bernard.

abschnitte.text: Even before the Romans, Celts lived here. The Romans built the town of **Octodurus** at this spot. Under Emperor Claudius it was also called **Forum Claudii Vallensium** and was the main town of Valais. One important reason was its position on the route over the Great St Bernard to Italy. During excavations, streets, temples and houses were found.

The Roman **amphitheatre** of Martigny is the only well-preserved amphitheatre in Valais. In an amphitheatre, spectators sat around an arena. Today events are held in it again. Well known are the **cow fights** of the Hérens cows, which are held here every year in autumn.

In Martigny stands the **Fondation Pierre Gianadda**, a well-known art museum. It was built over Roman wall remains, and there are sculptures in the garden. The town also has a museum about the **St Bernard dogs**, which in the past rescued travellers in the snow on the Great St Bernard.

Martigny lies at the **bend of the Rhône**, where the Rhône turns from south-west to north-west. The Dranse also flows into the Rhône here. From Martigny, roads lead to the **Great St Bernard** and Italy and over the Col de la Forclaz to Chamonix in France. That is why the place has always been an important junction for travellers.

gewusst: The name Octodurus is of Celtic origin, and the Romans took it over.
The Fondation Pierre Gianadda came about when the remains of a Roman temple were found during the building of a house.

teile.einleitung: Gruyère is one of the best-known cheeses in Switzerland. It is named after the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg, and is eaten all over the world today.
wichtigste: Le Gruyère is a hard cheese made from cow's milk.
Its name comes from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.
It is made in French-speaking Switzerland, above all in the cantons of Fribourg, Vaud, Neuchâtel and Jura.
Since 2001 it has had a protected designation of origin (AOP).
A wheel is round and weighs about 35 kilograms.
The cheese matures for several months in cellars.
Gruyère is part of many fondues.

abschnitte.text: Le Gruyère is made from the **raw milk** of cows, that is, milk that has not been heated. The cows may eat only grass and hay, no silage. Since 2001 the name has been protected as **AOP**. This means that only cheese from a precisely defined area and made according to fixed rules may be called Le Gruyère. This area lies mainly in French-speaking Switzerland.

In the **dairy**, the milk is warmed in large copper vats. With rennet it thickens, and then the cheesemaker cuts the mass into small grains. These go into round moulds and are pressed. After that the wheels lie in a **salt bath**. In the cellar they are regularly turned and rubbed with salt water while they mature for several months.

The **Gruyère region** lies in the south of the canton of Fribourg, on the edge of the Pre-Alps. Well known is the little town of **Gruyères** with its castle on a hill. In nearby Pringy there is a show dairy where you can watch cheese being made. The viewpoint mountain **Moléson** also belongs to this region.

Depending on its age, Le Gruyère tastes mild or strong. Young cheese is delicate, older cheese tastes spicier. It is often eaten with bread, grated over gratins or melted. In a **fondue moitié-moitié** (half and half) it is mixed half and half with Vacherin fribourgeois, another cheese from the canton of Fribourg.

gewusst: There is also a Le Gruyère d'alpage, which is made only in summer on alps.
A single wheel of Gruyère needs about 400 litres of milk.

teile.einleitung: Lake Murten is a lake in the west of Switzerland on which the town of Murten lies. It is the smallest of the three large lakes in the so-called Three Lakes Region. In summer you can swim, sail and take boat trips here.
wichtigste: Lake Murten lies in the cantons of Fribourg and Vaud.
On its shore lies the town of Murten.
Together with Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Biel, it forms the Three Lakes Region.
The Broye Canal links it with Lake Neuchâtel.
On the north shore lies the Mont Vully with its vineyards.

abschnitte.titel: A lake in the Three Lakes Region
abschnitte.text: Lake Murten is one of three lakes at the foot of the **Jura**. The other two are **Lake Neuchâtel** and **Lake Biel**. Together the area is called the **Three Lakes Region**. Lake Murten is the smallest of the three. It is linked with Lake Neuchâtel by the **Broye Canal**, so that boats can travel from one lake to the other.

In the past, the land around the three lakes was often flooded. In the 19th and 20th centuries, canals were therefore built and the water levels of the lakes were lowered. These large building works are called the **Jura Water Correction**. Since then, the land in the **Grosses Moos** has been dry and fertile. A lot of vegetables are grown there.

On the south shore lies the old town of **Murten** with its town wall. On the north shore rises the **Mont Vully**, a hill with vineyards. Wine is grown there. Walking and cycling paths lead around the lake. In summer, scheduled boats run, and many people swim in the lake.

gewusst: A large part of Swiss vegetables grows in the Grosses Moos next to Lake Murten.
Lake Murten lies partly in the canton of Fribourg and partly in the canton of Vaud.

teile.einleitung: Melchsee-Frutt is a holiday and ski area in the canton of Obwalden. It lies at almost 1,900 metres, high above the Melchtal, around Lake Melch.
wichtigste: Melchsee-Frutt lies in the canton of Obwalden, in the municipality of Kerns.
Lake Melch lies at almost 1,900 metres above sea level.
A gondola lift runs up from Stöckalp in the Melchtal.
On the Frutt there are several mountain lakes.
In summer people walk, in winter they ski.
A well-known walk leads over several lakes as far as Engelberg.

abschnitte.text: The **Melchtal** stretches up into the mountains from Sarnen and Kerns. At its far end lies **Stöckalp**. From there a **gondola lift** takes guests up to the high plateau of the Frutt. At the top lie **Lake Melch** and a small holiday village with hotels and a chapel. All around rise peaks such as the Hochstollen.

In summer, Melchsee-Frutt is a popular **walking area**. Beside Lake Melch lie the **Blausee** and the **Tannensee**. A well-known tour is the **Four Lakes Walk**: it leads from the Frutt past the Tannensee, the Engstlensee and the Trübsee as far as Engelberg. At Lake Melch you can also fish.

Because the Frutt lies so high, there is usually a lot of **snow** there in winter. Ski lifts and chairlifts open up the pistes around the lake. You can also sledge, go snowshoeing and cross-country skiing. In winter Lake Melch is often **frozen over** and covered with snow.

gewusst: The holiday village on Melchsee-Frutt is one of the highest holiday resorts in central Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Schaffhausen is the main town of the canton of Schaffhausen and has the same name as the canton. The town lies right on the Rhine in the north of Switzerland. It is known for its old town, the round Munot fortress and the nearby Rhine Falls.
wichtigste: Schaffhausen is the main town of the canton of the same name.
The town lies on the Rhine.
The canton lies almost entirely north of the Rhine and mostly borders Germany.
The town's landmark is the Munot, a round fortress.
In the old town there are many houses with ornate oriel windows.
The Rhine Falls at Neuhausen are very close by.

abschnitte.titel: A town thanks to the Rhine
abschnitte.text: Schaffhausen grew up at an important spot on the **Rhine**. Downstream lie the **Rhine Falls**, which no ships can pass. So goods had to be unloaded here and carried on by cart. Trade made the town rich in the Middle Ages. The name probably recalls the boat houses where goods were stored.

High above the old town stands the **Munot**, a round fortress. It was built in the 16th century. From the tower there is a wide view over the town and the Rhine. Every evening the **Munotglöggli** (little Munot bell) rings there. In the past it signalled that the town gates and inns were being closed.

The old town of Schaffhausen is well preserved. Many houses have colourful façades and richly decorated **oriel windows**, that is, small projecting bays with windows. That is why Schaffhausen is also called the **oriel town**. A well-known building is the House of the Knight with its painted façade. The Allerheiligen Minster used to be a monastery.

Schaffhausen joined the **Swiss Confederation** in 1501. The canton lies almost entirely north of the Rhine and is mostly surrounded by **Germany**. The town is a centre of industry, trade and culture. By train you can quickly reach Zurich, but also Germany.

gewusst: The Rhine Falls at Neuhausen are considered the largest waterfall in central Europe in terms of the amount of water.
In the Second World War, Schaffhausen was bombed by mistake by American aircraft in 1944.

teile.einleitung: The Pestalozzi Children's Village stands in Trogen in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. It was founded after the Second World War to give a home to children who had lost everything in the war.
wichtigste: The Pestalozzi Children's Village was founded in Trogen in 1946.
It took in children who had lost their family or their home in the Second World War.
It is named after the Swiss educator Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi.
Today it is a foundation that works for education and understanding between peoples.
School classes from many countries visit the village for exchange projects.

abschnitte.text: After the **Second World War**, very many children in Europe lived without parents or without a home. In Switzerland, the idea arose to build a village of their own for them. In **1946**, work began on it in **Trogen** in the Appenzell region. Many volunteers helped to build the houses.

The children came from different countries. They lived in houses, often together with children from their own country, and were looked after by house parents. At school they learned their own language and culture, but also those of the others. In this way, children from countries that had fought wars against each other were to become friends.

**Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi** lived from 1746 to 1827 and was a famous Swiss educator. He worked to ensure that poor children, too, received a good education. He wanted to develop children's head, heart and hands equally. That is why his name suits the children's village so well.

Today the **Pestalozzi Children's Village Foundation** is above all an organisation for education. It supports school projects in various countries of the world. In Trogen there are exchange weeks in which school classes learn together how to break down prejudice and live together peacefully.

gewusst: The idea for the children's village came from the Swiss man Walter Robert Corti.
The children's village in Trogen was a model for similar villages in other countries.

teile.einleitung: Le Corbusier is one of the most famous architects of the 20th century. He was born in 1887 in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel and, with his ideas, changed how houses and cities are built.
wichtigste: Le Corbusier was actually called Charles-Édouard Jeanneret.
He was born in 1887 in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel.
Later he lived mainly in Paris and became French.
He was an architect, town planner, painter and furniture designer.
He built with concrete, clear shapes and long bands of windows.
Several of his buildings have been UNESCO World Heritage Sites since 2016.
His portrait was on the Swiss ten-franc note of the eighth series.

abschnitte.text: Charles-Édouard Jeanneret grew up in **La Chaux-de-Fonds**, a watchmaking town in the Neuchâtel Jura. At first he learned engraving of watch cases at the art school. A teacher recognised his talent and encouraged him. Even as a young man he built his first houses in his home town, for example the **Maison Blanche** for his parents. After that he travelled through Europe and learned a great deal about old and new architecture.

In Paris, from about 1920, he called himself **Le Corbusier**. He wanted to build houses that are bright, practical and affordable for many people. Well known are his **five points of architecture**: pillars instead of thick walls, a garden on the roof, a freely arranged floor plan, long bands of windows and a free façade. He also invented the **Modulor**, a system of measurement based on the human body.

One of his best-known houses is the **Villa Savoye** near Paris. In Marseille he built the **Unité d'Habitation**, a large apartment block like a small town with shops and a roof terrace. The chapel of **Ronchamp** in France has a curved roof and looks almost like a sculpture. In India he planned large parts of the city of **Chandigarh**.

There are also works by Le Corbusier in Switzerland. On Lake Geneva he built the **Villa Le Lac** in Corseaux for his parents, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Geneva stands the apartment building **Immeuble Clarté**. In Zurich stands the colourful **Pavillon Le Corbusier**, his last building, which was only finished after his death in 1965. Switzerland honoured him with his portrait on the ten-franc note.

gewusst: Le Corbusier was not only an architect: he also painted many pictures and designed furniture such as comfortable steel-tube loungers.
In 2016, UNESCO added 17 of his buildings in seven countries together to the World Heritage List.

teile.einleitung: The Klewenalp is a ski and walking area in the canton of Nidwalden. It lies high above Beckenried on Lake Lucerne and is known for its beautiful view.
wichtigste: The Klewenalp lies above Beckenried in Nidwalden.
A cable car runs up from Beckenried.
In winter you can ski and sledge there.
In summer you can walk with a view of Lake Lucerne.
The area is linked with the Stockhütte above Emmetten.

abschnitte.text: From **Beckenried** on the shore of Lake Lucerne, a **cable car** runs up to the Klewenalp. The ride takes only a few minutes and passes over forest and meadows. At the top, the alp lies at about 1,600 metres above sea level. From there you can see far over the lake and the surrounding mountains.

In winter the Klewenalp is a popular **ski area**, above all for families from central Switzerland. Together with the **Stockhütte** above Emmetten, it forms a joint area with ski lifts and pistes. There are also sledging runs and winter walking trails.
