In summer the Klewenalp becomes a **walking area**. Cows graze on the pastures, and alpine paths lead to viewpoints. The view stretches over **Lake Lucerne** as far as Pilatus and the Rigi. Many visitors combine the cable car with a boat trip on the lake.

gewusst: From the Klewenalp, on clear days you can see several arms of Lake Lucerne at once.

teile.einleitung: The Linth Correction was a great construction project at the beginning of the 19th century. It tamed the Linth in the canton of Glarus and saved the Linth plain from flooding. From 1807 it was led by Hans Conrad Escher.
wichtigste: In the past, the Linth repeatedly flooded the plain between Lake Walen and Lake Zurich.
Many people suffered from poverty and marsh fever.
From 1807, Hans Conrad Escher of Zurich led the building work.
Since 1811, the Escher Canal has led the Linth into Lake Walen.
The Linth Canal links Lake Walen with Lake Zurich.
Escher was given the honorary name “von der Linth”.
The Linth Correction is regarded as one of the first joint works of Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The Linth carried a lot of **rubble** and gravel down from the mountains. Because of forest clearing, there was more and more of it. The material settled in the riverbed, which rose higher and higher. The Linth often burst its banks, and the level of Lake Walen rose. The plain turned into a **marsh**, fields were lost, and many people fell ill with marsh fever.

**Hans Conrad Escher** was a Zurich politician and naturalist. He worked to bring the Linth under control. The **Tagsatzung** (Diet), the assembly of the cantons, approved the plan. The money came, among other sources, from citizens all over Switzerland who bought **shares**. Escher led the work from 1807, often on site himself and without pay.

The plan was clever: the Linth was no longer to flow through the plain but through a canal into **Lake Walen**. There the rubble sinks to the bottom of the lake. This **Escher Canal** was opened in 1811. After that the **Linth Canal** was built from Lake Walen to Lake Zurich. Since then the water has flowed away in straight, reinforced canals.

After the correction, the Linth plain dried out and could be farmed again. The floods and the marsh fever declined sharply. Escher died in 1823. In thanks he was given the honorary name **Escher von der Linth**. The Linth Correction is regarded as one of the first great **joint building projects** of the Confederation.

gewusst: Hans Conrad Escher's son, Arnold Escher von der Linth, also became famous, as a geologist.
On the Linth, a monument recalls Escher and his work.

teile.einleitung: The Lucerne Carnival is one of the largest and most colourful festivals in Switzerland. For six days, Guggenmusigen (carnival brass bands) and people in imaginative masks parade through the alleys of Lucerne's old town.
wichtigste: The Lucerne Carnival lasts from Schmutziger Donnerstag (Fat Thursday) to Güdisdienstag (Shrove Tuesday).
It begins on Thursday at 5 am with the “Urknall”.
Guggenmusigen play loud, off-key and cheerful music.
Many people wear large, home-made masks, the “Grinde”.
On Güdismontag and Güdisdienstag there are large parades.
An important figure is the Fritschi.

abschnitte.text: The Lucerne Carnival begins on **Schmutziger Donnerstag** (Fat Thursday), early at 5 am. It starts with a loud bang, the **Urknall** (“Big Bang”). The **Fritschi**, the most important figure of the Lucerne Carnival, is welcomed. At once the Guggenmusigen begin to play. Thousands of people stand in the alleys despite the dark and the cold.

A **Guggenmusig** is a group that plays with trumpets, trombones, kettledrums and drums. The music is deliberately loud and a little off-key. Each group has its own **costumes**, which are often made over the whole year. On Güdisdienstag in the evening, many Guggenmusigen play at the same time in the old town, which is called the **Monsterkonzert**.

Typical of Lucerne are the large masks called **Grinde**. They show animals, fantasy creatures or funny faces. On **Güdismontag** and **Güdisdienstag**, large parades move through the city. Groups show floats and costumes, and often make fun of events of the year.

The carnival takes place every year before **Lent**, which begins on Ash Wednesday. That is why the date is different every year, as it depends on Easter. In Lucerne the carnival ends in the night leading into Ash Wednesday. The **Basel Carnival**, on the other hand, only begins on the Monday after Ash Wednesday.

gewusst: Every year the Lucerne Carnival draws a great many visitors from all over Switzerland.
The Fritschi is regarded as the father of the Lucerne Carnival and has been part of the carnival for centuries.

teile.einleitung: The **Paul Scherrer Institute**, **PSI** for short, is the largest research institute for natural sciences and engineering in Switzerland. It lies in Villigen and Würenlingen in the canton of Aargau. Here stand huge machines with which researchers study the smallest building blocks of the world.
wichtigste: The PSI is the largest research institute for natural sciences and engineering in Switzerland.
It lies in Villigen and Würenlingen on the Aare in the canton of Aargau.
It came into being in 1988 from two older research institutes.
It is named after the Swiss physicist Paul Scherrer.
The PSI belongs to the ETH Domain and is supported by the Confederation.
It runs large facilities such as particle accelerators and a synchrotron light source.

abschnitte.titel: An institute for the whole of Switzerland
abschnitte.text: The PSI was founded in **1988**, when two older research institutes were merged. It lies on both sides of the **Aare** between Villigen and Würenlingen. The institute belongs to the **ETH Domain**, together with ETH Zurich, EPFL in Lausanne and further research institutes. The money comes largely from the **Confederation**. A great many people work at the PSI, including researchers from all over the world.

**Paul Scherrer** was a Swiss **physicist**. He taught for many years at ETH Zurich and researched, among other things, how atoms are arranged in crystals. He campaigned for Switzerland to carry out its own research in nuclear physics. A method for studying crystals is also named after him. The institute bears his name to recall his work.

The PSI runs **large research facilities** that exist only here in Switzerland. A **proton accelerator** brings tiny particles to very high speed. The **Swiss Light Source (SLS)** produces extremely bright X-ray light. The **SwissFEL** is an X-ray laser with which you can observe very fast processes in molecules. Researchers from all over the world come to the PSI to use these facilities.

At the PSI there are three large areas: **matter and materials**, **energy and the environment** and **people and health**. For example, new materials for batteries or computers are studied. Other groups research how energy can be produced and stored more cleanly. In the area of health, the PSI offers **proton therapy**, with which certain tumours are irradiated very precisely.

The PSI wants children and young people to be able to experience research too. In the **visitor centre**, you are shown what happens at the institute. In a **school lab** of its own, school classes can do physics experiments themselves. In this way they learn how science works. Perhaps one of them will later work on the big machines in Villigen.

gewusst: The Swiss Light Source is a ring that is larger than a football pitch.
The PSI lies on two sides of the Aare, and the two parts are linked by a bridge.

teile.einleitung: The Culture and Congress Centre Lucerne, KKL for short, stands right on Lake Lucerne next to Lucerne railway station. It is world famous for its concert hall.
wichtigste: The KKL stands right on the lake in Lucerne.
It was designed by the French architect Jean Nouvel.
Its large, flat roof juts far out over the lake.
The concert hall is regarded as one of the best in the world.
The Lucerne Festival takes place there every year.

abschnitte.text: The **KKL Lucerne** stands on the shore of **Lake Lucerne**, right next to the railway station. The French architect **Jean Nouvel** designed it. It opened at the end of the 1990s. Especially striking is the huge, flat **roof**, which juts far out over the square and the water.

The heart of the KKL is the large **concert hall**. It was built so that the music sounds very clear everywhere in the hall. This is called good **acoustics**. Around the hall there are chambers that can be opened or closed to change the sound. Many famous orchestras like to play here.

Every year the **Lucerne Festival**, one of the most important music festivals in the world, takes place in the KKL. Orchestras, conductors and soloists from many countries perform. Besides this, the KKL also hosts other concerts, congresses and events.

On the top floor of the KKL is the **Lucerne Museum of Art**. It shows changing exhibitions with art from different periods. From the terrace you can see over the lake, the old town and the Chapel Bridge. In this way the building combines music, art and a view.

gewusst: The architect Jean Nouvel wanted the building to seem connected with the lake and the landscape.
The roof of the KKL is so large that on the forecourt beneath it you stay dry even in the rain.

teile.einleitung: IWC Schaffhausen is a well-known watch brand based in the city of Schaffhausen. The company was founded in 1868 by an American and still makes expensive mechanical watches today.
wichtigste: IWC is based in the city of Schaffhausen.
The company was founded in 1868.
The founder was the American watchmaker Florentine Ariosto Jones.
IWC stands for “International Watch Company”.
The company makes expensive mechanical watches.
It is one of the few large watch brands in German-speaking Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The watchmaker **Florentine Ariosto Jones** came to Switzerland from the USA. He wanted to combine good Swiss craftsmanship with modern machines. In 1868 he founded the **International Watch Company**, IWC for short, in Schaffhausen. The watches were mainly to be sold in America. That is why the company still has an English name today.

Most Swiss watch companies are in French-speaking Switzerland and in the Jura. Schaffhausen, however, offered something special: the **Rhine**. The power of the water could be used to drive machines. There were also workers in the area. This is how a large watch factory came to be built on the bank of the Rhine.

IWC mainly makes **mechanical watches**, which run without a battery. Inside, tiny cogwheels and springs do the work. The brand is known for pilot's watches and sturdy watches with many functions. The watches are very expensive, because a lot of handwork goes into them. Today IWC belongs to a large group, but it still produces in Schaffhausen.

gewusst: A mechanical watch can consist of hundreds of individual parts.
IWC is one of the few large watch brands that do not come from French-speaking Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Leimental is a valley south-west of Basel. It lies in three areas at once: in the canton of Basel-Landschaft, in the canton of Solothurn and in France.
wichtigste: The Leimental lies south-west of the city of Basel.
The Birsig flows through the valley and joins the Rhine in Basel.
One part belongs to the canton of Basel-Landschaft, one part to the canton of Solothurn.
Another part lies in Alsace in France.
At Schönenbuch, Basel-Landschaft borders directly on France.
A tram line runs through the valley and briefly through France.

abschnitte.text: The Leimental is a gentle, hilly valley. Municipalities such as Binningen, Oberwil, Therwil, Ettingen and Schönenbuch belong to the canton of **Basel-Landschaft**. Rodersdorf, Metzerlen and Hofstetten-Flüh, for example, belong to the canton of **Solothurn**. The western part, with places such as Leymen, lies in **Alsace**, that is, in France. The borders here are very winding.

**Tram line 10** runs from Basel through the Leimental to Rodersdorf. On the way it runs for a stretch through France and stops at Leymen. This makes it one of the few tram lines that cross a national border. Many people from the Leimental use it every day to travel to work or school in Basel.

The **Birsig** flows through the valley, a small river that flows under the city of Basel into the Rhine. In the Leimental there are fields, fruit trees, forests and many walking paths. High above Flüh lies **Mariastein Abbey**, a well-known place of pilgrimage in the canton of Solothurn.

gewusst: Anyone walking in the Leimental can cross back and forth between Switzerland and France several times in one afternoon.

teile.einleitung: **Pfäffikon** is a place in the canton of Schwyz on the southern shore of **Lake Zurich**. So that it is not confused with Pfäffikon in the canton of Zurich, it is often written “Pfäffikon SZ”. The place is an important transport hub in the Höfe region.
wichtigste: Pfäffikon SZ lies on the southern shore of Lake Zurich.
The place belongs to the municipality of Freienbach in the district of Höfe.
There is also a Pfäffikon in the canton of Zurich, hence the addition “SZ”.
Pfäffikon is linked with Rapperswil by the Seedamm.
Pfäffikon Castle belongs to Einsiedeln Abbey.
Pfäffikon is an important railway and motorway junction.

abschnitte.text: Pfäffikon lies on the **southern shore of Lake Zurich** in the **district of Höfe**. Politically the place belongs to the **municipality of Freienbach**. From the shore you can see the islands of **Ufenau** and **Lützelau**. The Ufenau is the largest island in Lake Zurich and is under nature protection. Behind the village the land rises to the Etzel, a hill with a lovely view.

Between Pfäffikon and Rapperswil, Lake Zurich is very narrow. Here the **Seedamm** (lake causeway) crosses the water, carrying road and railway. It separates Lake Zurich from the **Obersee** (Upper Lake). Even in ancient times, people crossed the lake here, for example pilgrims on their way to Einsiedeln. Today, beside the causeway, there is also a long **wooden footbridge** for pedestrians.

On the lake stands **Pfäffikon Castle** with an old residential tower. It has belonged to **Einsiedeln Abbey** since the Middle Ages. The island of Ufenau is also owned by the abbey. In the past, Einsiedeln Abbey had a lot of land and great influence in the Höfe region. The castle and many field names recall this to this day.

Pfäffikon SZ has an important **railway station**. Trains towards Zurich, Chur and Einsiedeln meet here. The motorway also passes by the place. That is why many firms and shops have settled here. For people who work in Zurich, Pfäffikon is a popular place to live.

The canton of Schwyz is known for its mountains, but it also has a lot of lakeshore. It borders **Lake Zurich**, **Lake Lucerne** and **Lake Zug**. Entirely within the canton lie **Lake Lauerz** and **Lake Sihl**, a reservoir. Pfäffikon is, so to speak, the canton's gateway to Lake Zurich.

gewusst: In Switzerland there are two places called Pfäffikon, one in the canton of Schwyz and one in the canton of Zurich.
The island of Ufenau belongs politically to the municipality of Freienbach and thus to the canton of Schwyz.

teile.einleitung: The Kunstmuseum Basel is one of the most important art museums in Switzerland. It is regarded as the oldest public art collection in the world, because its history begins as early as 1661.
wichtigste: The Kunstmuseum Basel stands in the canton of Basel-Stadt.
It is regarded as the oldest public art collection in the world.
In 1661 the city of Basel bought the Amerbach Cabinet.
The museum owns many works by Hans Holbein the Younger.
Today it consists of the main building, the new building and the Museum of Contemporary Art.

abschnitte.text: In the 16th century, the Basel **Amerbach** family collected paintings, drawings, coins and books. This collection is called the **Amerbach Cabinet**. In **1661**, the city of Basel, together with the university, bought the whole collection. In this way it became the property of the public, and this is regarded as the beginning of the oldest public art collection in the world.

The museum owns a large collection of works by **Hans Holbein the Younger**, who worked in Basel for a long time. There are also pictures from many centuries, from the Middle Ages to the present day. Works by well-known painters such as **Pablo Picasso** or Vincent van Gogh also hang here.

The **main building** on the St. Alban-Graben opened in the 1930s. In 2016 the **new building** was added on the other side of the street, linked by an underground passage. The **Museum of Contemporary Art** on the Rhine shows art of recent decades. Together they make up the Kunstmuseum Basel.

In **1967**, the people of Basel voted in a referendum on whether the city should spend money on two pictures by Picasso. The majority said yes. Picasso was so pleased about this that he gave the museum further works. This story shows how important their art collection is to many people in Basel.

gewusst: Basel is also known worldwide for the art fair Art Basel.
The purchase of the Amerbach Cabinet took place over 350 years ago.

teile.einleitung: Porrentruy Castle towers above the old town of Porrentruy in the canton of Jura. In German the town is called Pruntrut. From the 16th century the castle was the main residence of the Prince-Bishops of Basel.
wichtigste: Porrentruy (German: Pruntrut) lies in the canton of Jura.
The castle stands on a hill above the old town.
After the Reformation in Basel the Prince-Bishops moved to Porrentruy.
From here they ruled their prince-bishopric until the French Revolution.
The oldest part is a round tower from the Middle Ages.
Today the castle is used by the canton of Jura.

abschnitte.text: The **Prince-Bishops of Basel** were not only church leaders but also worldly rulers. They owned a territory, the **Prince-Bishopric of Basel**, which included the present-day Jura. When Basel became Protestant around 1529, the Catholic bishops could no longer stay in the city. They moved to **Porrentruy**.

The castle was extended to become the **residence** of the Prince-Bishops. From here they ruled their land for over 250 years. The oldest part is the round **Tour Réfous** from the Middle Ages. Alongside it, residential buildings, courtyards and gardens were added. From the castle you can look out over the roofs of the old town.

During the **French Revolution**, French troops occupied the territory. The last Prince-Bishop had to flee, and the prince-bishopric came to an end. After 1815 the Jura went to the canton of **Bern**. Only in 1979 did the Jura become a canton of its own.

Today the **canton of Jura** uses the castle, among other things for parts of the administration and the archive. The old town of Porrentruy has many beautiful buildings from the time of the Prince-Bishops. Porrentruy lies in the **Ajoie**, in the far north-west of Switzerland, close to France.

gewusst: The canton of Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland; it was created in 1979.
The Ajoie around Porrentruy borders France on three sides.

teile.einleitung: **Pilatus Aircraft** is a Swiss company that builds aeroplanes in **Stans** in the canton of Nidwalden. Its aircraft fly all over the world. The company is named after the mountain Pilatus, which stands nearby.
wichtigste: Pilatus Aircraft has its seat in Stans in the canton of Nidwalden.
The company was founded in 1939.
It builds trainer aircraft, business aircraft and robust light aircraft.
Well-known models are the PC-6 Porter, the PC-12, the PC-21 and the PC-24 jet.
Many air forces in the world train their pilots with Pilatus aircraft.
Pilatus is an important employer in central Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Pilatus Aircraft was founded in **1939**. The factory lies in **Stans** right next to **Buochs** airfield, from which the new aircraft can take off. The company is named after the mountain **Pilatus**. Today Pilatus is one of the largest employers in central Switzerland. In Stans, many young people are also trained as skilled workers.

A famous Pilatus aircraft is the **PC-6 Porter**. It can take off and land on very short runways, even on meadows or glaciers. That is why it was used in mountains and remote areas. The **PC-12** is an aircraft with only a single propeller engine. It is used, for example, as a business aircraft and for rescue flights.

Pilatus also builds **trainer aircraft** for air forces. These include the **PC-7**, the **PC-9** and the **PC-21**. On them, future military pilots learn to fly. The **Swiss Air Force** also uses such aircraft. The Air Force's **PC-7 Team** performs aerobatics with them at air shows.

With the **PC-24**, Pilatus built an aircraft with **jet engines** for the first time. It is a business aircraft that can nevertheless land on short and even unpaved runways. The PC-24 flew for the first time in 2015. Customers on several continents have bought it. In this way a company from a small canton exports its aircraft to the whole world.

gewusst: The PC-6 Porter is known for being able to take off and land over very short distances.
Pilatus aircraft take off in Buochs, right next to the factory, for their first flights.

teile.einleitung: Lake Sarnen is a lake in the canton of Obwalden. At its northern end lies Sarnen, the main town of the canton. In summer it is popular for swimming, rowing and sailing.
wichtigste: Lake Sarnen is in the canton of Obwalden.
Sarnen, the main town, lies at the northern end.
Other municipalities on the lake are Sachseln and Giswil.
The lake is several kilometres long.
The Sarner Aa flows into the lake and out of it again.
In summer people swim, row and sail here.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Sarnen** lies in a valley between green hills and mountains. **Sarnen** is in the north, **Sachseln** on the eastern shore and **Giswil** in the south. The **Sarner Aa** flows into the lake from the south and leaves it again at Sarnen. The lake was formed after the last ice age, when the glacier retreated.

In summer Lake Sarnen is a popular place for day trips. There are **lido pools** and places for barbecues. A lot of **rowing** is done on the lake, because the calm water is ideal for it. Sailing boats and stand-up paddlers are out too. A passenger boat crosses the lake in summer.

**Sachseln** lies on the shore. This is where the grave of **Niklaus von Flüe** can be found, who is called Brother Klaus. He lived in the 15th century and is the patron saint of Switzerland. Many people therefore visit Sachseln and nearby Flüeli-Ranft.

The **Brünig railway** runs along the eastern shore of the lake. It links Lucerne with Interlaken by way of the Brünig Pass. From the train you have a lovely view of the lake. The main road also follows the shore.

gewusst: Brother Klaus was declared a saint in 1947.
Sachseln on Lake Sarnen is an important place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Oberegg is a district of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden. The special thing is that Oberegg is not connected to the rest of the canton. It lies somewhat further north, between Appenzell Ausserrhoden and the canton of St Gallen.
wichtigste: Oberegg belongs to the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.
Oberegg is an exclave, that is, a separated area.
It lies between Appenzell Ausserrhoden and the canton of St Gallen.
The separation goes back to the division of the land of Appenzell in 1597.
From Oberegg you can see into the Rhine valley and to Lake Constance.

abschnitte.text: An **exclave** is a part of a territory that lies apart from the main part. Anyone wanting to travel from the main town **Appenzell** to Oberegg has to pass through another canton. Oberegg therefore lies like a small island outside the rest of the cantonal territory. All around lie **Appenzell Ausserrhoden** and **St Gallen**.

abschnitte.titel: The division of the land in 1597
abschnitte.text: In the past, Inner and Ausserrhoden together formed the land of **Appenzell**. After the **Reformation**, the people there were of different denominations. In **1597**, the land was therefore divided into two parts. The **Catholic** areas went to Innerrhoden, the **Reformed** ones to Ausserrhoden. Because the inhabitants of Oberegg remained Catholic, Oberegg still belongs to Innerrhoden today.

Oberegg is a rural place with farms, hills and woods. From the heights, for example near **St. Anton**, you have a lovely view over the **Rhine valley** as far as **Lake Constance** and Austria. Oberegg forms a **district** of its own within the canton.

gewusst: By population, Appenzell Innerrhoden is the smallest canton in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Rütli is a meadow on Lake Uri in the canton of Uri. According to legend, men from Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swore here to help one another. That is why the Rütli is regarded as the symbolic birthplace of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Rütli lies on Lake Uri, a part of Lake Lucerne.
It belongs to the municipality of Seelisberg in the canton of Uri.
According to legend, the Rütli Oath took place here.
Representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are said to have taken part.
The Rütli belongs to the Confederation.
On 1 August, celebrations for the national holiday take place there.

abschnitte.text: The legend tells that three men met secretly on the Rütli: **Walter Fürst** from Uri, **Werner Stauffacher** from Schwyz and **Arnold von Melchtal** from Unterwalden. They swore to defend themselves together against unjust bailiffs. This story was written down later, among other places in the **White Book of Sarnen**. Whether the meeting really took place like this is not known for certain.

What is certainly documented is the **Federal Charter of 1291**, an alliance between Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. But the Federal Charter does not mention the Rütli. The story of the Rütli Oath combines legend and reality. The poet **Friedrich Schiller** made it world famous in his play “William Tell”.

In the 19th century a hotel was to be built on the Rütli. The Swiss Society for the Public Good bought the meadow in 1859 and then gave it to the **Confederation**. So today the Rütli belongs to all the Swiss. It is meant to remain a simple, quiet place.

The best way to reach the Rütli is by **boat**, for example from Brunnen or Flüelen. You can also walk down from Seelisberg. On the shore, the **Swiss Path** also begins, a footpath around Lake Uri. On 1 August, celebrations take place on the meadow.

gewusst: In 1940, General Henri Guisan gathered the army's officers on the Rütli; this meeting is called the Rütli Report.
The name Rütli comes from “roden” (to clear): it refers to an area where forest was once cleared.

teile.einleitung: Lausanne in the canton of Vaud is the only Swiss city with a real metro. There are two lines, the m1 and the m2. The m2 climbs steeply up the slope from Lake Geneva.
wichtigste: Lausanne has two metro lines: the m1 and the m2.
The m1 opened in 1991.
The m2 has run since 2008.
The m2 runs without a driver, fully automatically.
It links Ouchy on Lake Geneva with Épalinges above the city.
In doing so the m2 climbs over 300 metres.
Lausanne is regarded as one of the smallest cities in the world with a metro.

abschnitte.text: The **m1** has run since 1991 from the centre, Lausanne-Flon, to the university and on to **Renens**. It mostly runs at surface level and is more like a modern light railway. The **m2** opened in 2008. It runs mostly underground and is a real **underground railway**. The two lines meet at Flon station.

Lausanne is built on a steep slope. That is why the **m2** is something special: it runs from the lakeside at **Ouchy** to **Épalinges** and climbs over 300 metres on the way. In some places the line is so steep that it is among the steepest metro lines in the world. So that the trains do not slip, they run on **rubber tyres**.

The trains of the m2 run **fully automatically**, that is, without a driver. A computer controls everything from a control centre. At the stations, glass doors on the platform protect the passengers. The trains run at short intervals, so you almost never have to wait long.

As early as the 19th century, a railway ran between Ouchy and Lausanne station that was called the **Ficelle**, in English “string”. It was a rack-and-funicular railway. For the building of the m2, its route was rebuilt and extended. For the future a third line, the **m3**, is planned.

gewusst: On its route the m2 climbs about as much height as the Eiffel Tower is tall.

teile.einleitung: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is a long railway tunnel through the Bernese Alps. It opened in 2007 and links Frutigen in the canton of Bern with Raron in Valais.
wichtigste: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 34 kilometres long.
It opened in 2007.
It runs from Frutigen in the canton of Bern to Raron in Valais.
It is part of NEAT, the New Rail Link through the Alps.
Thanks to it, the journey from Bern to Valais has become much shorter.
It is double-track on only part of its length.
Beside it there is also the old Lötschberg Tunnel of 1913.

abschnitte.text: A **base tunnel** runs deep down through the mountain, almost at the level of the valleys. This means trains do not have to climb steep ramps. The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about **34 kilometres** long. It begins at **Frutigen** in the Bernese Oberland and ends at **Raron** in Valais. Passenger trains run through it at high speed.

The tunnel is part of **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps. This also includes the Gotthard Base Tunnel and the Ceneri Base Tunnel. NEAT is intended to move more **goods from road to rail**. Lorries are meant to load their cargo onto trains so that the Alps have less traffic and fewer exhaust fumes. The Swiss people approved the building in a vote.

Before the base tunnel, trains ran on the winding **mountain route** through the old Lötschberg Tunnel. With the new tunnel, the journey from Bern to Visp and Brig became much shorter. Since then many people have commuted between Valais and Bern. Because the tunnel is only partly **double-track**, trains have to wait for each other at some points.

Inside the mountain it is warm. That is why **warm mountain water** flows out of the tunnel. In Frutigen, the **Tropenhaus** (tropical house) uses this water. Tropical plants grow there, and fish, sturgeon, are farmed. The old **Lötschberg Tunnel** between Kandersteg and Goppenstein is still in operation, among other things for the car-loading trains.

gewusst: The warm water from the tunnel has to be cooled before it may flow into the Kander, so that the fish in the river come to no harm.

teile.einleitung: Lausanne Cathedral is one of the most important Gothic churches in Switzerland. Particularly well known is the “Guet”, a night watchman who still calls out the hours from the tower every night.
wichtigste: Notre-Dame Cathedral stands high above the old town of Lausanne.
It was built in the Middle Ages in the Gothic style and consecrated in 1275.
Since the Reformation it has been a Reformed church.
The “Guet” calls out the hours from the tower every night.
This tradition has existed for centuries.
The large rose window is also famous.

abschnitte.text: **Notre-Dame Cathedral** stands on a hill above the old town of **Lausanne** in the canton of Vaud. It was built in the Middle Ages in the **Gothic style**. In 1275 it was solemnly consecrated, in the presence of the Pope and King Rudolf of Habsburg. It is regarded as one of the most important Gothic churches in Switzerland. In the 16th century it became Reformed with the **Reformation**.

The **Guet** is a night watchman. In the past he watched over the city and raised the alarm if a **fire** broke out somewhere. For centuries he has called out from the tower in every direction at every full hour during the night: “C'est le guet, il a sonné l'heure”, in English roughly “This is the watchman, the hour has struck”. The fire watch is no longer needed today. But the tradition lives on, night after night.

The large **rose window** from the 13th century is famous. It is a round window made of many pieces of coloured glass. It shows the world as people imagined it in the Middle Ages: with seasons, months and signs of the zodiac. There is also a beautifully painted **portal** with stone figures. The cathedral also has a large, modern organ.

gewusst: Lausanne is one of the few cities in Europe where a night watchman still calls out the hours every night.
You can climb the cathedral tower and look far out over Lake Geneva.

teile.einleitung: At the Riburg saltworks near Möhlin in the canton of Aargau, salt is produced. The salt lies deep under the ground. It is dissolved with water, pumped up and processed into table salt and road salt.
wichtigste: The Riburg saltworks lies in Möhlin in the canton of Aargau, close to the Rhine.
Salt is extracted there from the underground.
The salt comes from a sea that lay here a very long time ago.
Water is pumped down, and the salt dissolves in it.
The salty brine is pumped up and evaporated.
The saltworks belongs to the Swiss Saltworks (Schweizer Salinen).

abschnitte.text: About 200 million years ago there was a **shallow sea** here. When the water evaporated, the salt stayed behind and formed thick layers. Later these layers were covered by rock. Today the salt lies deep under the ground, in the area of the Riburg saltworks several hundred metres down.

Holes are drilled down to the salt layer and **water** is pumped down. The salt dissolves in the water, which produces **brine**, that is, very salty water. The brine is pumped back up. In the saltworks the water is evaporated until only the white salt crystals are left.

abschnitte.titel: What the salt is used for
abschnitte.text: Part of it becomes **table salt** for the kitchen. A large part is spread in winter as **road salt** on roads so that they do not freeze. Salt is also needed in industry, for example to make chemicals. There is also salt for animals, for example as a salt lick.

In Riburg there are huge round **salt stores** with a domed roof, the Saldome. A lot of road salt can be stored there for the winter. In this way Switzerland is well supplied even when there is a lot of snow. Other saltworks of the Swiss Saltworks lie in Schweizerhalle in the canton of Basel-Landschaft and in Bex in the canton of Vaud.

gewusst: Switzerland can cover almost all of its salt needs from its own saltworks.
The Riburg saltworks was founded in the 19th century, shortly after salt was discovered in the ground by the Rhine.

teile.einleitung: Madonna del Sasso is a famous pilgrimage church in Ticino. It stands on a rock high above Locarno and can be seen from far away.
wichtigste: Madonna del Sasso is a pilgrimage church above Locarno.
It stands on a rock in the municipality of Orselina.
“Sasso” is Italian and means rock.
The history of the place goes back to the 15th century.
You can reach the church on foot or by funicular.
From the top you can see far over Lake Maggiore.

abschnitte.text: The name **Madonna del Sasso** means “Mother of God of the Rock”. The church and monastery stand on a steep rocky outcrop above **Locarno**. The yellow buildings shine far across the town and the lake. A **pilgrimage church** is a church to which the faithful make a pilgrimage, that is, a special journey, to pray there.

According to an old tradition, in the **15th century** a monk had a vision of Mary on this rock. A first **chapel** was then built there. Over time, a church, a monastery and chapels were added. Valuable paintings hang in the church. Today Capuchin monks look after the place.

From Locarno a steep **footpath** with many steps leads up to the church. Small chapels stand along the way. More comfortable is the **funicular**, which runs from the town to Orselina. At the top you have a wonderful view over Locarno, the Maggia delta and **Lake Maggiore**.

gewusst: Madonna del Sasso is the landmark of Locarno and appears in many photos of the town.

teile.einleitung: The Laufental is a valley on the river Birs in the north-west of Switzerland. It belonged to the canton of Bern for a long time and in 1994, after popular votes, moved to the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
wichtigste: The Laufental lies on the Birs in the Jura.
Its main town is the town of Laufen.
From 1815 to 1993 it belonged to the canton of Bern.
On 1 January 1994 it moved to the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
German is spoken in the Laufental.

abschnitte.text: The **Laufental** lies in the **Jura** between Delémont and Basel. The **Birs** flows through the valley. The main town is the small town of **Laufen** with a small old town. Unlike in the nearby canton of Jura, **German** is spoken in the Laufental.

In the past the Laufental belonged to the **Prince-Bishopric of Basel**. After the time of Napoleon, in **1815**, it was assigned to the canton of **Bern**, together with the rest of the Jura. When the canton of Jura came into being in the 1970s, the Laufental stayed with Bern. But it now lay apart from the rest of the canton's territory.

The people of the Laufental were allowed to decide for themselves which canton they wanted to belong to. In a first vote in **1983**, they narrowly decided to stay with Bern. Later it emerged that the Bernese government had illegally supported the campaign with money. The **Federal Supreme Court** therefore ordered a new vote.

In the new vote in **1989**, a majority said yes to a move to **Basel-Landschaft**. After that, the voters of the two cantons and of the whole of Switzerland also had to agree. On **1 January 1994**, the Laufental finally belonged to the canton of Basel-Landschaft. There it now forms a district of its own.

gewusst: In Switzerland, a change of canton also requires a vote across the whole country.
In Laufen there is a well-known ceramics factory, for example for washbasins.

teile.einleitung: Rumantsch Grischun is the common written language of the Romansh people. It was created in 1982 so that all the valleys would have a uniform way of writing. But people still speak the various regional forms.
wichtigste: Romansh is one of the four national languages of Switzerland.
It is spoken mainly in the canton of the Grisons.
There are five regional written forms, called idioms.
Rumantsch Grischun was created in 1982 as a common written language.
The Confederation and the canton of the Grisons use Rumantsch Grischun for texts addressed to all Romansh speakers.
In everyday life people mostly speak their own idiom.

abschnitte.text: Romansh developed differently in the valleys of the Grisons. That is why there are five **idioms**: Sursilvan, Sutsilvan, Surmiran, Puter and Vallader. Each has its own words and its own spelling. Someone who speaks Sursilvan usually understands Vallader, but not always easily.

The **Lia Rumantscha**, the umbrella organisation of the Romansh, wanted a common written language. It commissioned the linguist **Heinrich Schmid**. In 1982 he created Rumantsch Grischun by choosing the most common forms from the large idioms. In this way a text would only have to be written once for all regions.

Since 1996, Romansh has been an **official language** of the Confederation in dealings with Romansh-speaking people. For this the Confederation uses Rumantsch Grischun, for example in voting materials or laws. The canton of the Grisons also uses it. Newspapers, radio and television use partly Rumantsch Grischun and partly the idioms.

In some municipalities Rumantsch Grischun was also introduced in **school**. Not everyone liked that. Supporters say a common written language strengthens Romansh. Others want children to learn to read and write their own idiom. That is why many municipalities have returned to their idiom.

gewusst: Romansh has been a national language of Switzerland since 1938; the people voted on it at the time.
“Grischun” is the Romansh word for the Grisons.

teile.einleitung: The Linth is the most important river in the canton of Glarus. It rises in the mountains in the south of the canton, flows through the whole of the Glarus region and then into Lake Walen.
wichtigste: The Linth rises in the south of the canton of Glarus, in the area of the Tödi.
It flows from south to north through the Glarus region.
It flows past places such as Linthal, Schwanden and Glarus.
Since the building of the Linth Canal, it has flowed into Lake Walen.
From Lake Walen, the Linth Canal leads on to Lake Zurich.
After Lake Zurich the river is called the Limmat.

abschnitte.titel: A source in the Glarus Alps
abschnitte.text: The Linth begins high up in the **Glarus Alps**, at the foot of the Tödi, the highest mountain in the region. Many streams from glaciers and snowfields flow into it. The water is therefore cold, and especially plentiful in spring when the snow melts. At Schwanden it is joined by the **Sernf**, which comes from the valley of Elm.

The valley of the Linth is narrow and surrounded by high mountains. Along the river lie the villages and the main town **Glarus**. In the past, many **factories** used the power of the water, for example for spinning mills and weaving mills. That is why Glarus was one of the first industrial cantons in Switzerland. Today power stations on the Linth produce electricity.

abschnitte.titel: From Lake Walen to Lake Zurich
abschnitte.text: In the past, the Linth flowed directly through the Linth plain to Lake Zurich and often burst its banks. At the beginning of the 19th century it was diverted by a canal into **Lake Walen**. From Lake Walen, the water flows on in the **Linth Canal** into **Lake Zurich**. Where it leaves Lake Zurich in Zurich, the river is called the **Limmat**.

gewusst: The Linth and the Limmat are really one river with two names: Linth above, Limmat below Lake Zurich.
A Glarus pumped-storage power station is named Linth-Limmern after the river.

teile.einleitung: Lausanne is the main town of the canton of Vaud. The city lies on a steep slope on Lake Geneva and is known all over the world as the Olympic Capital.
wichtigste: Lausanne is the main town of the canton of Vaud.
The city lies on a steep slope on Lake Geneva.
Since 1915 the International Olympic Committee has had its seat in Lausanne.
The Federal Supreme Court, the highest court in Switzerland, is also in Lausanne.
French is spoken in Lausanne.

abschnitte.text: **Lausanne** lies on the northern shore of **Lake Geneva**, which in French is called Lac Léman. The city climbs steeply up the slope from the lake at **Ouchy**. Between the lowest and the highest point of the city there are several hundred metres. That is why there are many steps and steep streets.

To overcome the slope, Lausanne has a **metro**. The **m2** line links Ouchy on the lake with the upper districts of the city. It is regarded as one of the steepest metro lines in the world. The trains run without a driver, fully automatically.

Since **1915**, the **International Olympic Committee** has had its seat in Lausanne. That is why the city is also called the **Olympic Capital**. On the lakeside stands the **Olympic Museum**, which shows the history of the Olympic Games. Many international sports federations also have their offices in Lausanne.

Above the old town stands the **cathedral**, a large church in the Gothic style. From its tower a **watchman** still calls out the hours every night, a custom from the Middle Ages. The **Federal Supreme Court**, the highest court in Switzerland, is also in Lausanne. There is also a university and the federal institute of technology **EPFL**.

gewusst: The cathedral's night watchman calls out “C'est le guet, il a sonné l'heure” every hour from 10 pm to 2 am.
In 2020 Lausanne hosted the Winter Youth Olympic Games.

teile.einleitung: The **Rigi** is a mountain in central Switzerland that is often called the “**Queen of the Mountains**”. It lies between Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz. Its summit, **Rigi Kulm**, belongs to the canton of Schwyz.
wichtigste: The Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”.
It lies between Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz.
It belongs partly to the canton of Schwyz and partly to the canton of Lucerne.
Its summit, Rigi Kulm, is just under 1,800 metres high.
The Vitznau-Rigi Railway of 1871 is the first mountain railway in Europe.
As early as the 19th century, many guests came to see the sunrise.

abschnitte.text: The Rigi is not particularly high: its summit, **Rigi Kulm**, lies at just under 1,800 metres. But because it stands free between three lakes, you have a huge view from the top. You can see many lakes, the Central Plateau and a long chain of Alpine peaks. That is why it is called the “**Queen of the Mountains**”. Incidentally, in German you say “die Rigi”, not “der Rigi”.

The Rigi lies between **Lake Lucerne**, **Lake Zug** and **Lake Lauerz**. One part of the mountain belongs to the canton of **Lucerne**, another to the canton of **Schwyz**. The summit, Rigi Kulm, lies on Schwyz territory. At the foot of the mountain lie places such as **Vitznau**, **Weggis** and **Arth-Goldau**. On the Rigi itself there are hamlets such as Rigi Kaltbad and Rigi Klösterli.

abschnitte.titel: The first mountain railway in Europe
abschnitte.text: In **1871**, the **Vitznau-Rigi Railway** opened. It was the **first mountain railway in Europe** and a rack railway. A few years later the **Arth-Rigi Railway** was added from the other side. Today a **cable car** also runs from Weggis to Rigi Kaltbad. On special days, old steam locomotives still run up the mountain.

abschnitte.titel: Guests from all over the world
abschnitte.text: As early as the 19th century, many tourists travelled to the Rigi. It was especially popular to spend the night at the top and to see the **sunrise** early in the morning. The American writer **Mark Twain** also wrote about his visit to the Rigi. Today you can walk here, and in winter go sledging and skiing. The Rigi is still one of the most popular destinations for outings in Switzerland.

gewusst: The Vitznau-Rigi Railway of 1871 was the first mountain railway in Europe.
In German people say “die Rigi”, because the mountain is seen as a “queen”.

teile.einleitung: The La Tène period is the later Iron Age of the Celts. It is named after the find site of La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel, where many Celtic objects have been found.
wichtigste: The La Tène period is the later Iron Age in central Europe.
It began around 450 BC and lasted until about the turn of the era.
It is named after the find site of La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel.
In the 19th century, many Celtic weapons and tools were found there.
The Helvetii lived in the area of present-day Switzerland at this time.

abschnitte.titel: A find site gives the name
abschnitte.text: At the eastern end of **Lake Neuchâtel** lies the place **La Tène**. In the **19th century**, many iron objects were found there in the shallow water: swords, spearheads, tools and jewellery. Later the water level dropped because of the Jura Water Correction, and even more was found. Researchers named a whole period after it.

After the Stone Age and the Bronze Age came the **Iron Age**. Iron is harder than bronze and is well suited to tools and weapons. The later Iron Age lasted from about **450 BC** until the time when the Romans conquered the area. This period is called the **La Tène period**.

In the La Tène period, the **Celts** lived in large parts of Europe. In the area of present-day Switzerland these were, for example, the **Helvetii**. The Celts were skilled craftspeople. They made decorated jewellery, struck **coins** and built fortified settlements called **oppida**.

Typical of this period is a special kind of decoration, the **La Tène style**. The Celts decorated objects with curving lines, spirals and tendrils. Such patterns can be found on sword scabbards, brooches and neck rings. Many finds from La Tène are now on display in the **Laténium** museum.

gewusst: A whole period of European history bears the name of a place in Switzerland.
Brooches (fibulae) were a kind of safety pin with which the Celts held their clothes together.

teile.einleitung: The Lorze is the most important river in the canton of Zug. It flows out of Lake Aegeri through a deep gorge into Lake Zug and leaves it again at Cham.
wichtigste: The Lorze flows through the canton of Zug.
It flows out of Lake Aegeri.
It flows towards Baar through the Lorzentobel, a deep gorge.
After that it flows into Lake Zug.
At Cham it leaves Lake Zug again.
In the end it flows into the Reuss.

abschnitte.titel: From Lake Aegeri into the valley
abschnitte.text: The Lorze leaves **Lake Aegeri** at Unterägeri. After that it flows through the **Lorzentobel**, a wild, wooded gorge. Here the river has cut deep into the rock. In the past, the power of the Lorze drove mills and factories, for example spinning mills. Today walking paths lead through the gorge.

At the edge of the Lorzentobel near Baar lie the **Höllgrotten caves**. These are stalactite caves that formed from **tufa**. Spring water rich in lime deposited lime there over a long time. In this way caves with stalactites and small lakes formed. You can visit them.

abschnitte.titel: Through Lake Zug to the Reuss
abschnitte.text: After Baar, the Lorze flows into **Lake Zug**. At **Cham** it leaves the lake again and flows on to the west. Finally it joins the **Reuss**. In this way its water reaches the North Sea via the Aare and the Rhine.

gewusst: The Lorze flows through two lakes: first out of Lake Aegeri, then through Lake Zug.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss National Museum in Zurich stands right next to Zurich main station. It shows the history of Switzerland from prehistoric times to the present, and its building looks like a castle.
wichtigste: The National Museum stands right next to Zurich main station.
It is part of the Swiss National Museum group.
It opened in 1898.
The building looks like a fairy-tale castle with towers.
In 2016 a modern new building was added.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss National Museum in Zurich** opened in **1898**. The architect **Gustav Gull** gave it towers, oriels and courtyards, so that it looks like a castle. He wanted to recall different building styles from Swiss history. The museum lies in a park between the main station and the rivers Sihl and Limmat.

In the museum you can see how people in Switzerland lived in the past. There are finds from the **Stone Age**, suits of armour, old furniture, traditional costumes and toys. A large exhibition tells the **history of Switzerland** from the Middle Ages to the present. There are also special exhibitions on particular themes again and again.

The National Museum in Zurich belongs to the **Swiss National Museum** group. This also includes the **Château de Prangins** in the canton of Vaud and the **Forum of Swiss History** in Schwyz. The Swiss National Museum is owned by the **Confederation** and collects objects that are important for the history of Switzerland.

In **2016** a large **new building** opened. It is made of concrete and has a modern shape, but with its windows and passages it fits in with the old castle. This gives the museum more space for exhibitions, a library and events.

gewusst: The National Museum belongs to the Confederation, that is, to the whole of Switzerland.
If you arrive in Zurich by train, you are in the museum in just a few steps.

teile.einleitung: Kreuzlingen is a town in the canton of Thurgau on Lake Constance. It borders directly on the German city of Konstanz, and the two towns have almost grown together.
wichtigste: Kreuzlingen lies in the canton of Thurgau on Lake Constance.
The town borders directly on Konstanz in Germany.
You can walk from Switzerland to Germany.
The name comes from Kreuzlingen Abbey.
Kreuzlingen is one of the largest towns in Thurgau.

abschnitte.text: Between **Kreuzlingen** and **Konstanz** runs the **national border** between Switzerland and Germany. The houses of the two towns stand close together. At several crossings you can cross the border on foot or by bicycle. Many people shop on the other side or work there.

The name Kreuzlingen is linked with **Kreuzlingen Abbey**. It was founded in the Middle Ages and owned a valuable cross as a relic. The abbey church from the Baroque period still stands today. Over time, the settlement that became the present town grew up around the monastery.

Kreuzlingen lies on the shore of **Lake Constance**. In the large **lakeside park**, many families walk and play. From the harbour, boats sail across the lake. Three countries border each other on Lake Constance: Switzerland, Germany and Austria.

Kreuzlingen is one of the largest towns in the canton of Thurgau. There are schools, museums and a university of teacher education. Because Konstanz is so close, the two towns are closely linked. People sometimes speak of a shared region across the border.

gewusst: Kreuzlingen and Konstanz lie so close together that some streets end right at the border.
Kreuzlingen is one of the few Swiss towns that has grown directly together with a foreign town.

teile.einleitung: Lugano is the largest city in the canton of Ticino. It lies on Lake Lugano, surrounded by mountains, and is an important centre for banking, tourism and culture in Italian-speaking Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lugano is the largest city in the canton of Ticino.
The capital of Ticino, however, is Bellinzona.
Lugano lies on Lake Lugano.
Beside the city stand the mountains Monte Brè and Monte San Salvatore.
Italian is spoken in Lugano.
Lugano is an important banking centre in Switzerland.
Since 1996 Lugano has had a university, the Università della Svizzera italiana.

abschnitte.text: Lugano lies in a bay of **Lake Lugano**, which in Italian is called Lago di Lugano or Ceresio. To the left and right of the city rise two mountains: **Monte Brè** and **Monte San Salvatore**. You can go up both by funicular. From the top you can see over the lake as far as Italy. The mild climate lets palm trees and camellias grow.

After Zurich and Geneva, Lugano is one of the largest **financial centres** in Switzerland. Many banks have offices here. **Tourism** is also important: guests come for the lake, the mountains and the southern flair. Many people commute to work in Lugano from Italy every day.

Since 2015 there has been the cultural centre **LAC**, short for Lugano Arte e Cultura, with a museum and concert hall right on the lake. Since 1996 the city has had a **university**, the Università della Svizzera italiana. In summer, concerts and festivals take place on the piazza. On the lakeshore lies the large **Parco Ciani** with old trees.

In recent decades, many municipalities around Lugano have **merged** with the city. As a result Lugano has become much larger and now reaches far into the surrounding valleys. The old town with its alleys, arcades and the **Piazza della Riforma** is the heart of the city. The cathedral of San Lorenzo lies on the slope above the centre.

gewusst: Lugano is the largest city in Switzerland in which Italian is spoken.
Very close by, in Melide, the Swissminiatur park shows Switzerland in miniature.

teile.einleitung: Lake Neuchâtel is a large lake in the west of Switzerland at the foot of the Jura. It is the largest lake lying entirely on Swiss soil. On its shore lie the towns of Neuchâtel and Yverdon-les-Bains.
wichtigste: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland.
Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but lie partly abroad.
The lake is about 38 kilometres long.
It borders the cantons of Neuchâtel, Vaud, Fribourg and Bern.
On the south shore lies the Grande Cariçaie, a large protected area.
Together with Lake Biel and Lake Murten, it forms the Three Lakes Region.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Neuchâtel** has an area of about 218 square kilometres. This makes it the **largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland**. Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but they belong partly to France, Germany and Austria. Lake Neuchâtel is long and narrow, about 38 kilometres in length.

On the north shore lies the city of **Neuchâtel**, and at the southern end the town of **Yverdon-les-Bains**, which is known for its warm thermal baths. On the shore there is also the little town of **Estavayer-le-Lac** and many small villages. In fine weather you can see across the lake as far as the **Alps**.

On the **south shore** lies the **Grande Cariçaie**. This is a long area of reeds, marsh and woodland. It is regarded as the largest lakeshore wetland in Switzerland. Many **birds**, frogs and rare plants live here. That is why the Grande Cariçaie is under **nature protection**.

Lake Neuchâtel is linked with **Lake Murten** and **Lake Biel** by canals. Together they form the **Three Lakes Region**. During the **Jura Water Correction**, the water level was lowered. In the process, remains of old **pile dwellings** came to light on the shore, which are now part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

gewusst: Traces of settlements several thousand years old have been found on Lake Neuchâtel.
The Grande Cariçaie on the south shore is the largest lakeshore wetland in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The **Reichenbach Falls** are a waterfall near **Meiringen** in the Bernese Oberland. They became world famous because the writer **Arthur Conan Doyle** set a story about the detective **Sherlock Holmes** here. In Meiringen there is therefore even a Sherlock Holmes museum.
wichtigste: The Reichenbach Falls lie near Meiringen in the canton of Bern.
Here the Reichenbach plunges down into the Haslital valley.
Arthur Conan Doyle made the waterfall the setting of a Sherlock Holmes story.
An old funicular runs up to the waterfall.
In Meiringen there is a Sherlock Holmes museum and a statue of the detective.

abschnitte.text: The **Reichenbach** comes from the mountains above Meiringen. Shortly before the valley, it plunges in several steps into the depths and then flows into the **Aare**. The largest drop is the Reichenbach Falls proper. As early as the 19th century, many travellers came to see them. Painters captured the roaring water in their pictures.

The British writer **Arthur Conan Doyle** invented the detective **Sherlock Holmes**. In the story “**The Final Problem**”, Holmes fights his opponent **Professor Moriarty** at the Reichenbach Falls. Readers believed that Holmes had died there. Many were so sad that Doyle later brought him back in new stories. Since then the waterfall has been known to Holmes fans all over the world.

From Meiringen, the **Reichenbach Falls Funicular**, an old **funicular railway**, runs up to the waterfall. It has been in operation for over a hundred years. At the top there are viewpoints looking down on the plunging water. In the village stands a **statue of Sherlock Holmes**, and in an old church a **Sherlock Holmes Museum** has been set up. There even his sitting room from London has been recreated.

gewusst: At the Reichenbach Falls, a star marks the spot where Holmes and Moriarty are supposed to have fought in the story.
Meiringen is said to be the possible origin of the name of meringue, a pastry made of egg white and sugar.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Schaffhausen is the northernmost canton of Switzerland. It lies almost entirely north of the Rhine and is surrounded by Germany on almost all sides.
wichtigste: The main town is the city of Schaffhausen.
German is spoken, in everyday life mostly the Schaffhausen dialect.
The canton lies largely north of the Rhine.
It is almost entirely surrounded by Germany, and its only neighbouring cantons are Zurich and Thurgau.
It consists of three parts that are not connected.
Schaffhausen joined the Confederation in 1501.
The Rhine Falls are in Neuhausen.

abschnitte.text: Almost the whole canton lies on the **northern side of the Rhine**. In Switzerland this is unusual, because elsewhere the Rhine often forms the border. Schaffhausen is surrounded by **Germany** on almost all sides. Only in the south does it border the cantons of **Zurich** and **Thurgau**. It is the northernmost canton of Switzerland.

The canton consists of **three parts** that are not connected. The largest part lies around the city of Schaffhausen and the Klettgau. In the east lies the area around **Stein am Rhein**. In the south lies the area of **Rüdlingen** and **Buchberg**. In between lies German or Zurich territory.

The city of Schaffhausen began as a trading place on the Rhine. Because the Rhine Falls stopped the ships, goods had to be unloaded here. In **1501**, Schaffhausen became a member of the **Confederation**, in the same year as Basel. Above the city stands the **Munot**, a round fortress from the 16th century. Every evening the little Munot bell rings there.

In **Neuhausen am Rheinfall**, the Rhine plunges over rocks into the depths. The **Rhine Falls** are regarded as one of the largest waterfalls in Europe. In the **Klettgau**, many vines grow, from which wine is made. The old town of **Stein am Rhein** is famous for its painted houses.

gewusst: At the Rhine Falls you can go by boat to a rock in the middle of the waterfall.
Because of the many borders, on some excursions in the canton of Schaffhausen you can cross several times between Switzerland and Germany.

teile.einleitung: The Landsgemeinde of Glarus is one of the last two Landsgemeinden in Switzerland. Every year on the first Sunday in May, the citizens entitled to vote gather on the Zaunplatz in Glarus.
wichtigste: The Glarus Landsgemeinde takes place on the Zaunplatz in Glarus.
It is held on the first Sunday in May.
Voting is done by a show of hands.
Every citizen entitled to vote may speak at the speaker's podium.
In 2007, Glarus was the first canton to allow voting from the age of 16.

abschnitte.text: The Landsgemeinde takes place on the **Zaunplatz** in the main town of **Glarus**. The citizens entitled to vote stand in a large circle, the **Ring**. In the middle stands a platform for the Landammann and the speakers. All around, the mountains of the Glarus region can be seen.

A special feature of the Glarus Landsgemeinde is that **every citizen entitled to vote** may step up to the speaker's podium. You can speak for or against a proposal and even propose changes. So it can happen that a proposal is finally passed in a very different form from the one the government had planned.

At the Landsgemeinde of **2007**, the people of Glarus decided that you may vote from the age of **16**. Glarus was thus the **first canton** in Switzerland with this voting age. However, you can only stand for election to an office from the age of 18.

The Landsgemeinde has also decided on big changes. In **2006** it decided to merge the many small municipalities of the canton into just **three municipalities**: Glarus, Glarus Nord and Glarus Süd. This was one of the largest municipal reforms in Switzerland.

gewusst: Glarus has only three municipalities, fewer than almost any other canton.
Children may also watch the Glarus Landsgemeinde, and they often stand right at the edge of the Ring.

teile.einleitung: Jean Tinguely was a Swiss artist who was born in Fribourg in 1925. He became famous for machine sculptures that move, squeak and clatter.
wichtigste: Jean Tinguely was born in Fribourg in 1925 and grew up in Basel.
He built moving sculptures from metal, wheels and scrap.
His art is often called kinetic art, that is art with movement.
He was married to the artist Niki de Saint Phalle.
In Basel there is the Museum Tinguely.
He died in 1991.

abschnitte.text: Jean Tinguely was born in **Fribourg** in 1925. He grew up in **Basel**, where he did an apprenticeship as a window dresser. Later he moved to **Paris**, which was then an important city for art. There he found friends among artists who wanted to try out new things. Soon he became known all over the world.

Tinguely built **machine sculptures** from wheels, belts, motors and old pieces of metal. They turn, rattle, squeak and sometimes make completely pointless movements. With them he wanted to show that machines can also be playful and funny. This art is called **kinetic art**. In 1960 in New York, he even built a machine that destroyed itself.

Tinguely was married to the artist **Niki de Saint Phalle**. She was known for colourful, round figures. Together they created works, for example a fountain in Paris with colourful figures and moving machines. In Fribourg, the **Espace Jean Tinguely et Niki de Saint Phalle** recalls the two of them.

In Basel, Tinguely's **Carnival Fountain** stands in front of the theatre, where machines spray water in all directions. On the Rhine is the **Museum Tinguely**, which shows many of his works. In Zurich, his big machine “Heureka” stands on the lakeshore. Tinguely died in Bern in 1991.

gewusst: Many machines in the Museum Tinguely can be switched on yourself with a button.
Tinguely often used scrap and found objects for his works of art.

teile.einleitung: At **3,247 metres**, the **Ringelspitz** is the highest mountain in the canton of St Gallen. It lies on the border with the canton of the Grisons. Many people think first of the Säntis, but the Ringelspitz is clearly higher.
wichtigste: The Ringelspitz is 3,247 metres high.
It is the highest point of the canton of St Gallen.
It lies on the border between St Gallen and the Grisons.
The Säntis, at 2,502 metres, is much better known but lower.
The Ringelspitz belongs to the Glarus Alps.

abschnitte.text: The Ringelspitz lies in the south of the canton of St Gallen, above the **Tamina valley** near Vättis. The border with the **Grisons** runs over its summit. On the Grisons side lie places such as Tamins and Flims. The mountain belongs to the **Glarus Alps**. Its summit is surrounded by rock, snow and small glaciers.

The best-known mountain in the canton of St Gallen is the **Säntis**. It is 2,502 metres high and has a cable car and a weather station. But the highest point of the canton is the **Ringelspitz**, which is about 750 metres higher. It is less well known because it lies remote and no railway leads up it. Only experienced mountaineers reach the summit.

In the area of the Ringelspitz lies the **Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona**, which has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 2008. Here, on the rock walls, you can see how older layers of rock were pushed over younger ones when the Alps were formed. This knowledge helped researchers to understand how mountains are formed. That is why geologists from all over the world come to this area.

gewusst: The Ringelspitz is about 750 metres higher than the Säntis.
No railway leads up the Ringelspitz, and you can only reach it on foot.

teile.einleitung: The Museggmauer is an old town wall in Lucerne with nine towers. It was built in the Middle Ages to protect the city and is still well preserved today. In the Zytturm hangs the oldest tower clock in the city.
wichtigste: The Museggmauer stands on the northern edge of Lucerne's old town.
It was built in the 14th century.
Nine towers belong to the wall.
Some towers can be climbed in summer.
The clock in the Zytturm is the oldest tower clock in Lucerne.
It is allowed to strike one minute before all the other clocks in the city.

abschnitte.text: In the Middle Ages, cities had to protect themselves against attackers. That is why Lucerne built the **Museggmauer** in the **14th century**. It runs along a hill above the old town. Together with the lake and the Reuss, it formed a protective ring around the city. The wall is about 870 metres long.

Nine **towers** belong to the Museggmauer. Each has a name of its own, for example **Männliturm**, **Wachtturm**, **Zytturm** or **Schirmerturm**. Some of the towers are open in summer. You can climb up and have a wonderful view of Lucerne, Lake Lucerne and the mountains.

In the **Zytturm** hangs a clock from the year **1535**. It is the oldest tower clock in the city. That is why it has a special right: it may strike **one minute earlier** than all the other clocks in Lucerne. On the large dial you can read the time from far away.

Today the Museggmauer is a popular destination for families and tourists. Part of the wall has a **wall walk** that you can walk along. From there you can also see the **Chapel Bridge** and the old town. The Museggmauer is one of the best-preserved town walls in Switzerland.

gewusst: Zytturm is simply Swiss German for time tower, that is, clock tower.
The Museggmauer is one of the best-known landmarks of Lucerne, together with the Chapel Bridge.

teile.einleitung: **Rorschach** is a small town in the canton of St Gallen on the shore of **Lake Constance**. It has a harbour and a historic granary. Through Rorschach, the canton of St Gallen has a share of Lake Constance.
wichtigste: Rorschach lies on Lake Constance in the canton of St Gallen.
The town has a very small area.
At the harbour stands the Baroque granary from the 18th century.
In the past Rorschach was an important place for the grain trade.
In the former Mariaberg Abbey there is now a university of teacher education.
A rack railway runs from Rorschach to Heiden.

abschnitte.text: Rorschach lies on the southern shore of **Lake Constance** between the Rorschacherberg and the lake. The municipality has only a very small **area** and is densely built up. On the shore there is a long promenade, a **harbour** for scheduled boats and other boats, and an old **bathing house** that stands on piles in the lake. The canton of St Gallen has a share of Lake Constance in the north at Rorschach and Goldach.

Right on the harbour stands the large **granary** (Kornhaus). It was built in the **18th century** on behalf of the Abbey of St Gallen. **Grain** that came by ship across Lake Constance, mainly from southern Germany, was stored here. Rorschach was therefore for a long time an important **trading place**. The granary is today one of the landmarks of the town.

Above the old town stands the former **Mariaberg Abbey**. This building also goes back to the Abbey of St Gallen. Today part of the **St Gallen University of Teacher Education** is housed in it. Teachers are trained there. With its beautiful cloister, the building is a special architectural monument.

From Rorschach, the **Rorschach-Heiden Railway** climbs up to Heiden in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. It is a **rack railway** and overcomes a large difference in height. From the top you have a lovely view of Lake Constance. Rorschach is also a railway junction on the line between St Gallen and the Rhine valley.

gewusst: Rorschach is among the Swiss municipalities with the smallest area.
In the past, the grain in the granary came by ship across Lake Constance.

teile.einleitung: The Museum zu Allerheiligen is a large museum in the town of Schaffhausen. It is housed in the buildings of a former monastery from the Middle Ages. There you can see art, history, archaeology and nature under one roof.
wichtigste: Allerheiligen Abbey was founded in the 11th century.
It was a Benedictine monastery.
In the Reformation the monastery was dissolved.
Today the buildings house the Museum zu Allerheiligen.
The museum shows art, history, archaeology and nature.
A large cloister and the Minster belong to the monastery.

abschnitte.text: **Allerheiligen** Abbey was founded in the **11th century** by a count. **Benedictine monks** lived here, who prayed, worked and copied books. The monastery was important for the development of the town of **Schaffhausen**. Next to it stands the **Minster**, a large Romanesque church of light-coloured stone.

In the **Reformation** in the 16th century, the monastery was dissolved. The buildings were then used for other purposes. In the 20th century, the town set up a **museum** in them. In this way the old rooms were preserved and given a new purpose.

The museum has several areas. In **archaeology** you can see finds from the Stone Age and Roman times. **History** shows how people in Schaffhausen lived in the past. There is also **art** from many centuries and an exhibition on the **nature** of the region.

A particularly beautiful place is the **cloister**. This is the name for a covered walkway around an inner courtyard in a monastery. An old bell known as the **Schiller Bell** also hangs there. Next to it lies a **herb garden** in which grow medicinal plants such as the monks used in the past.

gewusst: The Schiller Bell in the cloister is said to have inspired the poet Friedrich Schiller to write his famous poem “The Song of the Bell”.
The Museum zu Allerheiligen is one of the largest museums in eastern Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Jurassic is a period of Earth's history in which many dinosaurs lived. This period is named after the Jura mountains, because typical rocks from this time were found there.
wichtigste: The Jurassic is a period of Earth's history.
It began about 200 million years ago and lasted about 55 million years.
It lies between the Triassic and the Cretaceous.
It is named after the Jura mountains in Switzerland and France.
Many dinosaurs lived in this period.
Large parts of Europe were covered by shallow seas at that time.

abschnitte.text: Experts divide the long history of the Earth into **periods**. The **Jurassic** began about 200 million years ago and ended about 145 million years ago. Before it came the **Triassic**, and after it came the **Cretaceous**. Together, these three periods make up the Mesozoic Era. It is the age of the dinosaurs.

In the **Jura mountains** there are thick layers of limestone. Researchers found out that these layers come from a particular period of Earth's history. So they named this period after the mountains. Similar rocks from the same time can also be found in many other places in the world. This is how the name **Jurassic** became known worldwide.

In the Jurassic, many **dinosaurs** lived. Huge plant-eaters with long necks, the **sauropods**, ate leaves from tall trees. Brachiosaurus is one of them. Stegosaurus, with plates on its back, also lived then. Meat-eaters such as Allosaurus hunted on two legs. There were also already small mammals.

At that time the climate was warm, and shallow **seas** covered large parts of Europe. **Ammonites**, animals with coiled shells that are often found fossilised today, lived in them. Large marine reptiles such as ichthyosaurs also swam there. The **Archaeopteryx**, an early bird with feathers and teeth, also comes from the Jurassic. It was found in Germany.

gewusst: The film title “Jurassic Park” comes from the English word for the Jurassic.
Ammonites from the Jurassic can also be found in Switzerland, for example in the Jura.

teile.einleitung: At **3,402 metres**, the **Rheinwaldhorn** is the highest mountain in the canton of Ticino. In Italian it is called **Adula**. It lies on the border with the canton of the Grisons.
wichtigste: The Rheinwaldhorn is 3,402 metres high.
It is the highest point of the canton of Ticino.
In Italian the mountain is called Adula.
It lies on the border between Ticino and the Grisons.
On its north side the Posterior Rhine rises.

abschnitte.text: The Rheinwaldhorn lies in the **Adula Alps** between Ticino and the Grisons. On the Ticino side lies the **Blenio valley**, and on the Grisons side the **Rheinwald** and the Valser valley. At 3,402 metres, the mountain is the highest point of Ticino. The Italian name **Adula** is very old and gave its name to the whole mountain group. Glaciers lie around the summit.

On the north side of the Rheinwaldhorn lies the **Zapport Glacier**. From its meltwater the **Posterior Rhine** is formed, one of the two headwaters of the Rhine. It flows through the Rheinwald valley, which gave the mountain its German name. The water from the Rheinwaldhorn therefore flows via the Rhine to the North Sea. On the south side, by contrast, the water flows into Ticino and on to the Mediterranean.

The first person to climb the Rheinwaldhorn was the Benedictine monk **Placidus a Spescha** from Disentis Abbey, in **1789**. He was an enthusiastic mountaineer and naturalist and explored many peaks in the Grisons. Today the ascent is a demanding high-mountain tour over glaciers. For it you need experience and mountaineering equipment.

gewusst: From the Rheinwaldhorn, water flows both to the North Sea and to the Mediterranean.
The monk Placidus a Spescha is regarded as one of the first great mountaineers of the Grisons.

teile.einleitung: The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall on the border between the canton of Neuchâtel and France. Here the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. You can reach it, for example, by boat from Les Brenets.
wichtigste: The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall on the River Doubs.
It lies on the border between Switzerland and France.
On the Swiss side lies the canton of Neuchâtel.
The water falls about 27 metres.
Above the fall lies the Lac des Brenets.
Boats sail from Les Brenets to the waterfall.

abschnitte.text: “Saut” is French and means **leap**. At the Saut du Doubs the river leaps over a rocky edge and drops about **27 metres**. After a lot of rain or during the snowmelt, an especially large amount of water thunders down. In dry summers the waterfall sometimes almost disappears.

Above the fall the Doubs is dammed to form the **Lac des Brenets**, which in French is also called Lac de Chaillexon. Boats leave from the village of **Les Brenets** in the canton of Neuchâtel and cross the narrow lake. It lies between high rock walls. From the landing stage you can reach the waterfall on a short walk.

Here the **Doubs** forms the border between Switzerland and France. So you can visit the waterfall from both sides. There are viewpoints on the Swiss and on the French side. On the French side lies the municipality of Villers-le-Lac.

In very cold winters the Lac des Brenets can freeze over. Then you can even walk on the ice as far as the waterfall, if the authorities allow it. Sometimes large **icicles** hang from the waterfall. That is a rare and impressive sight.

gewusst: The Lac des Brenets was formed because, a long time ago, a rockfall dammed the Doubs.
The Doubs flows mostly through France, where it joins the Saône.

teile.einleitung: The **Reuss** is one of the great rivers of Switzerland. It rises in the **Gotthard area**, flows through the canton of Uri and **Lake Lucerne** and leaves it in **Lucerne**. In the canton of Aargau it finally joins the **Aare**.
wichtigste: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area.
It flows through the whole Uri Reuss valley into Lake Uri.
In Lucerne it flows out of Lake Lucerne.
The Chapel Bridge and the Spreuer Bridge cross the Reuss in Lucerne.
In the canton of Aargau the Reuss joins the Aare.
The Reuss is about 160 kilometres long.

abschnitte.text: The Reuss begins in the mountains around the **Gotthard** and the **Furka**. Several headwater streams join in the **Urseren valley** at Andermatt. After that the Reuss plunges through the wild **Schöllenen Gorge**. There the famous **Devil's Bridge** crosses the river, and a well-known legend surrounds it. The Schöllenen was for a long time a difficult obstacle on the way over the Gotthard.

After the Schöllenen, the Reuss flows north through the **Uri Reuss valley**. It passes places such as Wassen, Amsteg and Erstfeld. In the valley also run the Gotthard road, the motorway and the railway line. At Flüelen and Seedorf, the Reuss flows into **Lake Uri**, the southernmost part of Lake Lucerne. In this way it crosses almost the whole canton of Uri.

In **Lucerne**, the Reuss leaves **Lake Lucerne**. In the middle of the city, the **Chapel Bridge** with its water tower crosses the river, one of the oldest wooden bridges in Europe.
