A little further downstream stands the **Spreuer Bridge**. With the **Nadelwehr** (needle weir), you can regulate how much water flows out of the lake. In this way the water level of Lake Lucerne is also controlled.

Beyond Lucerne, the Reuss flows through the **Freiamt** into the canton of **Aargau**. It passes the old town of **Bremgarten**. Near **Brugg** it joins the **Aare**. There the Aare, Reuss and Limmat also meet in a small space, and the area is called the **Wasserschloss (“water castle”) of Switzerland**. The water of the Reuss finally reaches the North Sea via the Aare and the Rhine.

gewusst: Near the mouth of the Reuss, the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet, and the area is called the “Wasserschloss of Switzerland”.
The Chapel Bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne is one of the best-known structures in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Jungfraujoch is a mountain saddle between the peaks of the Jungfrau and the Mönch. At 3,454 metres above sea level, the highest railway station in Europe lies here, on the border between the cantons of Bern and Valais.
wichtigste: The Jungfraujoch station lies at 3,454 metres above sea level.
It is the highest railway station in Europe.
The Jungfrau Railway runs up from Kleine Scheidegg.
Most of the route goes through a tunnel inside the Eiger and the Mönch.
The railway opened in 1912.
From the Jungfraujoch you can see the Great Aletsch Glacier.

abschnitte.text: The **Jungfrau Railway** begins at **Kleine Scheidegg**. After a short ride, the train disappears into a long **tunnel** that runs through the **Eiger** and the **Mönch**. On the way there are stops where you can look out through windows in the rock. Building the line took many years and was very difficult. In 1912 the railway finally reached the Jungfraujoch.

abschnitte.titel: Between the Jungfrau and the Mönch
abschnitte.text: A **joch** (saddle) is a lower point between two mountain peaks. The Jungfraujoch lies between the **Jungfrau** and the **Mönch**. The border between the cantons of Bern and Valais runs here. The air is thin, so you get tired easily when walking fast. There is snow and ice almost all year round.

From the Jungfraujoch you look out over the **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the largest glacier in the Alps. It is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch. In the **Ice Palace** you can walk through passages dug into the glacier ice. Figures made of ice stand inside.

On a rock above the station stands the **Sphinx**, a viewing platform with a research station. There, experts measure the air and the weather, for example. Because the station is so high up, the air is very clean. In clear weather you can see from here as far as the Black Forest and France.

gewusst: The Jungfraujoch is also called the “Top of Europe”.
The train takes about half an hour to travel through the tunnel.

teile.einleitung: **Rapperswil-Jona** is, after the city of St Gallen, the **second largest municipality** in the canton of St Gallen. It came into being in **2007**, when Rapperswil and Jona merged. The municipality lies on Lake Zurich and the Obersee.
wichtigste: Rapperswil-Jona is the second largest municipality in the canton of St Gallen.
Rapperswil and Jona merged in 2007.
The municipality lies on Lake Zurich and the Obersee.
The municipality also includes places such as Kempraten, Wagen and Bollingen.
In Kempraten there was already a settlement in Roman times.
The Rapperswil-Jona Lakers play ice hockey in the top league.

abschnitte.text: Rapperswil was for a long time a small town with little land, while Jona was a large municipality around the town. The two places had long since grown together. On **1 January 2007** they merged into the new municipality of **Rapperswil-Jona**. Since then it has been, after the city of St Gallen, the second largest municipality in the canton. Such **municipal mergers** happen again and again in Switzerland.

The municipality lies at the eastern end of **Lake Zurich** and on the **Obersee**, which are separated by the Seedamm. Through Jona flows the small river **Jona**, after which the place is named. There are bathing spots, harbours and walking paths on the shore. Inland, green hills rise. In this way the municipality combines town, lake and countryside.

In the district of **Kempraten** there was already a settlement in **Roman times**. Archaeologists have found remains of houses and objects there. In **Bollingen** on the Obersee lies **Wurmsbach** Abbey, where nuns live. Also in Bollingen, the well-known psychologist **C. G. Jung** built a tower as a retreat. The old town of Rapperswil with the castle dates from the Middle Ages.

The municipality is also known for its ice hockey club, the **SC Rapperswil-Jona Lakers**. They play in the **National League**, the top Swiss league. **Circus Knie** also has its home in Rapperswil. From here you can travel by boat to Zurich and to the island of Ufenau. Many people from the region come to the lake for a walk.

gewusst: The municipality bears two names because it was formed from two former municipalities.
Even some 2,000 years ago, people lived in Kempraten in a Roman settlement.

teile.einleitung: Liechtenstein is a small country between Switzerland and Austria. It is a principality and lies right next to the canton of St Gallen, on the other side of the Rhine.
wichtigste: Liechtenstein is a principality with a prince as head of state.
The capital is called Vaduz.
The country borders Switzerland and Austria.
The Rhine forms the border with the canton of St Gallen.
In the south, Liechtenstein borders the canton of the Grisons.
In Liechtenstein people pay with the Swiss franc.
The national language is German.

abschnitte.text: Liechtenstein is a **constitutional monarchy**. This means that there is a prince, but also a constitution, an elected parliament, the **Landtag**, and a government. As in Switzerland, the people can take part in votes. Above the capital **Vaduz** stands the castle where the princely family lives. The country consists of eleven municipalities.

Liechtenstein is about 160 square kilometres in area and is one of the smallest countries in the world. In the west lies the flat **Rhine valley**, and in the east the mountains rise. The highest mountain is the Grauspitz on the border with the Grisons. Liechtenstein has no access to the sea, and neither do its two neighbouring countries. Elsewhere this is only the case for Uzbekistan.

Since 1923, Liechtenstein and Switzerland have formed a **customs union**. That is why there are no customs checks at the border, and people pay with the **Swiss franc**. Many people live in one country and work in the other. Liechtenstein does not belong to the European Union but is a member of the European Economic Area.

In the past, people in Liechtenstein lived mainly from farming. Today there are many **industrial firms**, for example for tools, machinery and dental products. Banks and insurance companies are also important. Because there are so many jobs, many people commute to Liechtenstein every day from Switzerland and Austria.

gewusst: Liechtenstein has no army of its own.
Liechtenstein is one of only two countries in the world that are entirely surrounded by landlocked countries.

teile.einleitung: Einsiedeln Abbey in the canton of Schwyz is one of the best-known monasteries in Switzerland. Benedictine monks live here, and every year many pilgrims come.
wichtigste: Einsiedeln Abbey lies in the canton of Schwyz.
It is a Benedictine monastery and over 1,000 years old.
It was founded in the year 934.
In the Chapel of Grace stands the famous Black Madonna.
The large abbey church is built in the Baroque style.

abschnitte.text: In the 9th century, a hermit named **Meinrad** lived in the “dark forest”. He lived alone in a small cell and prayed. After his death, other devout men came to this place. In the year **934**, a **Benedictine monastery** was founded there. The name Einsiedeln recalls the hermit Meinrad (in German, an Einsiedler).

The present abbey church was built in the **18th century** in the **Baroque** style. Inside it is richly decorated with gold, paintings and figures. In front of the church lies a large square with a fountain. You can see the mighty complex with its two towers from far away.

In the church stands the **Chapel of Grace**. In it is a figure of Mary with a dark face, the **Black Madonna**. It is the destination of many pilgrims. Einsiedeln is also an important stop on the **Way of St James**, which leads all the way to Santiago de Compostela in Spain.

The monks live by the **Rule of Saint Benedict**: prayer and work. The monastery includes a school, a large library and a stable for horses. For centuries, horses have been bred in the monastery stable, the Einsiedeln horses. There are also workshops and farming.

gewusst: The horse breeding of Einsiedeln Abbey is regarded as one of the oldest in Europe.
Einsiedeln is one of the most important places of pilgrimage in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: **Pilatus** is the local mountain of **Lucerne**. It lies on the border of the cantons of Lucerne, Obwalden and Nidwalden. Many legends, above all about **dragons**, surround the rugged mountain.
wichtigste: Pilatus is the local mountain of the city of Lucerne.
It lies in the cantons of Lucerne, Obwalden and Nidwalden.
Its highest peak is the Tomlishorn at 2,128 metres.
Many legends tell of dragons that are said to have lived on Pilatus.
The steepest rack railway in the world runs up from Alpnachstad.
From Kriens you can reach the mountain by gondola and cable car.

abschnitte.text: Pilatus stands south-west of Lucerne right on **Lake Lucerne**. Its highest peak is the **Tomlishorn** at 2,128 metres. At the top, on **Pilatus Kulm**, there are hotels, restaurants and viewing platforms. In clear weather you can see many lakes and the chain of the Alps. **Ibex** also live on Pilatus, and with a little luck you can see them.

In the past, many people believed that **dragons** lived in the caves of Pilatus. A well-known legend tells that in 1421 a dragon flew over the mountain and dropped a stone. This **dragon stone** is now in the Natur-Museum Luzern. Another legend tells of a man who fell into a dragon cave and spent the winter with the dragons. That is why the dragon is still a symbol of Pilatus today.

An old legend tells that the ghost of **Pontius Pilate** rests in a small lake on the mountain. Anyone who disturbs it is said to cause severe storms. That is why it was long forbidden to climb the mountain. Whether the name really comes from this is not certain. Other explanations link it with the Latin word for a mountain with a cap of cloud.

Two routes for mountain railways lead up Pilatus. From **Alpnachstad** runs the **Pilatus Railway**, the steepest rack railway in the world. From **Kriens** you go up by gondola lift and **cable car**. Popular is the “Golden Round Trip”: by boat from Lucerne to Alpnachstad, up by rack railway and down by cable cars to Kriens. If you prefer walking, you will find many paths up the mountain.

gewusst: The dragon is so important on Pilatus that you meet it in many places as a figure or picture.
The dragon stone that is said to have fallen from the sky is now on display in the Natur-Museum Luzern.

teile.einleitung: The Jura is a mountain range in the north-west of Switzerland. With its gentle hills, limestone cliffs and valleys, it shapes many cantons, including a large part of the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
wichtigste: The Jura stretches from the area around Geneva to northern Switzerland.
It also reaches into France and Germany.
The rock consists mainly of limestone, which was laid down in a sea.
A distinction is made between the Folded Jura with its folds and the flatter Tabular Jura.
In Basel-Landschaft there are table mountains, limestone cliffs and many cherry trees.
The Jura is lower than the Alps.

abschnitte.text: The Jura stretches in a long **arc** from the area around Geneva to Schaffhausen. It lies in Switzerland and in **France**, and in the north it reaches into **Germany**. Many cantons have a share in it, for example Vaud, Neuchâtel, Jura, Bern, Solothurn, Basel-Landschaft and Aargau. The Jura is much lower than the Alps. Its highest peaks reach only a little over 1,700 metres.

A very long time ago, a warm **sea** lay here. On its floor, the shells of sea animals and lime mud were deposited. Over time, this became **limestone**. As the Alps piled up, this rock was pushed and partly folded. That is why you often find **fossils** of sea animals in the Jura.

In the **Folded Jura**, the rock was pushed together into long folds. This created parallel mountain chains with valleys between them. In the **Tabular Jura**, the rock layers lie almost flat. Typical here are **table mountains** with flat tops and steep edges. A large part of Basel-Landschaft belongs to the Tabular Jura.

In Basel-Landschaft, many **cherry trees** grow in the valleys. In spring they blossom white, and in summer the cherries are harvested. In other parts of the Jura there are wide pastures, forests and cold winters. The **watch industry** has a long tradition in the Jura. Many people like walking on the Jura heights.

gewusst: One period of Earth's history, the Jurassic, is named after the Jura mountains.
There are many caves in the limestone of the Jura, because water can dissolve lime.

teile.einleitung: Monte San Giorgio is a mountain in southern Ticino on Lake Lugano. Because many fossilised marine reptiles and fish were found there, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003.
wichtigste: Monte San Giorgio lies in southern Ticino on Lake Lugano.
It is about 1,100 metres high.
About 240 million years ago, a sea lay here.
In the rock, many fossils of marine reptiles and fish were found.
These fossils date from the Triassic.
Since 2003 the mountain has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In Meride there is a fossil museum.

abschnitte.text: About **240 million years ago**, in the **Triassic**, a warm sea lay where Ticino is today. In a bay with little oxygen at the bottom, dead animals sank to the floor. They were covered by fine mud and did not decay. Over a very long time the mud turned into rock, and the animals became **fossils**.

On Monte San Giorgio, thousands of fossils were found. They include **fish**, shellfish and above all **marine reptiles**. A famous animal is **Tanystropheus**, a reptile with an extremely long neck. Ichthyosaurs that looked like dolphins were also found. Many species were discovered here for the first time.

Because the fossils are so numerous and so well preserved, **UNESCO** added the Swiss part of the mountain to the World Heritage List in 2003. Later the Italian part was added too. In the village of **Meride**, a **fossil museum** shows many finds. On a nature trail on the mountain you can learn more about the history of the Earth.

gewusst: The neck of Tanystropheus was longer than its whole body.
Monte San Giorgio is regarded as one of the most important sites in the world for marine fossils from the Triassic.

teile.einleitung: The Lac de Joux lies in the Vallée de Joux in the canton of Vaud. It is the largest lake in the Jura mountains and lies at over 1,000 metres above sea level.
wichtigste: The Lac de Joux is the largest lake in the Jura.
It lies in the Vallée de Joux in the canton of Vaud.
The lake lies at about 1,000 metres above sea level.
In winter it sometimes freezes over, and then you can skate on it.
The Vallée de Joux is famous for its watch industry.

abschnitte.titel: A lake in a high valley
abschnitte.text: The **Vallée de Joux** is a long high valley in the **Vaud Jura**, close to the border with France. The **Lac de Joux** lies in this valley. It is the largest lake in the whole Jura mountains. Because it lies so high, the climate in the valley is harsh, with long, cold winters.

The Lac de Joux has no visible outflow like other lakes. Its water seeps away into the **limestone** of the Jura. It flows on underground and comes back to light at **Vallorbe** as the source of the river Orbe. Landscapes like this, with caves and underground rivers, are called **karst**.

In cold winters the lake sometimes freezes over completely. It then becomes one of the largest natural **ice surfaces** in Europe. Many people come to skate. But you may only go on the ice when it has been officially opened, because thin ice is dangerous.

**Watches** have been made in the Vallée de Joux for centuries. In the past, farming families worked on watch parts in their living rooms during the long winter. Today well-known watch companies have their workshops here. Watchmaking in the Jura is part of UNESCO's **intangible cultural heritage**.

gewusst: The water of the Lac de Joux only reappears at Vallorbe, several kilometres away.
Next to the Lac de Joux lies the small Lac Brenet, which is connected to it.

teile.einleitung: Huldrych Zwingli was the most important reformer in German-speaking Switzerland. He was born in 1484 in Wildhaus in the Toggenburg and was later a priest in Glarus and Einsiedeln. From 1519 he preached at the Grossmünster in Zurich and changed the Church there.
wichtigste: Huldrych Zwingli was born in 1484 in Wildhaus in the Toggenburg.
From 1506 to 1516 he was a priest in Glarus.
After that he worked in Einsiedeln.
From 1519 he preached at the Grossmünster in Zurich.
He brought the Reformation to Zurich.
He died in 1531 in the Second War of Kappel.

abschnitte.text: **Huldrych Zwingli** was born in **1484** in **Wildhaus** in the Toggenburg, in what is now the canton of St Gallen. His father was a farmer and a respected man in the village. Zwingli was a good pupil and was able to study in Basel, Bern and Vienna. You can still visit his birthplace in Wildhaus today.

From **1506** to **1516**, Zwingli was **priest in Glarus** for ten years. During this time he read a great deal, especially the writings of the scholar **Erasmus of Rotterdam** and the Bible in its original languages. He also accompanied mercenaries from Glarus to Italy and afterwards became an opponent of the mercenary system. In 1516 he moved to **Einsiedeln**, a well-known place of pilgrimage.

From **1519**, Zwingli preached at the **Grossmünster** in **Zurich**. He explained the Bible chapter by chapter and criticised customs of the Church of the time that he could not find in the Bible. In time, the Zurich council decided to renew the Church according to his ideas. For example, pictures were removed from the churches and services were held in German. This change is called the **Reformation**.

Not all the states of the Confederation followed the Reformation. In particular, the states of central Switzerland stayed with the old faith, that is, **Catholic**. The conflict led to wars. In **1531**, Zwingli lost his life in the **Second War of Kappel**, near Kappel am Albis. His work in Zurich was carried on by his successor **Heinrich Bullinger**.

gewusst: Under Zwingli, a German Bible translation of its own was produced, which is now called the Zurich Bible.
A public sausage meal during Lent in 1522 in Zurich is regarded as one of the beginnings of the Zurich Reformation.

teile.einleitung: The Limmat is the river that flows out of Lake Zurich and runs through the middle of the city of Zurich. After that it flows through the Limmat valley and the canton of Aargau until it joins the Aare.
wichtigste: The Limmat begins at the outflow of Lake Zurich in Zurich.
It flows through the old town of Zurich.
It then flows through the Limmat valley, for example past Dietikon.
In the canton of Aargau it flows through the spa town of Baden.
At Brugg it joins the Aare.
The Limmat is the continuation of the Linth, which flows into Lake Zurich.

abschnitte.text: In Zurich, the Limmat flows from the lake through the **old town**. On both sides stand old houses, churches and guild houses. On the right bank lies the **Grossmünster** with its two towers, and on the left the **Fraumünster**. Several bridges link the two sides of the city. In summer, many people swim in the river baths on the Limmat.

abschnitte.titel: From the Linth to the Limmat
abschnitte.text: Strictly speaking, the Linth and the Limmat are one single river. The **Linth** comes from the Glarus Alps, flows through Lake Walen and then into **Lake Zurich**. Where the water leaves Lake Zurich again, the river is called the **Limmat**. The lake acts like a large basin in which gravel and sand settle. That is why the water of the Limmat is often clear.

abschnitte.titel: Through the Limmat valley to Baden
abschnitte.text: After Zurich, the Limmat flows through the **Limmat valley**, where many people live and work. In the canton of Aargau it reaches the town of **Baden**. There are hot springs there, which the Romans already used. The old town of Baden lies tight against a bend of the Limmat.

At **Brugg**, the Limmat flows into the **Aare**. Very close by, the Reuss and the Aare also join. Because three large rivers meet here, the area is called the **Wasserschloss (“water castle”) of Switzerland**. A large part of the water from the middle of Switzerland flows past here and later, via the Rhine, as far as the North Sea.

gewusst: In the Middle Ages, water mills stood directly on the Limmat in Zurich.
Every year a swimming race through the city of Zurich, the Limmatschwimmen, is held on the Limmat.

teile.einleitung: The **Pilatus Railway** is the **steepest rack railway in the world**. It runs from **Alpnachstad** in the canton of Obwalden up Pilatus. For over 130 years it has carried people up the mountain.
wichtigste: The Pilatus Railway is the steepest rack railway in the world.
It starts in Alpnachstad on Lake Alpnach in the canton of Obwalden.
The greatest gradient is 48 per cent.
The railway opened in 1889.
It runs up to Pilatus Kulm at over 2,000 metres.
Because of snow, it runs only in the summer half of the year.

abschnitte.text: At its steepest point, the Pilatus Railway has a gradient of **48 per cent**. This means that over 100 metres of track it climbs almost 50 metres. No other rack railway in the world is so steep. The line is about **4.6 kilometres** long and climbs some 1,600 metres. The journey from Alpnachstad to **Pilatus Kulm** takes about half an hour.

With so steep a gradient, an ordinary cog would jump out of the rack. The engineer **Eduard Locher** therefore invented a system of his own. In the **Locher rack system**, the teeth are on the side of the rail. Two horizontal cogwheels grip into them from left and right and hold the carriage firm. Because this system has no ordinary points, the carriages are moved onto other tracks with **transfer tables** and **turntables**.

The Pilatus Railway opened in **1889**. At first it ran on **steam**. Later it was converted to electric operation. The railway is regarded as a masterpiece of engineering and is admired by experts from all over the world. Over time the carriages were renewed several times.

In winter there is a lot of snow on Pilatus, and there is a **danger of avalanches**. That is why the rack railway runs only from about spring to autumn. In winter you can still get up the mountain, namely by the cable cars from **Kriens**. Many guests combine the trip with a boat ride on **Lake Alpnach**, a part of Lake Lucerne.

gewusst: Because the railway is so steep, the rows of seats in the carriages are arranged in steps.

teile.einleitung: The Battle of Grandson took place in 1476 in what is now the canton of Vaud. The Confederates defeated the army of Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy. It is part of the Burgundian Wars.
wichtigste: The Battle of Grandson took place on 2 March 1476.
Grandson lies on Lake Neuchâtel in what is now the canton of Vaud.
The Confederates' opponent was Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy.
The Confederates won the battle.
They captured valuable treasures, the Burgundian booty.
The battle is part of the Burgundian Wars.

abschnitte.text: **Charles the Bold** was Duke of **Burgundy** and one of the richest rulers in Europe. He wanted to enlarge his realm and in doing so fell out with the Confederates. This is how the **Burgundian Wars** began. Bern and its allies feared that Charles would become too powerful.

At the start of 1476 Charles marched to **Lake Neuchâtel** with a large army and captured the castle of **Grandson**. On **2 March 1476** the Confederates met the Burgundian army nearby. A battle followed, and the Burgundians fled. The Confederates had won.

As he fled, Charles left his whole camp behind. The Confederates found magnificent tents, cannons, tapestries, jewellery and money. These treasures are called the **Burgundian booty**. Some pieces can still be seen today in museums, for example in the Bern Historical Museum.

Only a few months later Charles also lost the **Battle of Murten**. At the start of 1477 he died in the Battle of **Nancy**. After that Burgundy was no longer a danger to the Confederates. The victories made the Confederate fighters famous throughout Europe.

gewusst: Grandson Castle still stands on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel today and can be visited.
The Burgundian Wars are often summed up in a saying: Charles lost his goods at Grandson, his courage at Murten and his blood at Nancy.

teile.einleitung: maxon is a company from Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden. It builds small, very precise electric motors that were even used in NASA vehicles on Mars.
wichtigste: maxon has its headquarters in Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
The company writes its name in lower case.
It makes small, precise electric motors and drives.
Motors from maxon were in several NASA Mars vehicles.
Its drives are also used in medical devices and robots.

abschnitte.text: The company **maxon** develops and builds **electric motors** that are often only as big as a finger. They have to work very precisely, reliably and economically. maxon also builds gearboxes and controls. Such drives are needed wherever something has to move precisely, for example in **medical devices**, robots or industrial machines.

In 1997 the small NASA Mars vehicle **Sojourner** drove over Mars, powered by motors from maxon. Motors from the company were also used in later **Mars rovers**. On Mars it is very cold and dusty, and there are strong swings in temperature. The motors therefore had to be especially robust and pass many tests.

The headquarters of maxon are in **Sachseln** on Lake Sarnen. The company now has sites in many countries. It shows that even in a small canton like Obwalden, high tech for the whole world can be created. Sachseln is also known as the place where **Niklaus von Flüe** is buried.

gewusst: A small piece of Obwalden is on Mars: motors from Sachseln work in NASA's rovers.

teile.einleitung: The Battle of Morgarten took place in 1315 near Lake Ägeri, on the border of what are now the cantons of Schwyz and Zug. The Confederates defeated an army of the Habsburgs there. Afterwards Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renewed their alliance.
wichtigste: The Battle of Morgarten took place on 15 November 1315.
It was fought near Lake Ägeri, on the border of what are now the cantons of Schwyz and Zug.
The opponents were the Confederates and a Habsburg army under Duke Leopold.
The Confederates won the battle.
Soon afterwards Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden renewed their alliance in the Pact of Brunnen.
A monument and a chapel recall the battle today.

abschnitte.text: For a long time there had been a dispute between the people of **Schwyz** and the monastery of Einsiedeln over pastures and forests. The **Habsburgs** were the protectors of the monastery and wanted to secure their power in the area. So **Duke Leopold** marched against Schwyz with an army of knights. The route led along Lake Ägeri towards Morgarten.

On **15 November 1315** the Confederates waited on the steep slope of Morgarten. Between the mountain and the lake the path was very narrow. The heavily armoured knights could hardly move there. The Confederates attacked from above and won the battle. Many soldiers of the Habsburg army lost their lives.

A few weeks after the battle, Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden met in **Brunnen**. There they renewed their alliance in the **Pact of Brunnen**. They promised to go on helping one another and not to make their own agreements with foreign lords. The victory strengthened the unity of the Confederates.

On the Zug side, a large **Morgarten Monument** has stood since the early 20th century. On the Schwyz side, the **Battle Chapel** recalls the event. Every year in November the **Morgarten shoot** takes place. Historians still debate where exactly the battle took place.

gewusst: The Battle of Morgarten is considered the first great battle of the Confederates.
The exact site of the battle is not known for certain, so places in both cantons commemorate it.

teile.einleitung: The Oberalp Pass is an Alpine pass between the cantons of Uri and the Grisons. It links Andermatt in the Urseren valley with Disentis in the Surselva (Bündner Oberland). The Rhine rises very close by.
wichtigste: The Oberalp Pass is about 2,044 metres high.
It links Andermatt in the canton of Uri with Disentis in the canton of the Grisons.
A road and a railway line lead over the pass.
The Glacier Express also runs over the Oberalp Pass.
Nearby lies Lake Toma, which is regarded as the source of the Rhine.
In winter the pass road is closed, but the railway keeps running.

abschnitte.text: The **Oberalp Pass** lies at about 2,044 metres above sea level. On one side lies **Andermatt** in the canton of **Uri**, and on the other the road goes down to Sedrun and **Disentis** in the **Grisons**. On the pass runs the border between the two cantons. Around the pass there are meadows, rocks and a small lake.

The **Matterhorn Gotthard Railway** runs over the Oberalp Pass. On steep stretches, a **rack rail** between the rails helps so that the train does not slip. The famous **Glacier Express** between Zermatt and St Moritz also runs over the pass. The railway also runs in winter, when the road is closed because of snow.

Not far from the pass lies the small **Lake Toma**. It is regarded as the **source of the Rhine**, that is, the origin of the **Anterior Rhine**. From here the water flows through the Grisons, Lake Constance and Germany to the North Sea. On the summit of the pass, a small red **lighthouse** stands in memory of this.

In summer the Oberalp Pass is a popular destination for **walks**, for example to Lake Toma. In winter it is part of a large **ski area** that links Andermatt and Sedrun. The road is then closed, but you can reach the pass by train.

gewusst: On the Oberalp Pass stands a lighthouse, although the sea is very far away: it recalls that the Rhine begins here and flows to the North Sea.
From Lake Toma to the North Sea, the Rhine covers over a thousand kilometres.

teile.einleitung: The Napoleon Museum Arenenberg is a castle with a museum in the municipality of Salenstein in the canton of Thurgau. It lies high above the Untersee, a part of Lake Constance. Here the future French emperor Napoleon III spent part of his youth.
wichtigste: Arenenberg Castle lies in Salenstein in the canton of Thurgau.
It stands above the Untersee, a part of Lake Constance.
Hortense de Beauharnais lived here with her son Louis Napoleon.
Her son later became Emperor of France as Napoleon III.
Today the castle is a museum with furniture and art from that time.
Around the castle lies a beautiful park.

abschnitte.text: **Arenenberg** Castle lies on a hill above the **Untersee**. From there you can see far over the water to Germany. At the beginning of the 19th century, **Hortense de Beauharnais** bought the castle. She was the stepdaughter of Emperor **Napoleon I** and for a time Queen of Holland.

After the fall of Napoleon I, the family had to leave France. Hortense moved with her son **Louis Napoleon** to the Arenenberg. He spent part of his youth here and also often visited Switzerland. Later he became president and then, as **Napoleon III**, Emperor of France.

At the beginning of the 20th century, the widow of Napoleon III, Empress **Eugénie**, gave the castle to the **canton of Thurgau**. Since then it has been a **museum**. You can see furnished living rooms, furniture, paintings and personal belongings of the family. This gives an impression of how distinguished people lived at that time.

Around the castle lies a large **park** with paths, trees and viewpoints. It was laid out in the style of an English landscape garden. On the Arenenberg there is also a school of agriculture. The place is a popular destination for outings on Lake Constance.

gewusst: Hortense de Beauharnais was the mother of Napoleon III and at the same time the stepdaughter of Napoleon I.
Louis Napoleon was made an honorary citizen by the canton of Thurgau.

teile.einleitung: The Jet d'eau is a huge fountain of water in Lake Geneva. It is the landmark of the city of Geneva and shoots water about 140 metres into the air.
wichtigste: The Jet d'eau stands in Lake Geneva, in the harbour basin of Geneva.
It shoots the water about 140 metres high.
The name is French and means “jet of water”.
The very first Jet d'eau in 1886 was a pressure relief valve.
Because people liked it, it became a sight to see.
Today powerful pumps drive the lake water up into the air.

abschnitte.text: The Jet d'eau stands on the shore in the **harbour basin** of Geneva, where the Rhône leaves Lake Geneva. It shoots the water about **140 metres** high. That is higher than most church towers. You can see the jet from far away, for example from an aeroplane. In the evening it is often lit up in colour.

The very first Jet d'eau came about in **1886** at a waterworks on the Rhône. When the factories switched off their machines in the evening, the pressure in the water pipes rose too high. So a **pressure relief valve** was built, from which the surplus water sprayed into the air. People liked this jet so much that they wanted to keep it.

A few years later, the Jet d'eau was moved to its present place in the **lake**, where it could spray much higher. Today powerful **pumps** drive the lake water upwards with great force. In this way it became the **landmark** of Geneva. It appears in many photos, postcards and posters of the city.

In strong wind, the Jet d'eau is sometimes switched off or turned down. Otherwise the wind would blow the water far over the people walking along the shore. In frost it is also switched off. Anyone who goes close still often gets a little wet. On sunny days you often see a **rainbow** in the spray.

gewusst: The water leaves the nozzle at about 200 kilometres per hour.
A drop of water takes several seconds to get back down into the lake.

teile.einleitung: The Sarner Aa is a river in the canton of Obwalden. It flows out of Lake Sarnen, through the main town of Sarnen, and into Lake Alpnach. Lake Alpnach is part of Lake Lucerne.
wichtigste: The Sarner Aa is a river in the canton of Obwalden.
It leaves Lake Sarnen at Sarnen.
It flows into Lake Alpnach at Alpnach.
Lake Alpnach is part of Lake Lucerne.
After heavy rain the Sarner Aa can flood.

abschnitte.text: The **Sarner Aa** links two lakes. It flows out of the northern end of **Lake Sarnen** and through Sarnen. Then it crosses the flat valley as far as **Alpnach**, where it flows into **Lake Alpnach**. Its water thus reaches Lake Lucerne and finally, by way of the Reuss, the Rhine.

The word **Aa** is a very old word for water or river. In central Switzerland several rivers have this name, for example the Engelberger Aa. So that they can be told apart, the name of the place or valley comes first. That is how the name Sarner Aa came about.

After heavy rain Lake Sarnen rises and the Sarner Aa can burst its banks. In 2005 there was a serious **flood** in which parts of Sarnen were under water. Since then a great deal has been done for **flood protection**. Among other things, a tunnel was planned and built to carry excess water past the town.

gewusst: The water of the Sarner Aa flows through Lake Lucerne, the Reuss, the Aare and the Rhine all the way to the North Sea.

teile.einleitung: The **Roothuus** in **Gonten** is a centre for **Appenzell folk music**. Here the music of the Appenzell region and the Toggenburg is collected, researched and passed on. Gonten lies in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.
wichtigste: The Roothuus stands in Gonten in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.
It is a centre for the folk music of the Appenzell region and the Toggenburg.
Sheet music, sound recordings and knowledge about the music are collected there.
The Roothuus also passes the music on in courses and events.
The name means “red house”.

abschnitte.text: “Roothuus” means “**red house**” in the dialect. It is an old, typical Appenzell wooden house in the village of **Gonten**. Gonten lies between Appenzell and Urnäsch. In the Roothuus a centre has been set up that is devoted entirely to **folk music**. It collects sheet music, old **sound recordings**, pictures and stories of musicians.

Typical of the Appenzell region is **Streichmusik** (string music). It usually includes two violins, a **hammered dulcimer** (Hackbrett), a cello and a double bass. The hammered dulcimer is an instrument with many strings that are struck with small hammers. Also well known are the **Zäuerli**, a natural yodel without words, and **Talerschwingen**, in which coins circle in a bowl. The neighbouring **Toggenburg** also has a rich musical tradition.

The Roothuus wants folk music to stay **alive**. That is why old melodies are written down and organised, so that they are not forgotten. Experts research where the pieces come from and how they were played in the past. There are also **courses**, concerts and events at which young and old make music together. In this way the music is passed from one generation to the next.

gewusst: In Talerschwingen, coins are made to circle in a clay bowl, which gives a ringing tone to go with the yodel.
Many Appenzell melodies were passed on only by word of mouth for a long time, not in written notes.

teile.einleitung: The Kernwald is a forest in central Switzerland. It lies between the cantons of Obwalden and Nidwalden and gave both cantons their names.
wichtigste: The Kernwald lies between Obwalden and Nidwalden.
In the past, both areas together formed the land of Unterwalden.
Obwalden is so called because it lies “ob dem Kernwald”, that is, above it.
Nidwalden is so called because it lies “nid dem Kernwald”, that is, below it.
Unterwalden is one of the three original cantons of the Confederation.

abschnitte.text: The **Kernwald** is a large wooded area between Lake Sarnen and Stans. In the past, a forest like this was a real obstacle, because paths led through it only with difficulty. That is why the forest separated the valleys on either side. People used it as a reference point when they said where they lived.

The old land of **Unterwalden** consisted of two parts. The part above the forest was called “ob dem Kernwald”, which became **Obwalden**. The part below was called “nid dem Kernwald”, which became **Nidwalden**. In the old language, “ob” means above, and “nid” means below or beneath.

Together with Uri and Schwyz, Unterwalden is one of the **original cantons**. But for a long time Obwalden and Nidwalden had managed their affairs separately. Today both are cantons in their own right, each with its own main town: Sarnen in Obwalden and Stans in Nidwalden. In the Council of States, each of the two cantons has one seat.

gewusst: The coats of arms of Obwalden and Nidwalden both show a key, an old symbol of Unterwalden.
The names of two cantons go back to a single forest.

teile.einleitung: The Olympic Museum stands in Lausanne in the canton of Vaud right on Lake Geneva. It tells the history of the Olympic Games from antiquity to today. Lausanne calls itself the “Olympic Capital” because the International Olympic Committee also has its seat here.
wichtigste: The Olympic Museum lies in the Ouchy district of Lausanne on Lake Geneva.
It opened in 1993 and was later extensively renovated.
There you can see torches, medals, sports equipment and films.
The International Olympic Committee has its seat in Lausanne.
Pierre de Coubertin, the founder of the modern Games, brought the committee to Lausanne.
Lausanne calls itself the “Olympic Capital”.

abschnitte.text: The **Olympic Museum** stands in **Ouchy**, the district of Lausanne right on Lake Geneva. It opened in **1993**. Around the building lies an **Olympic Park** with sculptures, paths and a view of the lake and the mountains. After a major renovation, the museum reopened in 2013.

In the museum you can see **Olympic torches** from many Games, **medals** and clothing of famous athletes. Films and games show how athletes train. You also learn something about the **ancient Games** in Olympia in Greece, which took place over 2,000 years ago.

The Frenchman **Pierre de Coubertin** founded the modern Olympic Games. In **1915**, he moved the seat of the **International Olympic Committee**, **IOC** for short, to Lausanne. Since then the city has been the centre of the Olympic movement. Many international sports federations also have their seat in the region.

In **2020**, the **Winter Youth Olympic Games** took place in Lausanne and the surrounding area. Young athletes from all over the world competed there. This suited the city, which calls itself the “Olympic Capital”.

gewusst: Pierre de Coubertin is buried in Lausanne, but his heart lies in Olympia in Greece.
In the Olympic Museum there are torches that come from Games on all continents.

teile.einleitung: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was a famous philosopher and writer. He was born in Geneva in 1712 and wrote important books on education and on how people live together.
wichtigste: Rousseau was born in Geneva in 1712 and died in France in 1778.
He was a philosopher, writer and also a composer.
His book “Emile” is about the education of children.
In the book “The Social Contract” he wrote about the state and freedom.
His ideas influenced the French Revolution.
In Geneva there is an island with his statue.

abschnitte.text: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was born in **Geneva** in 1712. His father was a watchmaker. As a teenager, Rousseau left the city and travelled around a lot. He lived for a long time in France, especially in **Paris**. There he got to know important thinkers of his time and began to write.

In 1762 his book **“Emile, or On Education”** appeared. In it Rousseau explained that children think differently from adults. They should not simply be made to learn things by heart. Children should learn from their own experiences, as far as possible in nature. These ideas were new at the time and later influenced many educators, including the Swiss Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi.

In the same year, **“The Social Contract”** appeared. In it Rousseau asked how people can live freely and yet together in one state. His answer: power should come from the **people**, and the laws should serve the common good. These ideas were dangerous for the rulers of the time. His books were banned in Geneva and Paris.

Rousseau's ideas influenced the **French Revolution** and thinking about **democracy**. For a time he also lived on St Peter's Island in Lake Biel. He died in France in 1778. In Geneva, the **Île Rousseau**, a small island in the Rhône, recalls him with a statue.

gewusst: Rousseau also composed music and even wrote an opera.
Although Geneva once banned his books, the city is proud of him today.

teile.einleitung: Hallwyl Castle is a famous moated castle in the canton of Aargau. It stands close to Lake Hallwil on two small islands and is completely surrounded by water. Today it is a museum.
wichtigste: Hallwyl Castle stands near Seengen in the canton of Aargau.
It lies at the northern end of Lake Hallwil.
The castle stands on two islands in the Aabach.
It is one of the best-known moated castles in Switzerland.
For centuries it belonged to the Hallwyl family.
Today it is a museum and part of Museum Aargau.

abschnitte.text: A **moated castle** is a fortress surrounded by water. Hallwyl Castle stands on **two small islands** in the Aabach, which flows out of Lake Hallwil. In the past the water protected the castle from attackers. You reach the castle by bridges.

The castle was built in the Middle Ages. For many centuries the **Hallwyl family**, a well-known noble family, lived here. The castle was rebuilt and extended several times. At the start of the 20th century the family had the castle thoroughly **restored**. Later it handed the castle over to a foundation, and today it is looked after by the canton of Aargau.

Today Hallwyl Castle is a **museum**. In its rooms you can find out how the family lived over the centuries. You can see furniture, clothes, tools and toys. An old mill also belongs to the site. There are guided tours and activities for children.

The castle lies in green countryside by **Lake Hallwil**. You can walk along the lake or take a boat trip. In summer there is sometimes theatre or music in the castle courtyard. So a visit combines history and nature.

gewusst: Lake Hallwil takes its name from the same family as the castle.
Hallwyl Castle is often counted among the most beautiful moated castles in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Kleinbasel is a part of the city of Basel. It lies on the right, northern side of the Rhine, opposite Grossbasel with the Minster and the old town.
wichtigste: Kleinbasel lies to the right of the Rhine, Grossbasel to the left of it.
Kleinbasel used to be a small town of its own.
In 1392 Basel bought the town of Kleinbasel and united it with itself.
Since the Middle Ages, the Mittlere Brücke has linked the two parts.
In January Kleinbasel celebrates the Vogel Gryff.

abschnitte.text: The **Rhine** flows right through Basel. On the left side lies **Grossbasel** with the Minster and the Town Hall. On the right side lies **Kleinbasel**. As early as the 13th century a bridge was built over the Rhine, and the present **Mittlere Brücke** stands on the same spot.

Kleinbasel began in the Middle Ages as a small town of its own with its own wall. For a long time it belonged to the Bishop of Basel. In **1392**, Grossbasel bought the town, and the two parts were united into one city. Even so, the people of Kleinbasel are still proud of their own history today.

Every year in January, Kleinbasel celebrates the **Vogel Gryff**. Three figures, the Vogel Gryff (griffin), the Leu (lion) and the Wilde Mann (wild man), dance through the streets. The Wilde Mann first travels down the Rhine on a raft. During the dance on the bridge, the figures turn their backs on Grossbasel, an old joke between the two parts of the city.

Today Kleinbasel is a lively district with homes, shops and restaurants. On the **bank of the Rhine** many people sit in summer, and some let themselves drift down the Rhine. The grounds of the **Messe Basel** trade fair also lie in Kleinbasel. Several bridges and small ferries link the two banks.

gewusst: The Basel Rhine ferries are driven only by the current of the Rhine, without an engine.
At the Vogel Gryff, the figures turn their backs on Grossbasel on purpose.

teile.einleitung: St Pierre Cathedral stands on the highest point of Geneva's old town. It is over 800 years old and was the church in which the reformer John Calvin preached.
wichtigste: St Pierre Cathedral stands on the highest point of Geneva's old town.
Building began in the 12th century.
Since the Reformation it has been a Reformed church.
John Calvin preached here in the 16th century.
From the towers there is a wonderful view over Geneva and the lake.
Under the church there is a large archaeological excavation.

abschnitte.text: Building of **St Pierre** Cathedral began in the 12th century. It is dedicated to the apostle Peter, in French Pierre. It was built over many decades. That is why different styles are mixed, above all **Romanesque** and **Gothic**. In the 18th century it received a new façade with columns that recalls an ancient temple.

In the 16th century, Geneva became **Reformed**. The pictures and altars were removed from the church, which is why it is plain inside today. The reformer **John Calvin** preached here for many years. A chair that is attributed to him still stands in the church. Since the Reformation, Geneva has had no bishop of its own, but the name cathedral has remained.

You can climb the **towers**. From the top you can see over the roofs of the old town, **Lake Geneva** and the Jet d'eau. In clear weather you can even see the Alps. Under the cathedral lies a large **archaeological excavation**. There you can see remains of earlier churches and buildings from Roman times.

gewusst: The bell “La Clémence” in one of the towers is over 600 years old.
Several older churches already stood on the same spot before the present cathedral.

teile.einleitung: “Schellen-Ursli” is one of the best-known Swiss picture books. It tells of a boy from the Engadine who fetches a big bell. The book came out in 1945 and is still read with pleasure today.
wichtigste: The story was written by Selina Chönz.
The pictures were painted by Alois Carigiet.
The book came out in 1945.
It is set in the Engadine in the canton of Graubünden, in the village of Guarda.
Ursli fetches a big bell for the custom of Chalandamarz.
In 2015 the story was made into a cinema film.

abschnitte.text: Little **Ursli** is only to get a tiny bell for the Chalandamarz procession. The other children laugh at him. So he climbs alone through the deep snow up to the **mountain hut** where a big bell hangs. He spends the night there while his parents worry. The next morning he comes back with the biggest bell and gets to lead the procession.

The story was written by **Selina Chönz**, an author from the Engadine. The pictures were painted by **Alois Carigiet**, an artist from Graubünden. His colourful, warm pictures made the book famous. The two later created further books, for example about Ursli's sister Flurina.

**Chalandamarz** means “first of March”. On this day in the Engadine and in other parts of Graubünden, children walk through the village with bells and cowbells. They sing songs and want to **drive away winter** with the noise. The custom is very old and is still celebrated today.

The story is set in **Guarda** in the Lower Engadine. The village has beautiful old **Engadine houses** with thick walls and decorated façades. Many visitors come here to see Schellen-Ursli's village. A trail with stations recalls the story.

gewusst: The book has been translated into many languages, including English, where the boy is called “Ursli” and the story “A Bell for Ursli”.
The name Chalandamarz comes from the Latin word for the first day of a month.

teile.einleitung: **Romanshorn** is a municipality in the canton of Thurgau on **Lake Constance**. Its harbour is one of the most important on the Swiss shore. From here a **car ferry** crosses the lake to **Friedrichshafen** in Germany.
wichtigste: Romanshorn lies in the canton of Thurgau on Lake Constance.
A car ferry runs from Romanshorn to Friedrichshafen in Germany.
The ferry takes people, bicycles and cars.
Romanshorn has one of the largest harbours on the Swiss shore of Lake Constance.
In the past, train ferries carried whole goods wagons across the lake here.
Romanshorn is also an important railway station in Thurgau.

abschnitte.text: Between **Romanshorn** and **Friedrichshafen**, a **car ferry** crosses Lake Constance. It takes people, bicycles, cars and even lorries. The crossing takes less than an hour. This saves the long detour around the lake. The ferry is run jointly by shipping companies from Switzerland and Germany.

As early as the **19th century**, Romanshorn became an important harbour. At that time **train ferries** ran here that carried whole goods wagons across Lake Constance. In this way goods such as grain from Germany could go on directly by train. Today this traffic is over. But Romanshorn station is still a junction where trains from St Gallen, Konstanz and Zurich meet.

Romanshorn has a large **harbour** with scheduled boats, sailing boats and ferries. On the shore there are bathing spots, parks and a long promenade. On the **Lake Constance cycle path**, many cyclists ride through the place. Lake Constance borders Switzerland, Germany and Austria. That is why boats run here between three countries.

gewusst: Three countries border each other on Lake Constance: Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
In the past, whole railway wagons were loaded onto ships in Romanshorn.

teile.einleitung: Neuhausen am Rheinfall is a municipality in the canton of Schaffhausen right next to the town of Schaffhausen. It is famous because the Rhine Falls are here. In addition, Neuhausen was for a long time an important place for industry.
wichtigste: Neuhausen am Rheinfall belongs to the canton of Schaffhausen.
The municipality borders directly on the town of Schaffhausen.
The Rhine Falls are regarded as one of the largest waterfalls in Europe.
The opposite bank with Laufen Castle belongs to the canton of Zurich.
The power of the water once helped in setting up factories.
Every year very many tourists visit the Rhine Falls.

abschnitte.text: At Neuhausen, the **Rhine** plunges over a rocky step into the depths. The **Rhine Falls** are about 150 metres wide and some 23 metres high. They are regarded as one of the largest waterfalls in Europe. Especially in summer, when a lot of meltwater comes from the Alps, the water thunders down with great force.

On the Neuhausen side stands **Schlössli Wörth**. Opposite, on a rock above the waterfall, lies **Laufen Castle**. This bank already belongs to the **canton of Zurich**. With small boats you can travel to the **rock** in the middle of the Rhine Falls and even climb it.

The water of the Rhine once supplied energy for factories. In the 19th century, the **Schweizerische Industrie-Gesellschaft** was founded in Neuhausen, which built railway carriages among other things. One of the first **aluminium works** in Europe was also founded here. Making aluminium needs a great deal of **electricity**, and hydropower supplied it.

Today Neuhausen is known mainly because of the Rhine Falls. There are viewing platforms, paths and boats from which you can experience the waterfall at close range. On **1 August** there is a large **firework display** at the Rhine Falls. The waterfall is then lit up in colour.

gewusst: The amount of water at the Rhine Falls is much greater in summer than in winter, because then snow and ice in the Alps melt.
The rock in the middle of the Rhine Falls has stood for thousands of years, although the water constantly gnaws at it.

teile.einleitung: Lake Klöntal is a mountain lake in the canton of Glarus. It lies in the Klöntal valley west of Glarus, framed by steep mountains that are reflected in the water.
wichtigste: Lake Klöntal lies in the Klöntal valley west of Glarus.
The Glärnisch massif rises above the lake.
The lake formed naturally but was enlarged by a dam.
Its water is used to generate electricity.
It is a popular destination for swimming, walking and picnics.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Klöntal** lies in a narrow valley above **Netstal** and Glarus. On the south side the **Glärnisch** rises steeply. On calm days the rock walls are reflected in the green-blue water. A narrow road runs along the north shore through the valley.

The lake originally formed in a natural way. At the beginning of the **20th century**, a **dam** was built at the end of the lake, which made it larger and deeper. The water flows through pipes into the valley and drives **turbines** there that produce electricity. That is why the water level varies with the season.

In summer many people come to Lake Klöntal. They swim, barbecue on the shore, camp or walk around the lake. In winter the lake sometimes freezes over and lies quiet and white in the valley. The Klöntal is part of the wild mountain world of Glarus.

gewusst: The Glärnisch, which rises above Lake Klöntal, is almost 3,000 metres high.

teile.einleitung: At **4,049 metres**, **Piz Bernina** is the highest mountain in the canton of the Grisons. It is the only four-thousand-metre peak of the **Eastern Alps**. Its famous ridge of snow and ice is called the “Biancograt”.
wichtigste: Piz Bernina is 4,049 metres high.
It is the highest mountain in the Grisons and in the whole of the Eastern Alps.
It is the only four-thousand-metre peak in the Eastern Alps.
It lies in the Upper Engadine near Pontresina.
The first ascent was made in 1850 by Johann Coaz and his companions.
The Biancograt is regarded as one of the most beautiful ridges in the Alps.

abschnitte.text: The Alps are often divided into the **Western Alps** and the **Eastern Alps**. In the Western Alps there are many four-thousand-metre peaks, but in the Eastern Alps only one: **Piz Bernina**. It is 4,049 metres high and belongs to the **Bernina group**. The mountain lies in the **Upper Engadine**, south of Pontresina, near the border with Italy. It is therefore also the highest point of the canton of the Grisons.

The first person to stand on the summit was **Johann Coaz**, in **1850**. He was a surveyor and was working on an accurate map of Switzerland. Two helpers climbed with him. Coaz also gave the mountain its name, after the nearby **Bernina Pass**. Later Coaz became the first federal chief forestry inspector of Switzerland.

From the north, a long, narrow ridge of snow leads to the summit. It is called the **Biancograt**, after the Italian word “bianco” for white. Because it rises so elegantly into the sky, it is also called the “**ladder to heaven**”. The ascent is only for experienced mountaineers with good equipment. Below Piz Bernina flows the **Morteratsch Glacier**.

Over the Bernina Pass runs the **Bernina Railway** of the Rhaetian Railway from St Moritz to Tirano in Italy. Together with the Albula Railway, it has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since **2008**. From the train you can see the glaciers and peaks of the Bernina group. The region is very popular with walkers, mountaineers and skiers.

gewusst: Piz Bernina is the easternmost four-thousand-metre peak in the Alps.
Because of its shape, the Biancograt is called the “ladder to heaven”.

teile.einleitung: The **Reformation Wall** in Geneva is a wall about 100 metres long with large stone figures. It stands in the **Parc des Bastions** and recalls the Reformation in the 16th century. At its centre stand four well-known reformers.
wichtigste: The Reformation Wall stands in the Parc des Bastions in Geneva.
It was built from 1909 and inaugurated in 1917.
It is about 100 metres long.
In the middle stand Farel, Calvin, Beza and Knox.
Above the figures stands the Geneva motto “Post tenebras lux”.
It was planned for the 400th birthday of John Calvin.

abschnitte.text: The monument is built against the old **city wall** of Geneva. In the middle stand four large stone figures, each about five metres high. They are **Guillaume Farel**, **John Calvin**, **Theodore Beza** (in French Bèze) and **John Knox**. They wear long robes and hold books in their hands. Beside them, smaller figures and pictures show further people and events from the history of the Reformation.

In **1909**, Geneva celebrated two anniversaries. It was the **400th birthday** of John Calvin, and the Geneva **Academy**, from which the university grew, was 350 years old. A competition was therefore announced for a monument. Building began in 1909, and the monument was inaugurated in **1917**. Above the figures, in large letters, stands the motto “**Post tenebras lux**”.

The **Reformation** was a movement that wanted to renew the church in the 16th century. From it came the **Reformed** and other Protestant churches. **Farel** brought the Reformation to Geneva, and **Calvin** shaped it over many years. **Beza** was Calvin's successor, and **Knox** carried the ideas to Scotland. Their teachings have influenced many countries.

The **Parc des Bastions** lies on the edge of Geneva's old town. Right in the park stands a main building of the **University of Geneva**. The monument stands in front of an old moat that was once part of the fortifications. In the park, many people play on large chessboards on the ground. For tourists, the Reformation Wall is one of the best-known photo spots in Geneva.

gewusst: The four main figures are about five metres high.
The monument is built against a part of the old Geneva city fortifications.

teile.einleitung: The Laténium is a large archaeology museum in Hauterive on Lake Neuchâtel in the canton of Neuchâtel. It shows finds from many thousands of years, from the lake dwellers to the Celts and Romans.
wichtigste: The Laténium stands in Hauterive on Lake Neuchâtel.
It is one of the largest archaeology museums in Switzerland.
It opened in the year 2001.
Its name recalls the find site of La Tène.
The museum includes a park with reconstructed houses from prehistoric times.

abschnitte.text: The **Laténium** lies in **Hauterive**, very close to the shore of Lake Neuchâtel. It opened in **2001** and is one of the largest museums of **archaeology** in Switzerland. Archaeology is the science that uses excavations to find out how people lived in the past.

abschnitte.titel: From lake dwellers to the Romans
abschnitte.text: The museum shows finds from many thousands of years. You can see tools of Stone Age hunters, objects of the **lake dwellers** and finds from the Bronze Age. Especially important are the finds of the **Celts** from La Tène, such as swords and jewellery. The time of the **Romans** is also shown, for example with a large boat.

Around the museum lies an **archaeological park**. There stand reconstructions of houses from prehistoric times, for example a pile dwelling. You can also see traces of what the shore looked like in the past. This makes it easy to imagine, outdoors, how people lived by the lake thousands of years ago.

gewusst: The name Laténium comes from the nearby find site of La Tène, after which a whole period is named.

teile.einleitung: Monte Verità is a hill above Ascona in the canton of Ticino. Around 1900, people gathered here who wanted to live differently from life in the big cities. Today the place is a museum, a hotel and a meeting place for science.
wichtigste: Monte Verità lies near Ascona on Lake Maggiore in the canton of Ticino.
The name means “Mountain of Truth”.
From 1900, drop-outs founded a settlement here with a life close to nature.
The residents ate vegetarian food, worked in the garden and spent a lot of time in the fresh air.
Famous artists, writers and dancers visited the place.
Today Monte Verità belongs to a foundation and serves as a museum and conference venue.

abschnitte.text: Around the year 1900, many cities were noisy, cramped and full of factories. Some young people from northern Europe therefore wanted to live more simply and more healthily. They bought land on the hill near Ascona and founded a small settlement there. This movement is called **Lebensreform** (life reform): people wanted to live in harmony with nature and to give up meat, alcohol and tobacco.

The residents built simple wooden houses and planted vegetables and fruit. They ate a **vegetarian** diet, wore loose clothes and often went barefoot. They spent a lot of time outdoors in the sun and air. Later the settlement became a spa where guests could recover.

Monte Verità attracted many well-known people. The writer **Hermann Hesse**, for example, came here to recover. Dancers also tried out new forms of free dance here. In this way the little hill in Ticino became a place where new ideas for art and life were born.

In the 1920s an art collector bought the site and had a modern **hotel** built. Today the place belongs to a foundation in which the canton of Ticino also has a share. In the museum, for example in the **Casa Anatta**, you can learn more about the history of the drop-outs. Scientific conferences are also held here, and there is a beautiful park.

gewusst: On Monte Verità there is a tea house with a small tea garden in which tea bushes grow.
Many ideas from Monte Verità, such as vegetarian food and exercise in the fresh air, are quite normal today.

teile.einleitung: Jurassica is a museum in Porrentruy in the canton of Jura. It shows finds from the time of the dinosaurs, above all thousands of footprints that were discovered when the A16 motorway was built.
wichtigste: Jurassica is in Porrentruy, in German Pruntrut, in the canton of Jura.
When the A16 motorway was built, thousands of dinosaur footprints were found.
The footprints are many millions of years old and date from the Jurassic.
At that time the coast of a warm sea lay here.
The museum shows fossils, footprints and a botanical garden.

abschnitte.text: When the **A16 motorway** was being built in the canton of Jura, experts examined the ground before building began. In doing so, they made a great discovery: **thousands of dinosaur footprints** in the limestone. The footprints are many millions of years old. Some come from huge plant-eaters with long necks, others from meat-eaters that walked on two legs. Many footprints form long trails, as if the animals had only just walked past.

In the **Jurassic**, the area looked completely different. The coast of a warm, shallow **sea** lay here. The dinosaurs walked across soft, muddy ground on the shore. The mud later turned into hard limestone, and the imprints were preserved. Besides footprints, fossilised bones, teeth, turtles and sea animals were also found.

In the **Jurassica** museum you can look at the finds and learn a lot about the Jurassic. It shows fossils, models and casts of the footprints. The museum also has a **botanical garden**. So here you get to know plants of today and animals from prehistoric times.

gewusst: The canton of Jura and the Jurassic both bear the name of the Jura mountains.
From footprints, experts can tell how big a dinosaur was and how fast it walked.

teile.einleitung: The Musée international d'horlogerie, in English the International Watchmaking Museum, stands in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the canton of Neuchâtel. It shows thousands of clocks and watches from many centuries. Here you learn how people measured time.
wichtigste: The museum stands in La Chaux-de-Fonds in the Neuchâtel Jura.
It shows thousands of clocks, watches and instruments for measuring time.
You can see sundials, pendulum clocks, pocket watches and wristwatches.
The museum building lies largely underground.
La Chaux-de-Fonds is one of the most important watchmaking towns in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: **La Chaux-de-Fonds** lies high in the **Jura** in the canton of Neuchâtel. Watches have been made here since the 18th century. After a fire, the town was laid out anew with straight streets so that the workshops would get plenty of light. Together with **Le Locle**, it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

In the museum there are **thousands of clocks and watches** from many countries and centuries. You can see simple **sundials** and **hourglasses**, splendid pendulum clocks, small **pocket watches** and modern wristwatches. Automata and very accurate timepieces for science are also on display. In this way you can follow how **timekeeping** became ever more accurate.

The present museum building lies for the most part **underground**. From outside you mainly see a park. In the museum there is also a workshop where old timepieces are **restored**, that is, carefully repaired. In front of the building stands a large **carillon**, which sounds at certain times.

gewusst: The urban landscape of La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site because of the watch industry.
The famous architect Le Corbusier was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

teile.einleitung: Interlaken is a town in the Bernese Oberland in the canton of Bern. It lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz and is one of the best-known holiday resorts in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
The name means “between the lakes”.
The flat land between the lakes is called the Bödeli.
Interlaken is a gateway to the Jungfrau region.
Many visitors from all over the world come here on holiday.
In the middle of the town lies the big meadow called the Höhematte.

abschnitte.text: Interlaken lies on a flat plain between **Lake Thun** and **Lake Brienz**. This plain is called the **Bödeli**. It was formed because streams deposited gravel and sand over a long time. The Aare links the two lakes and flows right through the town. High mountains rise all around.

The name comes from **Latin**: “inter lacus” means “between the lakes”. In the past there was a monastery here that carried this name. The place itself was long called something else. Only later did it get the name Interlaken, which is known around the world today.

abschnitte.titel: A holiday resort for a long time
abschnitte.text: As early as the 19th century, many travellers came to Interlaken. Large **hotels** with views of the mountains were built. From Interlaken, railways run into the **Jungfrau region**, for example to Grindelwald, Lauterbrunnen and up to the Jungfraujoch. Today visitors come from all over the world. Many also do adventure sports here, such as paragliding.

In the middle of the town lies the **Höhematte**, a large meadow. It may not be built on. From here you can see the snowy **Jungfrau** in fine weather. Paragliders often land on the meadow. Old hotels stand around it.

gewusst: Above Interlaken lies the viewpoint Harder, which you reach by funicular railway.
Interlaken has two big railway stations: Interlaken West and Interlaken Ost.

teile.einleitung: The Möhl cider mill (Mosterei Möhl) is a drinks company in Arbon in the canton of Thurgau. For many decades it has pressed apples from the region into juice. This suits it well, because Thurgau is known as the apple canton.
wichtigste: The Möhl cider mill has its seat in Arbon on Lake Constance.
Arbon lies in the canton of Thurgau.
The company is a family business with a long history.
It makes apple juice, apple spritzer and cider.
Some of the apples come from trees in eastern Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In the canton of **Thurgau** there are very many fruit trees. That is why it is also called **Mostindien**. For a long time, **Most** has been made from the apples. In Switzerland this is the name for freshly pressed apple juice and also for fermented cider. One of the best-known cider mills is the Möhl company in Arbon.

The Möhl cider mill has been run for generations by the **Möhl family**. In autumn, farmers bring their apples to the mill. There they are washed, crushed and **pressed**. Various drinks are made from the juice, for example cloudy apple juice or apple juice with mineral water, which is called **Schorle** (spritzer).

At the cider mill there is a **museum** of its own. There you can see old presses, barrels and machines. You learn how cider was made in the past and how important fruit trees were for farmers in Thurgau. Many school classes visit the museum on an outing.

gewusst: Because of its many apple trees, Thurgau is jokingly called “Mostindien”.

teile.einleitung: The Rorschach-Heiden Railway is a small mountain railway in eastern Switzerland. Since 1875 it has run from Lake Constance up into the Appenzell Vorderland to Heiden. On the steep stretch a cogwheel helps.
wichtigste: The Rorschach-Heiden Railway links Rorschach on Lake Constance with Heiden.
Rorschach lies in the canton of St Gallen, Heiden in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
The railway opened in 1875.
On the steep sections a cogwheel engages a rack rail.
The line is only a few kilometres long, but climbs almost 400 metres.
Today the railway belongs to the Appenzell Railways.

abschnitte.titel: From the lake up the mountain
abschnitte.text: The railway starts in **Rorschach** on the shore of Lake Constance. From there it climbs through meadows and woods up to **Heiden**. On the way you keep getting a wide view over the lake as far as Germany and Austria.

On steep stretches, normal wheels would spin on the smooth rails. That is why there is a **rack rail** between the rails. A cogwheel under the train engages this rack and pulls the train safely uphill. Going downhill it brakes just as reliably. On flat stretches the railway runs like a normal railway.

In the 19th century, Heiden became a popular **health resort**. Guests from many countries came to recover in the fresh air. The railway was meant to bring them comfortably up from Lake Constance. Ships and trains brought the travellers as far as Rorschach, and the mountain railway did the rest.

Heiden is a pretty village with many houses in the **Biedermeier style**. It is also well known because **Henry Dunant**, the founder of the Red Cross, spent his last years of life here. A museum commemorates him. To this day the railway brings visitors on outings and commuters to the village.

gewusst: The Rorschach-Heiden Railway is one of the few rack railways in the world that runs on standard-gauge track, that is, with the same gauge as the SBB.
Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901, and at that time he was living in Heiden.

teile.einleitung: The Säntis cable car (Säntis-Schwebebahn) is an aerial cable car in eastern Switzerland. It takes visitors from the Schwägalp in Appenzell Ausserrhoden to the summit of the Säntis.
wichtigste: The cable car starts on the Schwägalp.
It leads to the summit of the Säntis at 2,502 metres.
The first Säntis cable car opened in 1935.
The journey takes only a few minutes.
On the way the cable car climbs more than 1,000 metres.

abschnitte.titel: What is an aerial cable car?
abschnitte.text: An **aerial cable car** hangs from thick **steel cables** high above the ground. Large cabins travel back and forth between the valley station and the mountain station. The Säntis cable car has two cabins: while one goes up, the other goes down. In this way you get quickly and comfortably up a mountain, even if it is very steep.

abschnitte.titel: From the Schwägalp to the summit
abschnitte.text: The **valley station** lies on the **Schwägalp** at the foot of the Säntis. There is a large car park, a PostBus stop and a hotel. The cabin glides past steep rock walls up to the **mountain station** right by the summit. At the top there are a restaurant, viewing terraces and a wide view over eastern Switzerland.

The first cable car up the Säntis opened in **1935**. Before that you had to climb to the summit on foot. Over time the cable car was renewed several times and got larger, more modern cabins. Today very many visitors ride it up the Säntis every year.

gewusst: In winter the Schwägalp is also a popular place for cross-country skiing.
The cable car also runs in winter when the weather allows.

teile.einleitung: Jeremias Gotthelf is the pen name of Albert Bitzius. He was a pastor in the Emmental in the canton of Bern and wrote famous novels about the life of farmers.
wichtigste: Jeremias Gotthelf's real name was Albert Bitzius.
He lived from 1797 to 1854.
He was a pastor in Lützelflüh in the Emmental.
His books tell of the life of farmers and farmhands in the Emmental.
Well-known works are “Uli the Farmhand” and “The Black Spider”.
He is regarded as one of the most important Swiss writers.

abschnitte.text: Albert Bitzius was born in **Murten** in 1797. Like his father, he became a **pastor**. From 1832 he worked in **Lützelflüh** in the Emmental. There he got to know the life of farming families well. He also campaigned strongly for schools and for poor children.

abschnitte.titel: A name from his first book
abschnitte.text: In 1837 his first novel, **“Der Bauernspiegel”** (“The Farmer's Mirror”), appeared. The narrator in it is called **Jeremias Gotthelf**. Bitzius then used this name for all his books. Soon people knew him mainly by this name. He wrote a great deal, often alongside his work as a pastor.

In **“Uli der Knecht”** (“Uli the Farmhand”), a young farmhand becomes a capable man through hard work and honesty. The eerie tale **“Die schwarze Spinne”** (“The Black Spider”) is about an old legend and about courage and trust in God. Gotthelf described farms, festivals, work and the worries of people very precisely. Sometimes he had his characters speak **Bernese German**.

Gotthelf died in Lützelflüh in 1854. His books are still read today and have been filmed several times. In Lützelflüh there is a **Gotthelf Centre** with an exhibition about his life. Many people still link the Emmental with his stories today.

gewusst: “The Black Spider” is regarded as one of the best-known tales in German-language literature.
Many Swiss know Gotthelf's stories mainly from the films.

teile.einleitung: Nidwalden is a small canton in central Switzerland on Lake Lucerne. Together with Obwalden, it used to form the land of Unterwalden, one of the founding states of the Swiss Confederation.
wichtigste: The main town of Nidwalden is Stans.
German is spoken, in everyday life the Nidwalden dialect.
The coat of arms shows a white double key on a red background.
The key is the symbol of Saint Peter.
Nidwalden belongs to Unterwalden, one of the three original cantons.
Well-known mountains are the Stanserhorn and the Bürgenstock.

abschnitte.text: Nidwalden lies on the southern shore of **Lake Lucerne** in central Switzerland. The name means “nid dem Wald”, that is, below the forest. The main town is **Stans**. Other places include Hergiswil, Buochs and Beckenried. Neighbouring cantons include Obwalden, Lucerne, Uri and Bern.

The coat of arms of Nidwalden shows a white **double key** on a red background. The key is the symbol of **Saint Peter**. According to old belief, Peter keeps the keys to heaven. Obwalden also has a key in its coat of arms, but in different colours. This shows that the two cantons belong closely together.

Nidwalden and Obwalden together formed the land of **Unterwalden**. Together with Uri and Schwyz, Unterwalden is one of the three **original cantons** that are known from the Federal Charter of 1291. Later, Nidwalden and Obwalden separated into two half-cantons of their own. Today they are simply called cantons. In Stans there is a monument to **Arnold Winkelried**, a hero from an old legend.

A cable car with an open upper deck, where you stand in the open air, runs up the **Stanserhorn**. The **Bürgenstock** is a mountain right on the lake with hotels and a rock path. **Mount Pilatus** also borders Nidwalden. A well-known aircraft manufacturer also has its base in Stans.

gewusst: The cable car up the Stanserhorn was the first cable car in the world with an open upper deck.
Nidwalden is one of the smaller cantons of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Saane is a river in western Switzerland. In French it is called the Sarine. It flows through the city of Fribourg and winds there in a deep gorge around the old town.
wichtigste: The Saane is called the Sarine in French.
It rises in the Alps and flows through the cantons of Valais, Bern, Vaud and Fribourg.
The city of Fribourg lies on a rock above a loop of the Saane.
In Fribourg many bridges lead over the Saane.
The Saane flows into the Aare.
In parts it is a language border between German and French.

abschnitte.text: The Saane rises in the Alps near the **Sanetsch Pass**. It flows through the Saanenland near Gstaad and then through the Gruyère region.
