Further down it crosses the city of **Fribourg**. Finally it flows into the **Aare**. On the way it is dammed into several lakes, such as Lake Gruyère and Lake Schiffenen.

The old town of **Fribourg** lies high on a rock. Below, the Saane makes a large loop. This position was favourable in the Middle Ages, because the river protected the city like a moat. Steep sandstone cliffs rise there above the water.

Because the Saane flows so far down, Fribourg needs many **bridges**. There are old wooden bridges in the lower town and high bridges of stone and concrete. In the 19th century, one of the longest suspension bridges in the world spanned the valley here. Since 2014 the modern **Poya Bridge** has crossed the river.

In the area of Fribourg, the Saane roughly separates the German-speaking from the French-speaking area. That is why people jokingly speak of the **Röstigraben** (rösti ditch) when it comes to differences between German-speaking Switzerland and Romandie. In Fribourg itself both languages are spoken, and the city is **bilingual**.

gewusst: The city of Fribourg is called Freiburg in German, and the canton is officially bilingual.
The village of Saanen near Gstaad takes its name from the Saane.

teile.einleitung: Sarnen is the main town of the canton of Obwalden. The place lies at the northern end of Lake Sarnen in central Switzerland. The government and parliament of the canton are based here.
wichtigste: Sarnen is the main town of the canton of Obwalden.
Sarnen lies at the northern end of Lake Sarnen.
The Sarner Aa flows through Sarnen.
The famous “White Book of Sarnen” is kept in the State Archives.
Until 1998 the canton's Landsgemeinde (open-air assembly) met in Sarnen.

abschnitte.text: In Sarnen, the **Government Council** and the parliament of Obwalden, the **Cantonal Council**, hold their meetings. The old **town hall** stands in the middle of the village. Obwalden is a small canton, and Sarnen is its largest municipality. Some smaller villages in the surrounding area also belong to Sarnen.

In the State Archives of Obwalden, the **White Book of Sarnen** is kept. It was written around 1470 and has a white cover. In it is one of the oldest accounts of **William Tell** and the Rütli Oath. It is very important for the history of Swiss legends.

In the past, the Obwalden citizens entitled to vote met every year on the **Landenberg** in Sarnen for the **Landsgemeinde**. There they voted in the open air by raising their hands. In 1998 the people decided to abolish the Landsgemeinde. Since then people vote at the ballot box.

gewusst: On the Landenberg in Sarnen there once stood a castle; in its place there is now a shooting range building.
Sarnen has its own railway station on the line from Lucerne over the Brünig to Interlaken.

teile.einleitung: Nestlé is one of the largest food companies in the world. The company's headquarters are in Vevey on Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud. Nestlé makes many well-known products, from coffee to chocolate.
wichtigste: Nestlé has its headquarters in Vevey in the canton of Vaud.
The company goes back to Henri Nestlé, who made food for infants in Vevey.
In 1905, Nestlé merged with a condensed milk company from Cham.
Nestlé sells its products in almost all countries of the world.
Its brands include, for example, Nescafé, Nespresso, Maggi and KitKat.
Nestlé is one of the largest companies in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In the 19th century, the pharmacist **Henri Nestlé** lived in Vevey. He developed an **infant cereal** made of milk, wheat and sugar for babies who could not tolerate other food. The product soon sold in many countries. The bird's nest in the logo recalls his name, because “Nestle” means “little nest” in Swabian dialect.

In **Cham** in the canton of Zug, there was at the same time a company that made **condensed milk**. The two companies were competitors for a long time. In **1905** they merged. Over time the new company became a worldwide **group**, that is, a very large company with many parts.

Nestlé makes thousands of products. Very well known is the instant coffee **Nescafé**, which came onto the market in 1938. There are also the coffee capsules from **Nespresso**, the soups and stock cubes from **Maggi** and chocolate such as **KitKat**. Pet food and mineral water are also part of it. The products are sold in very many countries.

Nestlé employs hundreds of thousands of people all over the world. The group is important for the Swiss economy. Like many large companies, however, Nestlé is also **criticised**, for example on questions concerning water, the environment or the advertising of baby food in poorer countries. Nestlé itself stresses its efforts for quality and sustainability.

gewusst: In Lake Geneva off Vevey stands a huge metal fork, which belongs to the Alimentarium food museum.
The Alimentarium in Vevey is a museum on the subject of food.

teile.einleitung: The San Bernardino Pass is an Alpine pass in the canton of the Grisons. It links the Rheinwald in the north with the Italian-speaking Misox in the south. From there you go on into Ticino.
wichtigste: The San Bernardino Pass lies in the canton of the Grisons.
It is a good 2,000 metres high.
It links the Rheinwald with the Misox.
The San Bernardino Tunnel runs under the pass.
The tunnel opened in 1967.
The A13 motorway runs through the tunnel into Ticino.

abschnitte.text: The pass lies at just over **2,000 metres** above sea level. On the north side lies the village of **Hinterrhein** in the Rheinwald, and on the south side the village of **San Bernardino** in the Misox. At the top of the pass there is a small lake. In winter the pass road is closed because of snow.

In the Rheinwald people speak German. The **Misox**, in Italian Mesolcina, also belongs to the canton of the Grisons, but there people speak **Italian**. So the pass links two language areas in the same canton. At the end of the Misox you reach Ticino near Bellinzona.

Since 1967 there has been the **San Bernardino Tunnel**. It is about 6.6 kilometres long and runs under the pass. The **A13 motorway** goes through it. In this way you can drive from Chur to Ticino all year round. The tunnel is an important alternative to the Gotthard.

Many centuries ago, merchants with pack animals already crossed this pass. The name comes from Saint **Bernardino of Siena**, to whom a chapel on the south side is dedicated. In the 19th century a carriage road was built. Today the old pass road is popular with cyclists and motorcyclists.

gewusst: The Hinterrhein, one of the two source rivers of the Rhine, rises near the pass.
The village of San Bernardino was once known as a spa with a mineral spring.

teile.einleitung: The Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein in eastern Switzerland. It is 2,502 metres high and easy to recognise from far away. On its summit three cantons meet.
wichtigste: The Säntis is 2,502 metres high.
It is the highest peak in the Alpstein.
At the summit, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and St Gallen meet.
Since 1935 a cable car has run up from the Schwägalp.
On the summit there is a weather station and a tall transmission tower.
In clear weather you can see into several countries.

abschnitte.text: The **Alpstein** is a mountain range in the cantons of Appenzell and St Gallen. It consists mainly of **limestone** and has steep rock walls. The Säntis is its highest peak. Because it stands somewhat alone in front of the Alps, it is easy to see from Lake Constance and from the Zürich Oberland.

On the summit of the Säntis, three cantons meet: **Appenzell Innerrhoden**, **Appenzell Ausserrhoden** and **St Gallen**. The Schwägalp at the foot of the mountain belongs to Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Around the Säntis lie many alpine pastures where cows graze in summer. The area is known for Appenzeller cheese and local customs.

On the Säntis a **weather station** has measured temperature, wind and precipitation since the 19th century. At the top it is often very windy and cold. A lot of snow also falls. On the summit there is also a tall **transmission tower** for radio, television and telephone.

Most visitors travel to the summit with the **Säntis cable car** from the Schwägalp. Experienced walkers climb up on mountain paths, for example from Wasserauen or Wildhaus. At the top there is a restaurant and a viewing terrace. From there, in clear weather you can see as far as Germany, Austria and Liechtenstein.

gewusst: The Säntis is among the places with the most precipitation in Switzerland.
In the Alpstein lie well-known mountain lakes such as the Seealpsee and the Fählensee.

teile.einleitung: Murten is a small town in the canton of Fribourg on the shore of Lake Murten. It is known for its well-preserved old town with its medieval town wall. In addition, a famous battle took place here in 1476.
wichtigste: Murten lies in the canton of Fribourg on Lake Murten.
In French the town is called Morat.
The town wall from the Middle Ages is very well preserved.
Today you can walk on the wall walk along the top of the wall.
In 1476 the Confederates defeated the army of Charles the Bold at Murten.
In Murten the majority speak German, but many people also speak French.

abschnitte.titel: A town from the Middle Ages
abschnitte.text: Murten was founded in the Middle Ages by the **Zähringen**, a powerful noble family. Around the old town, a strong **town wall** with towers was built. This wall has survived almost completely to this day. On the covered **wall walk** you can walk along the top and look over the roofs to the lake.

In **1476**, an important battle took place at Murten in the **Burgundian Wars**. Duke **Charles the Bold** of Burgundy laid siege to the town. An army of the Confederates and their allies came to help and defeated the Burgundians. This victory made the Confederates known throughout Europe.

A legend tells that after the Battle of Murten, a messenger ran all the way to **Fribourg** to bring the news of victory. In memory of this, the **Murten Run** (Murtenlauf) is held every year. Thousands of runners run the roughly 17 kilometres from Murten up to Fribourg.

Murten lies on the **language border** between German and French. Most residents speak German, but many also speak French. That is why the town has two names: **Murten** and **Morat**. With its arcades, alleys and view of the lake, it is a popular destination for outings.

gewusst: A speciality from Murten is the Nidelkuchen, a sweet tart with cream.
At the national exhibition Expo.02, a huge rust-coloured cube, the Monolith, stood in Lake Murten.

teile.einleitung: Leukerbad is a village in the canton of Valais that is known for its hot springs. It lies at over 1,400 metres and is one of the largest thermal spa resorts in the Alps.
wichtigste: Leukerbad lies in Upper Valais, in the district of Leuk.
The village lies at over 1,400 metres above sea level.
Many hot springs bubble up out of the ground.
At some springs the water is over 50 degrees warm.
In several thermal baths you can bathe outdoors in warm water.
Behind the village, the steep rock wall rises to the Gemmi Pass.
German is spoken in Leukerbad.

abschnitte.text: Rain and meltwater seep into the mountains around Leukerbad. Deep in the rock, the water is heated and absorbs **minerals**. Then it rises again and emerges as a **thermal spring**. Every day, millions of litres of warm water flow into the village in this way. Part of it is led into the baths, and the rest flows into the stream.

In Leukerbad there are large **thermal baths** with pools indoors and outdoors. It is especially lovely in winter, when snow lies all around and you sit in warm water. Centuries ago, guests already came here because they believed the water helped against pain. Today **tourism** is the village's most important source of income.

Above the village rises an almost vertical rock wall. Above it lies the **Gemmi Pass**, which links Valais with Kandersteg in the canton of Bern. In the past, pack-animal drivers and travellers climbed up on a steep path. Today a **cable car** goes up to the Gemmi. At the top lies Lake Daubensee, and there are lovely walks.

In winter you can **ski** and cross-country ski in Leukerbad. In summer, walking paths, via ferrata routes and excursions into the mountains are the attraction. The village lies at the end of a valley that leads up north from Leuk. It is only a few kilometres down to the Rhône valley.

gewusst: Leukerbad is the largest thermal spa resort in the Swiss Alps.
The rock wall near Leukerbad is so steep that the old Gemmi path leads straight up it in many tight bends.

teile.einleitung: The Ruinaulta is a wild gorge of the Rhine in the canton of the Grisons. It is sometimes called the “Grand Canyon of Switzerland”. It was formed after a huge rockslide near Flims.
wichtigste: The Ruinaulta is a gorge of the Vorderrhein between Ilanz and Reichenau.
It was formed after the Flims rockslide about 10,000 years ago.
The Flims rockslide is regarded as the largest known rockslide in the Alps.
The Rhine then cut its way through the masses of rock.
Trains of the Rhaetian Railway run through the gorge.
The pale, steep rock walls are in places several hundred metres high.

abschnitte.text: About 10,000 years ago, shortly after the last Ice Age, a huge piece of a mountain broke away near **Flims**. An unimaginable amount of rock thundered into the valley and filled it. This was the **Flims rockslide**, the largest known rockslide in the Alps. As a result the Rhine was dammed for a time.

The water of the **Vorderrhein** looked for a new way. Over thousands of years it cut deep into the loose rubble of the rockslide. This is how the gorge with its steep, pale walls was formed. This work of the river is called **erosion**. It continues to this day.

abschnitte.titel: By train, by boat and on foot
abschnitte.text: The **Rhaetian Railway** runs through the Ruinaulta, and so does the Glacier Express. The tracks lie right beside the river, and there is no road in the gorge. Footpaths lead down and to viewpoints on the edge. In summer many people travel through the gorge in inflatable boats, which is called **river rafting**.

In the Ruinaulta grow pines and other plants that cope with dry soil. The river has formed gravel banks and floodplains in which many animals live. The landscape is under **protection** because it is so unique. The lakes near Flims, such as Lake Cauma, also lie in the area of the old rockslide.

gewusst: The name Ruinaulta comes from Romansh and means roughly “high collapse” or “high rock wall”.
The turquoise water of Lake Cauma near Flims lies in the middle of the debris of the Flims rockslide.

teile.einleitung: The **Rhine** is one of the greatest rivers in Europe. It rises in the **Grisons**, flows through Lake Constance and past Schaffhausen as far as **Basel**. From there, large ships travel to the **North Sea**.
wichtigste: The Rhine is formed in the Grisons from the Anterior Rhine and the Posterior Rhine.
The two headwaters meet at Reichenau.
The Rhine flows through Lake Constance and often forms the border with Germany.
At Schaffhausen lie the Rhine Falls, the largest waterfall in Europe by volume of water.
In Basel the Rhine divides the city into Grossbasel and Kleinbasel.
From Basel, ships travel as far as Rotterdam on the North Sea.

abschnitte.text: The Rhine has two headwaters in the **Grisons**. The **Anterior Rhine** begins at **Lake Toma** near the Oberalp Pass. The **Posterior Rhine** rises in the area of the Rheinwaldhorn. At **Reichenau** the two join and form the Rhine. After that it flows past Chur to the north, along the border with Liechtenstein and Austria.

abschnitte.titel: Lake Constance and the Rhine Falls
abschnitte.text: The Rhine flows into **Lake Constance** and leaves it at **Stein am Rhein**. From here it forms the **border with Germany** over long stretches. At Neuhausen am Rheinfall it plunges over the **Rhine Falls**. The town of **Schaffhausen** came into being because ships had to unload their goods before the Rhine Falls. The goods were then carried overland around the waterfall.

Shortly before Basel, the Rhine flows past **Augst**, **Pratteln** and **Birsfelden** in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. In **Basel** it divides the city into **Grossbasel** and **Kleinbasel**. Small **ferries** without an engine take people across the river, driven only by the current. In summer many people let themselves drift down the Rhine. They pack their clothes into a waterproof bag, the “**Wickelfisch**”.

From Basel, the Rhine is navigable for large ships. In the **Rhine ports** of Basel, Birsfelden and Muttenz, goods such as oil, grain and containers are handled. The ships travel through France, Germany and the Netherlands as far as **Rotterdam**. In this way Switzerland, although it has no sea, has a waterway to the **North Sea**. In total the Rhine is over 1,200 kilometres long.

gewusst: By volume of water, the Rhine Falls are the largest waterfall in Europe.
The Basel ferries across the Rhine run entirely without an engine, using only the power of the current.

teile.einleitung: Saint-Ursanne is a small medieval town in the canton of Jura. It lies in a loop of the River Doubs. With its town gates, the old stone bridge and the large church, it is regarded as one of the most beautiful small towns in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Saint-Ursanne lies in the canton of Jura on the River Doubs.
Today the place belongs to the municipality of Clos du Doubs.
It is named after Saint Ursicinus, in French Ursanne.
An old stone bridge leads over the Doubs.
The large collegiate church dates from the Middle Ages.
The town still has old town gates.

abschnitte.text: The name comes from Saint **Ursicinus**, in French Ursanne. He was a monk who is said to have lived as a **hermit** on the Doubs in the 7th century. Later a monastery grew up at this spot and from it the town. Ursanne is venerated there to this day.

The **Doubs** flows right past Saint-Ursanne. A beautiful **stone bridge** with several arches links the town with the other bank. On the bridge stands a statue of Saint John of Nepomuk, who is regarded as the patron saint of bridges. At the end of the bridge stands an old town gate.

In the middle of the place stands the large **collegiate church**, in French the Collégiale. It was built in the Middle Ages and has a richly decorated portal. Around the church lie narrow lanes with old houses. Three **town gates** lead into the old town.

The countryside around Saint-Ursanne is green and hilly. Many people walk along the Doubs or travel by **canoe** on the river. Above the town lie the remains of a castle. A railway line also passes the place on a high viaduct.

gewusst: The Doubs flows in a large loop through Switzerland and then returns to France.
Saint-Ursanne has only a few hundred inhabitants, but is very well known as a small town.

teile.einleitung: Schabziger clover is a spicy herb. Dried and ground, it gives Glarus Schabziger its green colour and strong aroma. The plant is related to clover.
wichtigste: Schabziger clover is an annual plant.
It belongs to the legume family, like clover and peas.
It has small blue flowers.
When dried it smells very strong and spicy.
It makes Schabziger green and gives it its flavour.
It is also called blue fenugreek.

abschnitte.text: **Schabziger clover** grows to about knee height. Its leaves consist of three small leaflets, like those of clover. In summer it bears small **blue flowers**. The plant lives for only one year, so it has to be sown again every year. Afterwards it forms small pods containing seeds.

For Schabziger the plants are harvested, **dried** and finely ground. The green powder is mixed with the Ziger. This gives the cheese its **green colour**. The spicy smell, which is a little like hay, also comes from the clover.

The herb is not only used in Glarus. In the **Tyrol** and **South Tyrol** it is called **bread clover**. There it is mixed into bread dough so that the bread tastes more savoury. Some people also put it in herb butter or soups.

gewusst: Schabziger clover is closely related to fenugreek, whose seeds are used in curries.
Dried Schabziger clover keeps its aroma for a very long time.

teile.einleitung: A **Poya** is a colourful picture from the **Gruyère region** in the canton of Fribourg. It shows the **alpine ascent**: herders drive their cows up to the alp in early summer. Such pictures often hang over the stable doors of farmhouses.
wichtigste: A Poya shows the alpine ascent with cows and herders.
The pictures come from the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.
They are often hung over the door of a stable or barn.
The cows usually walk in a long line one behind the other.
Poya painting has been known since the 19th century.

abschnitte.titel: What you see on a Poya
abschnitte.text: A Poya is usually a long, narrow picture. On it, a **line of cows** goes up the mountain one behind the other. At the front and at the back walk the **herders** in their traditional costume, often with goats, a dog and a cart with equipment for making cheese. In the background you see mountains and sometimes the family's farmhouse. The colours are strong and the figures are simply painted.

Farmers had the Poya painted on a wooden board and hung it **over the door of the stable or barn**. In this way they proudly showed off their herd. The word “poya” comes from Patois, the old dialect of the area, and is connected with going up to the alp. The pictures have been known since the **19th century**. To this day, artists paint new Poyas.

The **Gruyère region** (in French Gruyère) lies in the south of the canton of Fribourg. The region is known for its alpine farming and for **Gruyère cheese**. The alpine ascent is an important event of the year there. In the **Musée gruérien** in Bulle you can look at old Poyas. At some festivals in the Gruyère region too, the Poya plays a role.

gewusst: On old Poyas, every single cow of the herd is often painted, so that you can see the family's wealth.

teile.einleitung: The Marché-Concours is a large horse festival in the canton of Jura. It takes place every year in August in Saignelégier in the Freiberge, and the Freiberger horses are at its centre.
wichtigste: The Marché-Concours takes place in Saignelégier in the canton of Jura.
It is held every year in August.
The festival has existed since the end of the 19th century.
At its centre is the Freiberger, the only Swiss horse breed.
There are horse shows, horse races and a parade.
Tens of thousands of people visit the festival.

abschnitte.text: The name **Marché-Concours** means roughly “market and competition”. It was originally a **horse market** where breeders showed and sold their animals. Today it is a large public festival. The best **Freiberger horses** are judged and awarded prizes. There is also music, food and stalls.

One highlight is the **horse races**. There are also funny races, for example with carts in which farmers steer their horses themselves. On Sunday a large **parade** moves through Saignelégier. Horses, carriages and decorated floats show themes from history and everyday life.

Saignelégier is the main town of the **Freiberge**, in French Franches-Montagnes. The landscape is a high plateau with pastures, fir trees and moors. Here the horses often live freely on the pastures among the trees. The **Freiberger** is strong, calm and versatile. In the past it helped on the farm, and today it is also popular as a riding horse.

gewusst: The Freiberger is the only horse breed that originally comes from Switzerland.
For a long time the Swiss Army used Freiberger horses as pack animals.

teile.einleitung: **Post tenebras lux** is the Latin motto of the canton and city of **Geneva**. It means “After darkness, light”. The saying is closely linked with the **Reformation** in Geneva.
wichtigste: “Post tenebras lux” is the motto of Geneva.
In English it means “After darkness, light”.
The saying is Latin.
It comes from a sentence in the Bible.
Geneva has linked it with itself since the Reformation in the 16th century.
It appears on the Geneva coat of arms and on the Reformation Wall.

abschnitte.text: “Post” means “after”, “tenebras” means “darkness” and “lux” means “light”. Together this gives: “**After darkness, light**”. The words go back to a sentence from the **Book of Job** in the Latin Bible. There it originally read “Post tenebras spero lucem”, that is, “After darkness I hope for light”. Geneva later shortened the saying.

In the 16th century, Geneva became a city of the **Reformation**. The reformers wanted to renew the church. Especially well known became **John Calvin**, who worked in Geneva for a long time. For the Reformed people of Geneva, the saying stood for the idea that after a dark time a new light would come. Other faith groups saw this period differently. The saying thus became a sign of the city.

The **Geneva coat of arms** shows on the left half a black **eagle** on a yellow ground and on the right a golden **key** on a red ground. Above it stands a radiant sun. Often the motto “Post tenebras lux” is also included. You can see the coat of arms on buildings, on flags and on documents of the canton. Geneva has belonged to the Confederation since **1815**.

In the **Parc des Bastions** in Geneva stands the large **Reformation Wall**. It is a long wall with figures of reformers. Above them, in large letters, stands “POST TENEBRAS LUX”. Many tourists photograph the wall. In this way you meet the motto in the middle of the city.

gewusst: Originally the saying was “Post tenebras spero lucem”, that is, with the words “I hope”.
The motto stands in huge letters on the Reformation Wall in Geneva.

teile.einleitung: Uri is a canton in central Switzerland whose main town is Altdorf. It is one of the three original cantons and is closely linked with the story of William Tell and the Gotthard.
wichtigste: The main town of Uri is Altdorf.
German is spoken, more precisely the Uri dialect.
Together with Schwyz and Unterwalden, Uri is one of the three original cantons.
The coat of arms shows a black bull's head on a yellow background.
The route over the Gotthard to the south runs through Uri.
Uri borders many cantons, but not Lucerne.

abschnitte.text: Uri is a canton with high mountains and deep valleys. The **Reuss** flows through the valley into **Lake Uri**, the southern part of Lake Lucerne. The main town **Altdorf** lies close to the lake. Uri borders Schwyz, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Bern, Valais, Ticino, the Grisons and Glarus. Uri does not border **Lucerne**.

Together with Schwyz and Unterwalden, Uri is one of the three **original cantons**. The **Rütli meadow**, where according to legend the Rütli Oath took place, lies on the territory of Uri. In Altdorf stands the famous **Tell Monument**. It shows William Tell with his crossbow and his son. According to the legend, Tell shot an apple from his son's head here.

The coat of arms of Uri shows a black **bull's head** with a red nose ring on a yellow background. The name Uri is often linked with the word “Ur” for the aurochs. In the canton people speak **German**, and in everyday life the **Uri dialect**. It is a form of Swiss German with words of its own.

One of the most important links between north and south runs through Uri. In the past, pack-animal drivers crossed the **Gotthard Pass** with their animals. In the Schöllenen Gorge, the **Devil's Bridge** crosses the Reuss. Today trains run through the **Gotthard Base Tunnel**, which opened in 2016. Its northern portal is at Erstfeld in Uri.

gewusst: At about 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
There is a legend about the Devil's Bridge, according to which the devil built the first bridge.

teile.einleitung: The **Rhône Glacier** lies in Upper Valais near the **Furka Pass**. From its meltwater the **Rhône**, one of the great rivers of Europe, is formed. The glacier is known for its ice grotto and for having melted heavily.
wichtigste: The Rhône Glacier lies in Upper Valais near the Furka Pass.
From its meltwater the Rhône is formed.
Every year an ice grotto is dug into the glacier.
The glacier has retreated sharply since about 1850.
A glacial lake has formed in front of the glacier.
Below it lies the small place of Gletsch.

abschnitte.text: The Rhône Glacier lies between the **Furka Pass** and the **Grimsel Pass** in Upper Valais. It is several kilometres long and reaches up to the Dammastock. The meltwater collects at the lower end and flows into the valley as the young **Rhône**. From here the water flows through Valais, Lake Geneva and France to the Mediterranean. The glacier is therefore the beginning of a long journey.

At the Hotel Belvédère on the Furka road, you can walk into the glacier. Every year a new **ice grotto** is dug into the ice there, because the glacier moves and melts. Inside, the ice glows blue. To slow the melting at this spot, the glacier is partly covered in summer with **white blankets**. They reflect the sunlight.

Around **1850**, the Rhône Glacier reached down to the valley floor at **Gletsch**. Since then it has **retreated** sharply, especially in recent decades. Where ice once lay there is now bare rock and a **glacial lake**. Experts measure the glacier regularly. The Rhône Glacier is a clear example of how the climate in the Alps is warming.

Below the glacier lies the small place of **Gletsch**. In summer the **Furka Cogwheel Steam Railway** passes by here, a historic railway with steam locomotives. It links Realp in the canton of Uri over the Furka with Oberwald in Valais. In the past the railway line led over the pass, and today normal trains run through the **Furka Base Tunnel**. Volunteers keep the old mountain line in operation.

gewusst: In summer part of the Rhône Glacier is covered with white blankets so that it melts more slowly.
Around 1850 the glacier still reached down to the valley floor at Gletsch.

teile.einleitung: The Martinsloch is a large hole in a rock wall of the Tschingelhörner in the canton of Glarus. Twice a year, the sun shines exactly through this hole onto the church of Elm.
wichtigste: The Martinsloch lies in the Tschingelhörner above Elm in the canton of Glarus.
It is a natural hole in the rock.
In spring and autumn, the sun shines through the hole onto the church tower of Elm.
This spectacle lasts only a short time each time.
A legend tells how the hole came about.
The rock wall belongs to the Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: The **Martinsloch** is so large that you can see it well from the valley. On a few days in March and at the end of September, the sun stands in the morning in just such a way that its rays fall through the hole. Then, for a short time, a patch of sunlight glows on the **church tower of Elm**. Many people come to see this spectacle.

An old **legend** tells of a shepherd named Martin. A giant wanted to steal his sheep. Martin threw his stick at the giant. The stick flew so hard that it knocked a hole in the mountain. Since then, says the legend, it has been called the Martinsloch.

On the **Tschingelhörner** you can see a sharp line in the rock, the **Glarus Main Thrust**. There, older rock lies above younger rock, because when the Alps were formed, huge plates of rock were pushed over each other. That is why the area has belonged since 2008 to the **Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: You can also see the sun through the Martinsloch in Elm itself, if you stand in the right place.

teile.einleitung: The OLMA is a large trade fair held every year in autumn in the city of St Gallen. Agriculture and food are at its centre. Hundreds of thousands of people visit the fair to see animals, products and specialities.
wichtigste: The OLMA takes place every year in October in St Gallen.
It lasts eleven days.
OLMA stands for Ostschweizerische Land- und Milchwirtschaftliche Ausstellung (Eastern Swiss Agricultural and Dairy Exhibition).
The first OLMA took place in 1943.
Especially popular are the animals and the piglet race.
Every year a different canton is invited as guest.

abschnitte.text: The name **OLMA** is an abbreviation for **Ostschweizerische Land- und Milchwirtschaftliche Ausstellung**. The fair has existed since **1943**. It takes place every year in **October** in St Gallen and lasts eleven days. It is one of the largest public fairs in Switzerland.

At the OLMA you can see many farm **animals**, for example cows, sheep, goats and horses. A special experience is the **Säulirennen** (piglet race). Small pigs, the Säuli, race each other. Many children and adults cheer them on loudly. There are also animal demonstrations in the arena.

The famous **St Gallen bratwurst**, which is traditionally eaten without mustard, is part of the OLMA. In the halls you can try many **specialities** from all over Switzerland, such as cheese, bread or sweets. Companies also show machines, appliances and products for the household and for farming.

Every year a different **canton** or region is invited as **guest**. The guest canton presents its customs, specialities and sights. For the opening there is a large **parade** through the city of St Gallen. In this way visitors get to know a different part of Switzerland each time.

gewusst: In St Gallen people say that a real bratwurst needs no mustard.
The OLMA has its own exhibition grounds in the middle of the city of St Gallen.

teile.einleitung: “La Rauracienne” is the anthem of the canton of Jura. The song is in French, and its name recalls the Raurici, a Celtic tribe from the area.
wichtigste: “La Rauracienne” is the anthem of the canton of Jura.
The song is sung in French.
The name recalls the Raurici, a Celtic tribe.
The song was written in the 19th century.
The canton of Jura has existed since 1979.

abschnitte.text: Many cantons have a song of their own, a **cantonal anthem**. The anthem of the canton of **Jura** is called **“La Rauracienne”**. It is sung at celebrations and official occasions. The song was written as early as the **19th century**, long before the canton of Jura existed. It was a song of the people who wished for more independence.

The name comes from the **Raurici**. They were a **Celtic tribe** that lived over 2,000 years ago on the Upper Rhine and in the Jura. The Roman town of **Augusta Raurica** near Basel is also named after them. With the name of their anthem, the people of Jura recall this ancient history of their region.

For a long time the Jura belonged to the canton of **Bern**. Many people in the French-speaking northern Jura wanted a canton of their own. After several votes, the **canton of Jura** was founded and has been a canton in its own right since **1979**. This makes it the youngest canton in Switzerland, and “La Rauracienne” became its anthem.

gewusst: The canton of Jura is the youngest of the 26 Swiss cantons.

teile.einleitung: The Landsgemeinde is an old form of democracy in Switzerland. The citizens entitled to vote in a canton gather in the open air and vote by raising their hands.
wichtigste: At the Landsgemeinde, the citizens entitled to vote vote in the open air.
Voting is done by a show of hands.
Nidwalden abolished the Landsgemeinde in 1996.
Obwalden abolished it in 1998.
Today there are Landsgemeinden only in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.

abschnitte.text: At a **Landsgemeinde**, the citizens entitled to vote in a canton meet on a certain day in a large square. They elect the government and decide on laws. Voting is done by **raising a hand**. The Landammann (head of the cantonal government) then estimates which side has more hands.

Landsgemeinden have existed in central and eastern Switzerland since the **Middle Ages**. In the past there were some in several cantons, for example in Uri, Schwyz, Zug, Obwalden, Nidwalden and the two Appenzells. It is regarded as one of the oldest forms of **direct democracy**, in which the people decide for themselves.

Over time, many cantons abolished the Landsgemeinde. **Nidwalden** did so in **1996**, **Appenzell Ausserrhoden** in 1997 and **Obwalden in 1998**. Reasons included that not everyone can come on the day of the assembly and that the vote is not secret. Since then, people there have voted at the **ballot box** or by post.

Today the Landsgemeinde exists in only two cantons: in **Appenzell Innerrhoden** and in **Glarus**. In Appenzell it takes place on the last Sunday in April, in Glarus on the first Sunday in May. Many guests from Switzerland and abroad come to watch this special assembly.

gewusst: Because hands are raised, at the Landsgemeinde everyone can see how the others vote.
When results are very close, the Landammann decides by eye where there are more hands.

teile.einleitung: Beromünster is a place in the canton of Lucerne. The name became known throughout Switzerland through the national transmitter, a large radio station that broadcast radio programmes from here.
wichtigste: Near Beromünster stood the national transmitter for German-speaking Switzerland.
The transmitter went into operation in the 1930s.
It broadcast on medium wave and could be heard very far away.
Many people simply called the radio programme “Beromünster”.
At the end of 2008 the transmitter was switched off.

abschnitte.titel: A transmitter for the whole country
abschnitte.text: At the beginning of the **1930s**, a large **national transmitter** was built near Beromünster. It broadcast the radio programmes for **German-speaking Switzerland**. For French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino, there were national transmitters of their own. Because the transmitter was so well known, many people simply said “Radio Beromünster”.

The transmitter sent out its signals from a very tall **transmitter tower** that is well over 200 metres high. It broadcast on **medium wave**. Such radio waves travel very far, especially at night. That is why Beromünster could also be received in many countries outside Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: Important in the Second World War
abschnitte.text: During the **Second World War**, many people in other countries of Europe also secretly listened to Radio Beromünster. Switzerland was neutral, and the transmitter was regarded as a **reliable source of news**. Well known, for example, was the weekly programme by the historian Jean Rudolf von Salis about the state of the world.

Over time, people listened to the radio on **FM**, and later on DAB+ and the internet. Medium wave was hardly needed any more. At the **end of 2008**, the Beromünster national transmitter was switched off. The transmitter tower still stands and recalls the history of Swiss radio.

gewusst: For decades the name Beromünster was printed on many radio dials in Europe.
Beromünster is also known for its old collegiate foundation of canons.

teile.einleitung: **Raclette** is a famous cheese speciality from **Valais**. Half a wheel of cheese is melted and the soft cheese is scraped off. With it you eat potatoes, gherkins and pearl onions.
wichtigste: Raclette is a cheese speciality from Valais.
Half a wheel of cheese is heated and the melted cheese is scraped off.
The name comes from the French word “racler”, which means to scrape.
With it come potatoes in their skins, pickled gherkins and pearl onions.
Valais Raclette cheese is a protected speciality (AOP).
Many families eat raclette at home with small pans.

abschnitte.text: For real raclette you take a **half wheel of cheese**. The cut surface is held close to a fire or to a raclette oven. When the cheese is soft and bubbling, it is **scraped off** onto the plate with a knife. The French word for this is “**racler**”, which is where the name comes from. After that the wheel goes back to the heat, and the next portion melts.

With raclette you eat **potatoes in their skins**, in Switzerland often called “Gschwellti”. With them come **pickled gherkins**, **pearl onions** and freshly ground pepper. Many people also like a little paprika on the cheese. You eat portion after portion for as long as you are hungry. Raclette is a sociable meal at which you sit together for a long time.

Raclette is an old tradition from **Valais**. In the past, shepherds and herders are said to have melted the cheese at an open fire. For a long time the dish was simply called roasted cheese. The cheese **Raclette du Valais** has a protected designation of origin (**AOP**). It is made from the **raw milk** of Valais cows. Raclette cheese is, however, also made in other parts of Switzerland.

In many Swiss homes there is a **raclette oven with small pans**. Everyone puts a slice of cheese in their pan and slides it under the heater. In this way each person can decide for themselves how crispy the cheese gets. It is especially popular on holidays and in winter. For the half wheel, on the other hand, you need a larger raclette oven.

gewusst: The word raclette refers both to the dish and to the cheese.
For a raclette with the half wheel, you need a whole cheese, which is first cut through the middle.

teile.einleitung: Gruyères Castle stands on a hill above the little town of Gruyères in the canton of Fribourg. The famous Gruyère cheese is also named after the town. Today the castle is a museum.
wichtigste: Gruyères is called Greyerz in German.
The little town lies on a hill in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg.
Gruyères Castle towers above the town.
In the Middle Ages the Counts of Gruyères lived here.
Today the castle belongs to the canton of Fribourg and is a museum.
The cheese Le Gruyère is named after the region.

abschnitte.text: **Gruyères Castle** was built in the Middle Ages. For a long time the **Counts of Gruyères**, who ruled the area, lived here. Later it passed to Fribourg. Since the 20th century it has belonged to the **canton of Fribourg**. In the castle you can see splendid halls, old furniture and works of art.

The little town of **Gruyères** consists mainly of a broad main street with old houses and a fountain. Cars are not allowed in. From above you can see across the green **Gruyère region** to the Fribourg Alps. Every year a great many tourists from all over the world come here.

**Gruyère** is a hard cheese named after this area. It is made from cow's milk and matures for many months. At the foot of the hill there is a **show dairy** where you can watch cheese being made. Meringues with thick **Gruyère double cream** are also well known.

Besides the castle, Gruyères has other museums. One shows works by the artist **HR Giger**, who designed fantastic, slightly eerie figures. A **crane** can be seen on the coat of arms of the counts and of the region. That fits the name, because “grue” is the French word for crane.

gewusst: The cheese Le Gruyère has a protected designation of origin (AOP), so it may only be made in a certain area.
Lake Gruyère nearby is a reservoir on the Sarine.

teile.einleitung: The Montreux Jazz Festival is one of the most famous music festivals in the world. It takes place every summer in Montreux on Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud. Since 1967, stars from all kinds of music have performed here.
wichtigste: The Montreux Jazz Festival was founded in 1967.
Its founder was Claude Nobs of Montreux.
The festival lasts about two weeks in July.
Besides jazz there is also blues, rock, pop, soul and many other styles of music.
Many world stars have performed in Montreux.
The recordings of the concerts are regarded as a valuable music archive.

abschnitte.text: The first festival took place in **1967** and lasted only a few days. It was founded by **Claude Nobs**, who at the time worked at the Montreux tourist office. He wanted to bring more guests to the town on Lake Geneva. Over time, the small jazz festival became an event of world renown.

At the beginning, mainly jazz musicians played. But soon **blues**, **rock**, **pop** and **soul** were added too. Today, musicians from many countries and styles appear on the stages. Besides the big concerts in halls, there are also many free concerts on the lakeside.

In **1971**, the casino of Montreux burned down during a concert. The British rock band **Deep Purple** saw the smoke over the lake. This gave rise to their world-famous song “Smoke on the Water”. In it the band sings about Montreux, the fire and Lake Geneva.

Claude Nobs had many concerts filmed and recorded from an early stage. This created a huge **archive** with thousands of hours of music. It was added by UNESCO to the “Memory of the World” register. This makes it an important cultural heritage for all people.

gewusst: On the lakeside in Montreux stands a statue of Freddie Mercury, the singer of the band Queen, who was often in Montreux.
The festival takes place every year on the shore of Lake Geneva, with a view of the mountains.

teile.einleitung: The Openair Frauenfeld is a large music festival in Frauenfeld, the main town of the canton of Thurgau. It takes place every summer and is one of the largest hip-hop festivals in Europe. It is held on the Grosse Allmend.
wichtigste: The Openair Frauenfeld takes place every summer in Frauenfeld in the canton of Thurgau.
It is one of the largest hip-hop festivals in Europe.
The festival takes place on the Grosse Allmend.
It lasts several days.
Tens of thousands of visitors spend the night in tents on the site.

abschnitte.text: The **Openair Frauenfeld** has existed for many years. In the past, other kinds of music were also in the foreground there. Later **hip-hop** became the focus. Today the festival is one of the **largest hip-hop festivals in Europe**. On several stages, well-known rappers from Switzerland and all over the world perform.

The festival takes place on the **Grosse Allmend**, a wide plain on the river **Murg** in Frauenfeld. At other times the site is used by the military and for horse races, among other things. During the festival, a small **tent city** springs up there for a few days. Many visitors spend the night on the site.

A festival of this size needs a lot of organisation. There are medical services, security staff, waste collection and catering. Many **helpers** work on it. For the town of Frauenfeld, the Openair is an important event every year that attracts people from all over Switzerland.

gewusst: Frauenfeld is the main town of the canton of Thurgau and lies on the Murg.
